    84→def _is_excluded_dir(name: str, rel_path: str, extra: tuple[str, ...]) -> bool:
    85→    in_default_exclusions = name in DEFAULT_EXCLUSIONS or name.endswith(".egg-info")
    86→    is_virtualenv_dir = name.startswith(".venv") or name.startswith("venv")
    87→    matches_extra_exclusion = bool(
    88→        extra
    89→        and any(
    90→            matches_exclusion(rel_path, exclusion) or exclusion == name
    91→            for exclusion in extra
    92→        )
    93→    )
    94→    return in_default_exclusions or is_virtualenv_dir or matches_extra_exclusion
    95→
    96→
    97→def _find_source_files_cached(
    98→    path: str,
    99→    extensions: tuple[str, ...],
   100→    exclusions: tuple[str, ...] | None = None,
   101→    extra_exclusions: tuple[str, ...] = (),
   102→) -> tuple[str, ...]:
   103→    """Cached file discovery using os.walk with traversal-time pruning."""
   104→    cache_key = (path, extensions, exclusions, extra_exclusions)
   105→    cache = current_runtime_context().source_file_cache
   106→    cached = cache.get(cache_key)
   107→    if cached is not None:
   108→        return cached
   109→
   110→    project_root = get_project_root()
   111→    root = Path(path)
   112→    if not root.is_absolute():
   113→        root = project_root / root
   114→    all_exclusions = (exclusions or ()) + extra_exclusions
   115→    ext_set = set(extensions)
   116→    files: list[str] = []
   117→    for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(root):
   118→        rel_dir = _normalize_path_separators(_safe_relpath(dirpath, project_root))
   119→        dirnames[:] = sorted(
   120→            d
   121→            for d in dirnames
   122→            if not _is_excluded_dir(d, rel_dir + "/" + d, all_exclusions)
   123→        )
   124→        for fname in filenames:
   125→            if any(fname.endswith(ext) for ext in ext_set):
   126→                full = os.path.join(dirpath, fname)
   127→                rel_file = _normalize_path_separators(_safe_relpath(full, project_root))
   128→                if all_exclusions and any(
   129→                    matches_exclusion(rel_file, ex) for ex in all_exclusions
   130→                ):
   131→                    continue
   132→                files.append(rel_file)
   133→    result = tuple(sorted(files))
   134→    cache.put(cache_key, result)
   135→    return result
   136→
   137→
   138→def find_source_files(
   139→    path: str | Path, extensions: list[str], exclusions: list[str] | None = None
   140→) -> list[str]:

   142→    return list(
   143→        _find_source_files_cached(
   144→            str(path),
   145→            tuple(extensions),
   146→            tuple(exclusions) if exclusions else None,
   147→            get_exclusions(),
   148→        )
   149→    )

    12→def matches_exclusion(rel_path: str, exclusion: str) -> bool:
    13→    """Check if a relative path matches an exclusion pattern."""

    18→        import fnmatch
    19→
    20→        if any(fnmatch.fnmatch(part, exclusion) for part in parts):
    21→            return True
    22→    if "/" in exclusion or os.sep in exclusion:
    23→        normalized = exclusion.rstrip("/").rstrip(os.sep)
    24→        return rel_path.startswith(normalized + "/") or rel_path.startswith(
    25→            normalized + os.sep
    26→        )
    27→    return False
    28→
    29→
    30→def normalize_path_separators(path: str) -> str:
    31→    return path.replace("\\", "/")
    32→
    33→
    34→def safe_relpath(path: str | Path, start: str | Path) -> str:
    35→    try:
    36→        return os.path.relpath(str(path), str(start))
    37→    except ValueError:
    38→        return str(Path(path).resolve())
    39→
    40→
    41→def rel(path: str) -> str:
    42→    root = get_project_root()
    43→    resolved = Path(path).resolve()
    44→    try:
    45→        return normalize_path_separators(str(resolved.relative_to(root)))
    46→    except ValueError:
    47→        return normalize_path_separators(safe_relpath(resolved, root))
    48→
    49→
    50→def resolve_path(filepath: str) -> str:
    51→    """Resolve a filepath to absolute, handling both relative and absolute."""
    52→    p = Path(filepath)
    53→    if p.is_absolute():
    54→        return str(p.resolve())
    55→    return str((get_project_root() / filepath).resolve())
    56→
    57→
    58→def resolve_scan_file(
    59→    filepath: str | Path,
    60→    *,
    61→    scan_root: str | Path | None = None,
    62→) -> Path:
    63→    """Resolve a scan file path with explicit scan-root-first semantics.
    64→
    65→    Relative file paths are resolved against ``scan_root`` first (when provided)
    66→    and then against the process project root as a fallback.
    67→    """
    68→    p = Path(filepath)
    69→    if p.is_absolute():
    70→        return p.resolve()
    71→
    72→    root = get_project_root()
    73→    if scan_root is not None:
    74→        scan_root_path = Path(scan_root)
    75→        scan_root_abs = (
    76→            scan_root_path.resolve()
    77→            if scan_root_path.is_absolute()
    78→            else (root / scan_root_path).resolve()
    79→        )
    80→        scan_candidate = (scan_root_abs / p).resolve()
    81→        if scan_candidate.exists():
    82→            return scan_candidate
    83→
    84→    return (root / p).resolve()
    85→
    86→
    87→def safe_write_text(filepath: str | Path, content: str) -> None:
    88→    """Atomically write text to a file using temp+rename."""
    89→    p = Path(filepath)
    90→    p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    91→    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=p.parent, suffix=".tmp")
    92→    try:
    93→        with os.fdopen(fd, "w") as f:
    94→            f.write(content)
    95→        os.replace(tmp, str(p))
    96→    except OSError:
    97→        if os.path.exists(tmp):
    98→            os.unlink(tmp)
    99→        raise

   108→    "safe_relpath",
   109→    "safe_write_text",

   294→                if isinstance(ann, ast.Name):
   295→                    ann_name = ann.id
   296→                elif isinstance(ann, ast.Attribute):
   297→                    ann_name = ann.attr
   298→                if ann_name in typed_dicts:
   299→                    typed_vars[node.target.id] = ann_name
   300→            # Also check function param annotations
   301→            if isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef):
   302→                for arg in node.args.args + node.args.kwonlyargs:
   303→                    ann = arg.annotation
   304→                    if ann is None:
   305→                        continue
   306→                    ann_name = None
   307→                    if isinstance(ann, ast.Name):
   308→                        ann_name = ann.id
   309→                    elif isinstance(ann, ast.Attribute):
   310→                        ann_name = ann.attr
   311→                    if ann_name in typed_dicts:
   312→                        typed_vars[arg.arg] = ann_name
   313→
   314→        if not typed_vars:
   315→            continue
   316→
   317→        # Scan for violation calls — collect per (td_name, method, field)
   318→        hits: list[tuple[str, str, str | None, int]] = []
   319→        for node in ast.walk(tree):
   320→            if not isinstance(node, ast.Call):
   321→                continue
   322→            func = node.func
   323→            if not isinstance(func, ast.Attribute):
   324→                continue
   325→            if func.attr not in _VIOLATION_METHODS:
   326→                continue
   327→            if not isinstance(func.value, ast.Name) or func.value.id not in typed_vars:
   328→                continue
   329→            td_name = typed_vars[func.value.id]
   330→            # Extract the field name from the first argument if it's a string constant
   331→            field: str | None = None
   332→            if node.args and isinstance(node.args[0], ast.Constant):
   333→                val = node.args[0].value
   334→                if isinstance(val, str):
   335→                    field = val
   336→            hits.append((td_name, func.attr, field, node.lineno))
   337→
   338→        # Group by (td_name, method, field) for compact reporting
   339→        groups: dict[tuple[str, str, str | None], list[int]] = {}
   340→        for td_name, method, field, lineno in hits:
   341→            groups.setdefault((td_name, method, field), []).append(lineno)
   342→
   343→        for (td_name, method, field), lines in groups.items():
   344→            entry: dict = {
   345→                "file": rpath,
   346→                "typed_dict_name": td_name,
   347→                "violation_type": method,
   348→                "line": lines[0],
   349→                "count": len(lines),
   350→            }
   351→            if field is not None:
   352→                entry["field"] = field
   353→            violations.append(entry)
   354→
   355→    return violations
   356→
   357→
   358→def _abstractions_context(file_contents: dict[str, str]) -> dict:
   359→    util_files = []
   360→    wrappers_by_file: list[dict[str, object]] = []
   361→    interface_declarations: dict[str, set[str]] = defaultdict(set)
   362→    implementations: dict[str, set[str]] = defaultdict(set)
   363→    indirection_hotspots: list[dict[str, object]] = []
   364→    wide_param_bags: list[dict[str, object]] = []
   365→    delegation_classes: list[dict] = []
   366→    facade_modules: list[dict] = []
   367→    typed_dict_defs: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
   368→    parsed_trees: dict[str, ast.Module] = {}
   369→
   370→    total_function_signatures = 0
   371→    total_wrappers = 0
   372→
   373→    for filepath, content in file_contents.items():
   374→        rpath = rel(filepath)
   375→        loc = len(content.splitlines())
   376→        basename = Path(rpath).stem.lower()
   377→        if basename in {"utils", "helpers", "util", "helper", "common", "misc"}:
   378→            util_files.append(
   379→                {
   380→                    "file": rpath,
   381→                    "loc": loc,
   382→                    "excerpt": file_excerpt(filepath) or "",
   383→                }
   384→            )
   385→
   386→        # ── Regex-based detectors (all languages) ────────────
   387→        signatures = _DEF_SIGNATURE_RE.findall(content)
   388→        total_function_signatures += len(signatures)
   389→
   390→        ts_wrappers = [
   391→            (wrapper, target)
   392→            for wrapper, target in _TS_PASSTHROUGH_RE.findall(content)
   393→            if wrapper != target
   394→        ]
   395→
   396→        for match in _INTERFACE_RE.finditer(content):
   397→            iface = match.group(1) or match.group(2)
   398→            if iface:
   399→                interface_declarations[iface].add(rpath)

    16→def _audit_excluded_dirs(
    17→    exclusions: tuple[str, ...],
    18→    scanned_files: list[str],
    19→    project_root: Path,
    20→) -> list[dict]:
    21→    """Check if any --exclude directory has zero references from scanned code.
    22→
    23→    Returns findings for directories that appear stale (no file references them).
    24→    """
    25→    if not exclusions:
    26→        return []
    27→
    28→    candidate_dirs = [
    29→        ex_dir
    30→        for ex_dir in exclusions
    31→        if ex_dir not in DEFAULT_EXCLUSIONS and (project_root / ex_dir).is_dir()
    32→    ]
    33→    if not candidate_dirs:
    34→        return []
    35→
    36→    # Read each scanned file once and mark any exclusions observed in content.
    37→    unresolved = set(candidate_dirs)
    38→    for filepath in scanned_files:

    41→        abs_path = (

    44→        content = read_file_text(abs_path)
    45→        if content is None:
    46→            logger.debug(
    47→                "Skipping unreadable file %s while auditing exclusions", filepath
    48→            )
    49→            continue
    50→
    51→        matched = {ex_dir for ex_dir in unresolved if ex_dir in content}
    52→        if matched:
    53→            unresolved.difference_update(matched)
    54→
    55→    stale_findings = []
    56→    for ex_dir in candidate_dirs:

    59→        stale_findings.append(

    76→def _collect_codebase_metrics(lang, path: Path) -> dict | None:

    78→    if not lang or not lang.file_finder:

    80→    files = lang.file_finder(path)

   100→def _resolve_scan_profile(profile: str | None, lang) -> str:

   102→    if profile in {"objective", "full", "ci"}:

   105→    if default_profile in {"objective", "full", "ci"}:

   124→    explicit_lang = getattr(args, "lang", None)

   410→        max_chain_depth = max((token.count(".") for token in chain_matches), default=0)
   411→        if max_chain_depth >= 3 or len(chain_matches) >= 6:
   412→            indirection_hotspots.append(
   413→                {
   414→                    "file": rpath,
   415→                    "max_chain_depth": max_chain_depth,
   416→                    "chain_count": len(chain_matches),
   417→                }
   418→            )
   419→
   420→        wide_functions = sum(
   421→            1 for params_blob in signatures if _count_signature_params(params_blob) >= 7
   422→        )
   423→        bag_mentions = len(_CONFIG_BAG_RE.findall(content))
   424→        if wide_functions > 0 or bag_mentions >= 10:
   425→            wide_param_bags.append(
   426→                {
   427→                    "file": rpath,
   428→                    "wide_functions": wide_functions,
   429→                    "config_bag_mentions": bag_mentions,
   430→                }
   431→            )
   432→
   433→        # ── AST-based detectors (Python files only) ──────────
   434→        try:
   435→            tree = ast.parse(content)
   436→        except SyntaxError:
   437→            tree = None
   438→
   439→        if tree is not None:
   440→            parsed_trees[filepath] = tree
   441→
   442→            py_wrappers = _find_python_passthrough_wrappers(tree)
   443→
   444→            for entry in _find_delegation_heavy_classes(tree):
   445→                delegation_classes.append({"file": rpath, **entry})
   446→
   447→            facade_result = _find_facade_modules(tree, loc=loc)
   448→            if facade_result is not None:
   449→                facade_modules.append({"file": rpath, **facade_result})
   450→
   451→            _collect_typed_dict_defs(tree, typed_dict_defs)
   452→        else:
   453→            py_wrappers = []
   454→
   455→        wrapper_pairs = py_wrappers + ts_wrappers
   456→        if wrapper_pairs:
   457→            total_wrappers += len(wrapper_pairs)
   458→            wrappers_by_file.append(
   459→                {
   460→                    "file": rpath,
   461→                    "count": len(wrapper_pairs),
   462→                    "samples": [f"{w}->{t}" for w, t in wrapper_pairs[:5]],
   463→                }
   464→            )
   465→
   466→    # ── Post-loop cross-file analysis ─────────────────────────
   467→
   468→    one_impl_interfaces: list[dict[str, object]] = []
   469→    for iface, declared_in in interface_declarations.items():
   470→        implemented_in = sorted(implementations.get(iface, set()))
   471→        if len(implemented_in) != 1:
   472→            continue
   473→        one_impl_interfaces.append(
   474→            {
   475→                "interface": iface,
   476→                "declared_in": sorted(declared_in),
   477→                "implemented_in": implemented_in,
   478→            }
   479→        )
   480→
   481→    typed_dict_violations = _find_typed_dict_usage_violations(
   482→        parsed_trees, typed_dict_defs
   483→    )[:20]
   484→    total_typed_dict_violations = sum(v.get("count", 1) for v in typed_dict_violations)
   485→    typed_dict_violation_files = {v["file"] for v in typed_dict_violations}
   486→
   487→    # ── Sort ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
   488→
   489→    wrappers_by_file.sort(key=lambda item: -int(item["count"]))
   490→    indirection_hotspots.sort(
   491→        key=lambda item: (-int(item["max_chain_depth"]), -int(item["chain_count"]))
   492→    )
   493→    wide_param_bags.sort(
   494→        key=lambda item: (
   495→            -int(item["wide_functions"]),
   496→            -int(item["config_bag_mentions"]),
   497→        )
   498→    )
   499→    one_impl_interfaces.sort(key=lambda item: str(item["interface"]))
   500→    delegation_classes.sort(key=lambda d: -d["delegation_ratio"])
   501→    delegation_classes = delegation_classes[:20]
   502→    facade_modules.sort(key=lambda d: -d["re_export_ratio"])
   503→    facade_modules = facade_modules[:20]
   504→
   505→    # ── Sub-axis scoring ──────────────────────────────────────
   506→
   507→    wrapper_rate = total_wrappers / max(total_function_signatures, 1)
   508→    abstraction_leverage = _score_clamped(
   509→        100 - (wrapper_rate * 120) - (len(util_files) * 1.5)

## Comprehensive Detector Analysis Report

Based on my complete read of the detector registry and implementation files, here's what desloppify's detectors are actually capable of detecting:

### CANONICAL DETECTOR REGISTRY (45 detectors total)

The registry in `registry.py` defines the complete set across all languages. Here are all detectors organized by category:

#### AUTO-FIXABLE DETECTORS:
1. **unused** - removes unused imports and variables
2. **logs** - removes debug logs
3. **smells** - auto-fixes dead useEffect and empty if chains

#### REORGANIZATION DETECTORS (move-based):
4. **orphaned** - dead files
5. **uncalled_functions** - dead/unused functions
6. **flat_dirs** - shallow directory structures
7. **naming** - naming convention violations
8. **single_use** - files imported by only one other file (inlining candidates)
9. **coupling** - architectural boundary violations (shared→tools, tools→tools)
10. **cycles** - circular dependencies
11. **facade** - unnecessary re-export facades

#### REFACTORING DETECTORS:
12. **structural** - large/complex files needing decomposition
13. **props** - React component complexity
14. **react** - React antipatterns (state sync, provider nesting, hook bloat)
15. **dupes** - duplicate/near-duplicate functions
16. **patterns** - inconsistent patterns across codebase
17. **dict_keys** - dict key mismatches (dead writes, schema drift)
18. **test_coverage** - untested production modules
19. **signature** - inconsistent function signatures
20. **global_mutable_config** - module-level mutable state that gets modified
21. **private_imports** - private symbol imports across boundaries
22. **layer_violation** - architectural layer violations
23. **responsibility_cohesion** - modules with too many responsibilities
24. **boilerplate_duplication** - copy-pasted boilerplate across language plugins

#### MANUAL FIX DETECTORS:
25. **deprecated** - deprecated symbols
26. **stale_exclude** - stale exclusion rules
27. **security** - security findings (severity-ranked)

#### SUBJECTIVE REVIEW DETECTORS:
28. **review** - AI code review findings
29. **subjective_review** - design quality evaluation
30. **concerns** - design concerns from subjective evaluation

---

### LANGUAGE-SPECIFIC PYTHON DETECTORS (detailed from smells.py)

#### REGEX-BASED SMELL DETECTIONS:
- **eval_exec** - eval()/exec() usage (HIGH severity)
- **magic_number** - Magic numbers >1000 in logic (LOW severity)
- **todo_fixme** - TODO/FIXME/HACK/XXX comments (LOW severity)
- **hardcoded_url** - Hardcoded URLs in source (MEDIUM severity) — but skips UPPER_CASE constant assignments
- **debug_tag** - Vestigial debug tags in logs/prints like [TAG] (LOW severity)
- **workaround_tag** - Workaround tags in comments like [PascalCaseTag] (LOW severity)

#### MULTI-LINE/AST-BASED SMELL DETECTIONS:
- **star_import_no_all** - Star imports from modules without __all__ (MEDIUM severity)
- **empty_except** - Bare except blocks with just `pass` (HIGH severity)
- **swallowed_error** - Except blocks that only log the error (HIGH severity)
- **monster_function** - Functions >150 LOC (HIGH severity)
- **dead_function** - Functions with only `pass`/`return`/`return None` (MEDIUM severity)
- **inline_class** - Classes defined inside functions (MEDIUM severity)
- **deferred_import** - Function-level imports (possible circular import workarounds) (LOW severity)
- **subprocess_no_timeout** - subprocess calls without timeout (HIGH severity)
- **lru_cache_mutable** - @lru_cache/@cache on functions that read mutable globals (MEDIUM severity)
- **unsafe_file_write** - Non-atomic file writes (MEDIUM severity)
- **duplicate_constant** - Constants defined identically in multiple modules (MEDIUM severity)
- **unreachable_code** - Code after unconditional return/raise/break/continue (HIGH severity)
- **constant_return** - Functions always returning same constant (MEDIUM severity)
- **regex_backtrack** - Regex with nested quantifiers (ReDoS risk) (HIGH severity)
- **naive_comment_strip** - re.sub strips comments without string awareness (MEDIUM severity)
- **callback_logging** - Logging passed as callback parameter (MEDIUM severity)
- **hardcoded_path_sep** - Hardcoded '/' path separator (Windows incompatibility) (MEDIUM severity)
- **vestigial_parameter** - Parameters marked as unused/deprecated in comments (MEDIUM severity)
- **noop_function** - Non-trivial functions whose body does nothing (HIGH severity)
- **stderr_traceback** - traceback.print_exc() bypassing structured logging (HIGH severity)
- **import_path_mutation** - sys.path mutation at import time (HIGH severity)
- **import_env_mutation** - Environment loading at import time (MEDIUM severity)
- **import_runtime_init** - Runtime initialization at import time (MEDIUM severity)
- **sys_exit_in_library** - sys.exit() outside CLI entry points (HIGH severity)
- **silent_except** - Except handlers that silently suppress errors with pass/continue (HIGH severity)
- **optional_param_sprawl** - Too many optional params (MEDIUM severity)
- **annotation_quality** - Loose type annotations (MEDIUM severity)
- **nested_closure** - Deeply nested inner functions (MEDIUM severity)
- **mutable_ref_hack** - Mutable-list ref hacks like x=[v]; x[0] inside nested functions (MEDIUM severity)
- **high_cyclomatic_complexity** - Cyclomatic complexity >12 decision points (MEDIUM severity)

#### LANGUAGE-AGNOSTIC STRUCTURAL DETECTORS:

**Large Files (from large.py):**
- Default threshold: **500 lines of code**
- Simple LOC-based detection with no complexity scoring

**Complexity Scoring (from complexity.py):**
- Configurable per-language signals with weighted scoring
- Default threshold: score ≥15 to flag
- Minimum 50 LOC to consider
- Each signal has threshold and weight parameters
- Supports both regex patterns and custom compute functions

**Duplication Detection (from dupes.py):**
- **Exact duplicates** - same normalized body hash (similarity 1.0)
- **Near-duplicates** - difflib SequenceMatcher with configurable threshold (default 0.9)
- Only considers functions ≥15 LOC for near-duplicate comparison
- Uses body normalization (not AST-based)
- Output is clustered (N similar functions = 1 entry, not N² pairs)

**Coupling Analysis (from coupling.py):**
- **Backward coupling** - files in shared/ importing from tools/ (architectural violation)
- **Cross-tool coupling** - tools/A importing from tools/B (monolithic tool violation)
- **Boundary candidates** - shared/ files used by only one tool (move candidates)
- Prefix-based architectural enforcement (requires specific directory patterns)
- Tracks violating vs eligible edges

**Single-Use Detection (from single_use.py):**
- Files imported by exactly one other file
- Filters out test importers, language plugin entrypoints, barrel files
- Size range: 20-300 LOC (rejects too-small and too-large)
- Returns only reorganization candidates (not refactoring)

**Responsibility Cohesion (from responsibility_cohesion.py):**
- Detects modules with **disconnected responsibility clusters** (≥3 components, largest ≤65% of functions)
- Detects **mixed function families** (≥4 families, ≥2 components based on name prefix)
- Detects **import divergence** (≥3 distinct import cluster groups)
- Minimum 200 LOC, minimum 8 top-level functions per module
- Returns component decomposition analysis and family breakdown

**Global Mutable State (from mutable_state.py):**
- Module-level names initialized to mutable values: `[]`, `{}`, `set()`, `list()`, `dict()`, `defaultdict`, `OrderedDict`, `Counter`
- Detects **mutations via subscript** (name[k] = v) — no `global` keyword needed
- Detects **mutations via method calls** (name.append(x), name.update(y)) — no `global` keyword needed
- Detects **bare reassignments** (name = x) only if `global name` keyword is explicit
- Detects **augmented assignments** (name += x) only if `global name` is declared
- Excludes UPPER_CASE constants (assumed immutable by convention)
- **ALSO detects stale import bindings**: `from X import mutable_name` when the mutable gets reassigned in X
- Returns both definition line and list of mutation sites

**Implicit Mixin Contracts (from coupling_contracts.py):**
- Detects mixin-like classes (classes ending in "Mixin" or in `/phases/` paths)
- Flags classes that read undeclared host self-attributes (implicit contracts)
- Minimum 3 required attributes to flag
- Ignores declared contract attributes (annotated or set via setattr)
- Skips classes with explicit Protocol bases
- Helps identify missing mixin contracts

---

### WHAT IT CANNOT DETECT

Based on my thorough review, here are **limitations and gaps**:

#### a. FUNCTIONS WITH 16-22 PARAMETERS
**NOT DETECTED.** There is no parameter count detector. The `optional_param_sprawl` smell only flags "too many optional params" in a heuristic way (not counted). Parameter signature analysis exists but is for finding **inconsistent** signatures across functions, not bloated signatures.

#### b. 1400+ LINE FILES
**DETECTED, BUT WEAKLY.** The `large.py` detector flags files >500 LOC by default — a 1400-line file would be flagged, but there's no specific threshold or categorization by severity. The `structural` dimension is about decomposition, not absolute size.

#### c. GLOBAL MUTABLE STATE (module-level dicts/sets mutated at runtime)
**STRONGLY DETECTED.** `mutable_state.py` is explicitly designed for this:
- Catches `_extra_exclusions: dict = {}` at module level
- Detects both mutation via subscript (`_extra_exclusions[key] = value`) AND method calls (`_extra_exclusions.update(...)`)
- Detects reassignments when `global` keyword is present
- Also catches stale import bindings in other modules

#### d. BACKWARDS-COMPAT HACKS (string-matching on exception messages)
**NOT DETECTED.** There is no detector for this pattern. It would require string literal analysis paired with exception handling context, which no current detector does.

#### e. DICT SOUP (untyped dict params instead of dataclasses)
**NOT DETECTED.** While there's a `dict_keys` detector, it only flags **key mismatches** (dead writes, schema drift) detected via dict literal usage patterns, not function parameters. There's no type annotation analysis for parameter quality.

#### f. COPY-PASTED BOILERPLATE ACROSS 13 LANGUAGE PLUGINS
**REGISTRY HAS IT, BUT LANGUAGE-SPECIFIC IMPLEMENTATION MISSING.** The registry defines `boilerplate_duplication` as a refactoring-level detector, but I didn't find an actual implementation in the detector modules. The generic `dupes.py` catches near-duplicate **functions** (0.9+ similarity), but has no language-specific boilerplate clustering.

#### g. CIRCULAR IMPORT WORKAROUNDS (in-function imports)
**PARTIALLY DETECTED.** The `deferred_import` smell (in smells.py) flags function-level imports with comment "possible circular import workaround". However, it doesn't verify actual circular imports — it just flags the symptom.

#### h. OVERLY BROAD EXCEPTION CATCHING
**STRONGLY DETECTED.** Multiple detectors catch this:
- `empty_except` - bare `except:` blocks with just `pass`
- `swallowed_error` - broad except blocks that only log
- `silent_except` - except handlers with pass/continue and no logging
- Combines bare except (`except:`), `Exception`, and `BaseException` detection

---

### SUMMARY TABLE: CAN IT CATCH YOUR SPECIFIC ISSUES?

| Issue | Detected? | Detector | Notes |
|-------|-----------|----------|-------|
| **16-22 parameter functions** | ❌ NO | — | No parameter count analysis |
| **1400+ line files** | ✅ YES | `large.py` | Flags >500 LOC, no graduated severity |
| **Global mutable state (dict/set mutation)** | ✅ **STRONG YES** | `mutable_state.py` | Catches subscript, method calls, reassignments, stale imports |
| **Backwards-compat hacks (exception string matching)** | ❌ NO | — | Would need string+exception context analysis |
| **Dict soup (untyped dict params)** | ❌ NO | — | Only catches dict **key** mismatches, not type quality |
| **Boilerplate duplication (13 plugins)** | ⚠️ PARTIAL | `boilerplate_duplication` (registry only), `dupes.py` (functions only) | Registry defines it, but no cross-language boilerplate clustering |
| **Circular import workarounds** | ✅ YES | `deferred_import` smell | Flags symptom (function-level imports), not root cause verification |
| **Overly broad exception catching** | ✅ **STRONG YES** | `empty_except`, `swallowed_error`, `silent_except` | Comprehensive bare/Exception/BaseException detection |

### KEY INSIGHTS

1. **Strengths:** desloppify excels at detecting **architectural issues** (coupling, cycles), **code quality anti-patterns** (smells, duplication), and **runtime state hazards** (global mutable config).

2. **Architectural focus:** The detector registry is biased toward **structural/organizational problems** (reorganize category is largest) rather than **signature/interface quality** (parameter counts, type annotation strictness).

3. **Global mutable detection is mature:** The `mutable_state.py` detector is thorough and would catch the `_extra_exclusions` issue in your codebase immediately.

4. **Missing: Type/interface quality:** There are NO detectors for parameter counts, type annotation quality at a granular level, or function signature consistency (only cross-function inconsistency).

5. **Duplication detection is function-level:** The `dupes.py` detector uses body hashing and difflib for **functions**, not boilerplate **patterns** or **class hierarchies** across language boundaries.

## Summary: Understanding Desloppify's LLM-Based Review System

Based on reading the key files, here's what I've learned about the system:

### 1. **Review Dimensions Evaluated (20 total)**

The LLM reviewer evaluates code across these dimensions:

- **Naming quality** - intent-revealing names (detects: generic verbs like "process, handle, do, run", name/behavior mismatches)
- **Logic clarity** - control flow correctness (detects: identical branches, dead code, always-true conditions, redundant checks, async without await)
- **Type safety** - annotation/runtime contract matching (detects: return types missing paths, parameter type mismatches, over-union types)
- **Contract coherence** - function/module API honesty (detects: undocumented side effects, docstring divergence)
- **Error consistency** - unified error handling strategies (detects: mixed error types across modules, lost error context)
- **Abstraction fitness** - leveraging abstractions (detects: pass-through wrappers, delegation chains, "wide options/context bag APIs", leaky abstractions)
- **AI-generated debt** - LLM hallmarks (detects: restating comments, defensive overengineering, boilerplate duplication, debug logging)
- **High/Mid/Low-level elegance** - decomposition, handoffs, and implementation craft
- **Cross-module architecture** - dependency direction and cycles
- **Initialization coupling** - import-time side effects and boot-order dependencies
- **Convention outlier** - naming/organizational consistency
- **Dependency health** - unused/conflicting/heavy dependencies
- **Test strategy** - coverage and cross-module verification
- **API surface coherence** - consistency in function shapes and signatures
- **Authorization consistency** - auth patterns uniformly applied
- **Incomplete migration** - old+new API coexistence
- **Package organization** - directory layout matching ownership/change boundaries
- **Design coherence** - function focus and pattern consistency

### 2. **What the Review System ASKS About (From Dimensions)**

The prompts explicitly ask reviewers to look for:

- **"Wide options/context bag APIs"** - mentioned in abstraction_fitness as a leaky abstraction pattern
- **Parameter lists that should be config objects** - in design_coherence dimension
- **Functions doing too many things** - mixed responsibilities
- **Repeated structural patterns** - opportunities for data-driven refactoring
- **Boilerplate duplication** - explicitly called out in ai_generated_debt ("Identical boilerplate error handling copied verbatim")
- **Helper/util dumping grounds** - "systemic util/helper dumping grounds that create low cohesion"

### 3. **What Gets Collected for the Holistic Context**

The system gathers these signals before the LLM review:

- **`wide_param_bags`** (from budget.py lines 364, 420-431):
  - Counts functions with **≥7 parameters** 
  - Counts mentions of "config", "options", "params", "context" keywords (10+ mentions flagged)
  - Files with either metric get highlighted as potential abstraction fitness issues

- **`delegation_classes`** - Classes where >50% of methods forward to a single inner object
- **`facade_modules`** - Re-export-only modules (>70% public names are re-exports)
- **`typed_dict_violations`** - TypedDict fields accessed via `.get()/.setdefault()/.pop()` (breaking promised contracts)
- **`indirection_hotspots`** - Code with deep call chains (`obj.x.y.z...`)
- **`passthrough_wrappers`** - Functions that just forward to another function
- **Architecture context** - God modules (≥5 importers)
- **Coupling context** - Module-level I/O (import-time side effects)
- **Testing context** - Critical untested paths

### 4. **File Selection for Review**

From `selection.py`, files are prioritized by:

1. **Higher priority = more likely to be reviewed:**
   - High importer count (blast radius) - weighted 10x for regular files, 2x for low-value files
   - Existing open findings - weighted 5x each
   - Wontfixed structural findings - weighted 15x (human review adds most value here)
   - High complexity (>100 on complexity map) - weighted +20
   - Larger LOC (+1 point per 50 lines)

2. **Lower priority = less likely to be reviewed:**
   - Low-value files (types, constants, enums, index files) - score divided by 3
   - <20 LOC - filtered out completely
   - Small size in general

**For specific files you mentioned:**
- **runner_helpers.py** - Would be selected if: high importer count, >20 LOC, has open findings ✓
- **batches.py** - Would be selected if: high importer count, >20 LOC ✓
- **flat_dirs.py** - Would be selected if: high importer count, >20 LOC, has existing findings ✓

All three are implementation files (not types/constants), so they'd have normal priority weighting.

### 5. **Blind Spots in the Review System**

Based on the dimensions and signals gathered, here are **patterns the system might miss or underweight**:

1. **Global state / mutable import-time data** - While `initialization_coupling` flags import-time side effects, ongoing manipulation of module-level mutable state during normal execution is NOT explicitly flagged. The `_extra_exclusions` pattern in utils.py would pass through.

2. **Parameter count explosion** - Only flagged when ≥7 parameters. Functions with 5-6 parameters accumulate without triggering `wide_param_bags`.

3. **Dict soup / untyped data dictionaries** - The system looks for TypedDict violations (wrong access patterns), but doesn't flag:
   - Plain dicts passed around (no TypedDict contract)
   - Nested dict structures with unclear shapes
   - Dict keys as magic strings

4. **Context/options objects masking true API complexity** - If you hide 20 parameters inside a `config` object, `wide_param_bags` still counts it as passing (because function signature shows only 1-2 params). The system flags the NAME ("config" mentions), but not the underlying complexity.

5. **Monolithic functions with single responsibility** - The system skips "long functions with a single coherent responsibility" (design_coherence skip rules). A 300-line state machine in one function would score high if it's coherent.

6. **Coupling between internal implementation details** - The system looks at PUBLIC dependency graphs, but not internal coupling (functions calling many other functions in the same module through convoluted paths).

7. **Intermediate boilerplate/glue layers** - Translators and adapters that ARE doing something (not pure pass-throughs) but are thin/repetitive won't be flagged as easily.

8. **Complex conditional logic that's correct but hard to follow** - Logic_clarity flags provable errors (dead code, always-false conditions), not just hard-to-read logic.

9. **Comment debt / misleading documentation** - While mentioned in `comment_quality` dimension, it's not actively gathered in holistic context signals. The system relies on the LLM to spot it.

10. **Inter-file naming consistency** - `convention_outlier` catches naming drift across DIRECTORIES, but not subtle inconsistencies within modules (e.g., `run_X()` vs `execute_X()` patterns in sibling functions).

### 6. **Key Prompt Instructions to LLM**

From `batch_prompt_template.py`, the LLM is told:

- Start with seed files, then freely explore
- Prioritize high-signal leads (unexplored files, historical issue areas, hotspot neighbors)
- For package_organization: ground scoring in objective structure signals (fan_in/fan_out, coupling_matrix)
- For abstraction_fitness: use evidence from `holistic_context.abstractions` (delegation_heavy_classes, facade_modules, typed_dict_violations)
- Think structurally — when you see multiple issues with a common root cause, report the structural issue, not just symptoms
- Return 0-N findings (empty list is valid)
- Score conservatively: "Do not default to 100"

---

**In summary:** The review system is quite comprehensive at catching structural and cross-cutting issues, but has blind spots around **mutable global state, context-object parameter hiding, monolithic-but-coherent functions, and internal implementation coupling**. It's strongest at finding **API contracts, naming clarity, boilerplate duplication, and abstraction fitness issues**.

    81→    if not isinstance(value, ast.Call):
    82→        return None
    83→    target = value.func
    84→    if isinstance(target, ast.Name):
    85→        return target.id
    86→    return None
    87→
    88→
    89→def _find_python_passthrough_wrappers(tree: ast.Module) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    90→    """Find Python wrapper pairs via AST traversal."""
    91→    wrappers: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    92→    for node in ast.walk(tree):
    93→        if not isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef):
    94→            continue
    95→
    96→        body = _strip_docstring(list(node.body))
    97→        if len(body) != 1:
    98→            continue
    99→
   100→        target_name = _python_passthrough_target(body[0])
   101→        if target_name and node.name != target_name:
   102→            wrappers.append((node.name, target_name))
   103→    return wrappers
   104→
   105→
   106→def _is_delegation_stmt(stmt: ast.stmt) -> str | None:
   107→    """Return the delegate attribute name if *stmt* is a pure delegation.
   108→
   109→    Matches patterns like:
   110→    - ``return self.x.method(...)``
   111→    - ``return self.x``  (property forwarding)
   112→    - ``self.x.method(...)``  (void delegation)
   113→    """
   114→    # Unwrap Expr nodes (void calls like ``self.x.do()``)
   115→    if isinstance(stmt, ast.Expr):
   116→        value = stmt.value
   117→    elif isinstance(stmt, ast.Return) and stmt.value is not None:
   118→        value = stmt.value
   119→    else:
   120→        return None
   121→
   122→    # ``self.x.method(...)`` or ``self.x(...)``
   123→    if isinstance(value, ast.Call):
   124→        value = value.func
   125→
   126→    # Walk the attribute chain to find ``self.<attr>``
   127→    node = value
   128→    depth = 0
   129→    while isinstance(node, ast.Attribute):
   130→        node = node.value
   131→        depth += 1
   132→    if depth < 1 or not isinstance(node, ast.Name) or node.id != "self":
   133→        return None
   134→
   135→    # The first attribute after self — walk back down from the outermost
   136→    # Attribute to find the one whose .value is the Name("self") node.
   137→    first = value
   138→    while isinstance(first, ast.Attribute) and isinstance(first.value, ast.Attribute):
   139→        first = first.value
   140→    if isinstance(first, ast.Attribute) and isinstance(first.value, ast.Name):
   141→        return first.attr
   142→    return None
   143→
   144→
   145→def _find_delegation_heavy_classes(tree: ast.Module) -> list[dict]:
   146→    """Find classes where most methods delegate to a single inner object."""
   147→    results: list[dict] = []
   148→    for node in ast.walk(tree):
   149→        if not isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef):
   150→            continue
   151→
   152→        methods: list[ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef] = [
   153→            child
   154→            for child in node.body
   155→            if isinstance(child, ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef)
   156→            and child.name != "__init__"
   157→        ]
   158→        if len(methods) <= 3:
   159→            continue
   160→
   161→        # Track which methods delegate to which attribute
   162→        delegating_methods: dict[str, list[str]] = {}  # attr -> [method_names]
   163→        for method in methods:
   164→            body = _strip_docstring(list(method.body))
   165→            if len(body) != 1:
   166→                continue
   167→            attr = _is_delegation_stmt(body[0])
   168→            if attr:
   169→                delegating_methods.setdefault(attr, []).append(method.name)
   170→
   171→        if not delegating_methods:
   172→            continue
   173→
   174→        # Use the most common delegate target
   175→        top_attr = max(delegating_methods, key=lambda a: len(delegating_methods[a]))
   176→        delegate_count = len(delegating_methods[top_attr])
   177→        ratio = delegate_count / len(methods)
   178→        if ratio > 0.5:
   179→            results.append(
   180→                {
   181→                    "class_name": node.name,
   182→                    "line": node.lineno,
   183→                    "delegation_ratio": round(ratio, 2),
   184→                    "method_count": len(methods),
   185→                    "delegate_count": delegate_count,
   186→                    "delegate_target": top_attr,
   187→                    "sample_methods": delegating_methods[top_attr][:5],
   188→                }
   189→            )
   190→    return results
   191→
   192→
   193→def _find_facade_modules(tree: ast.Module, *, loc: int) -> dict | None:
   194→    """Detect modules where >70% of public names come from imports."""
   195→    import_names: set[str] = set()
   196→    defined_names: set[str] = set()
   197→
   198→    for node in ast.iter_child_nodes(tree):
   199→        if isinstance(node, ast.Import):
   200→            for alias in node.names:
   201→                name = alias.asname or alias.name.split(".")[-1]
   202→                import_names.add(name)
   203→        elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):
   204→            for alias in node.names:
   205→                if alias.name == "*":
   206→                    continue
   207→                name = alias.asname or alias.name
   208→                import_names.add(name)
   209→        elif isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef):
   210→            defined_names.add(node.name)
   211→        elif isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef):
   212→            defined_names.add(node.name)
   213→        elif isinstance(node, ast.Assign):
   214→            for target in node.targets:
   215→                if isinstance(target, ast.Name) and target.id == "__all__":
   216→                    continue
   217→                if isinstance(target, ast.Name):
   218→                    defined_names.add(target.id)
   219→
   220→    # Remove private names
   221→    public_imports = {n for n in import_names if not n.startswith("_")}
   222→    public_defs = {n for n in defined_names if not n.startswith("_")}
   223→
   224→    total_public = len(public_imports | public_defs)
   225→    if total_public < 3:
   226→        return None
   227→
   228→    # Re-exported = imported names that aren't shadowed by a local definition
   229→    re_exported = public_imports - public_defs
   230→    re_export_ratio = len(re_exported) / total_public
   231→
   232→    if re_export_ratio < 0.7 or len(public_defs) > 3:
   233→        return None
   234→
   235→    return {
   236→        "re_export_ratio": round(re_export_ratio, 2),
   237→        "defined_symbols": len(public_defs),
   238→        "re_exported_symbols": len(re_exported),
   239→        "samples": sorted(re_exported)[:5],
   240→        "loc": loc,
   241→    }
   242→
   243→
   244→def _collect_typed_dict_defs(
   245→    tree: ast.Module, accumulator: dict[str, set[str]]
   246→) -> None:
   247→    """Collect TypedDict class definitions from a single file's AST."""
   248→    for node in ast.walk(tree):
   249→        if not isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef):
   250→            continue
   251→        is_typed_dict = any(
   252→            (isinstance(b, ast.Name) and b.id == "TypedDict")
   253→            or (isinstance(b, ast.Attribute) and b.attr == "TypedDict")
   254→            for b in node.bases
   255→        )
   256→        if not is_typed_dict:
   257→            continue
   258→        fields: set[str] = set()
   259→        for child in node.body:
   260→            if isinstance(child, ast.AnnAssign) and isinstance(child.target, ast.Name):
   261→                fields.add(child.target.id)
   262→        if fields:
   263→            accumulator[node.name] = fields
   264→
   265→
   266→_VIOLATION_METHODS = frozenset({"get", "setdefault", "pop"})
   267→
   268→
   269→def _find_typed_dict_usage_violations(
   270→    parsed_trees: dict[str, ast.Module],
   271→    typed_dicts: dict[str, set[str]],
   272→) -> list[dict]:
   273→    """Find .get()/.setdefault()/.pop() calls on TypedDict-annotated variables.
   274→
   275→    *parsed_trees* maps absolute file paths to pre-parsed ASTs (built during
   276→    the main collection loop to avoid redundant parses).
   277→
   278→    Returns a list of violation dicts with file, typed_dict_name, violation_type,
   279→    line, field (when extractable), and count.
   280→    """
   281→    if not typed_dicts:
   282→        return []
   283→
   284→    violations: list[dict] = []
   285→    for filepath, tree in parsed_trees.items():
   286→        rpath = rel(filepath)
   287→
   288→        # Collect variable names annotated with known TypedDict types
   289→        typed_vars: dict[str, str] = {}  # var_name -> TypedDict name
   290→        for node in ast.walk(tree):
   291→            if isinstance(node, ast.AnnAssign) and isinstance(node.target, ast.Name):
   292→                ann = node.annotation
   293→                ann_name = None
   294→                if isinstance(ann, ast.Name):
   295→                    ann_name = ann.id
   296→                elif isinstance(ann, ast.Attribute):
   297→                    ann_name = ann.attr
   298→                if ann_name in typed_dicts:
   299→                    typed_vars[node.target.id] = ann_name
   300→            # Also check function param annotations
   301→            if isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef):
   302→                for arg in node.args.args + node.args.kwonlyargs:
   303→                    ann = arg.annotation
   304→                    if ann is None:
   305→                        continue
   306→                    ann_name = None
   307→                    if isinstance(ann, ast.Name):
   308→                        ann_name = ann.id
   309→                    elif isinstance(ann, ast.Attribute):
   310→                        ann_name = ann.attr
   311→                    if ann_name in typed_dicts:
   312→                        typed_vars[arg.arg] = ann_name
   313→
   314→        if not typed_vars:
   315→            continue
   316→
   317→        # Scan for violation calls — collect per (td_name, method, field)
   318→        hits: list[tuple[str, str, str | None, int]] = []
   319→        for node in ast.walk(tree):
   320→            if not isinstance(node, ast.Call):
   321→                continue
   322→            func = node.func
   323→            if not isinstance(func, ast.Attribute):
   324→                continue
   325→            if func.attr not in _VIOLATION_METHODS:
   326→                continue
   327→            if not isinstance(func.value, ast.Name) or func.value.id not in typed_vars:
   328→                continue
   329→            td_name = typed_vars[func.value.id]
   330→            # Extract the field name from the first argument if it's a string constant
   331→            field: str | None = None
   332→            if node.args and isinstance(node.args[0], ast.Constant):
   333→                val = node.args[0].value
   334→                if isinstance(val, str):
   335→                    field = val
   336→            hits.append((td_name, func.attr, field, node.lineno))
   337→
   338→        # Group by (td_name, method, field) for compact reporting
   339→        groups: dict[tuple[str, str, str | None], list[int]] = {}
   340→        for td_name, method, field, lineno in hits:
   341→            groups.setdefault((td_name, method, field), []).append(lineno)
   342→
   343→        for (td_name, method, field), lines in groups.items():
   344→            entry: dict = {
   345→                "file": rpath,
   346→                "typed_dict_name": td_name,
   347→                "violation_type": method,
   348→                "line": lines[0],
   349→                "count": len(lines),
   350→            }
   351→            if field is not None:
   352→                entry["field"] = field
   353→            violations.append(entry)
   354→
   355→    return violations
   356→
   357→
   358→def _abstractions_context(file_contents: dict[str, str]) -> dict:
   359→    util_files = []
   360→    wrappers_by_file: list[dict[str, object]] = []
   361→    interface_declarations: dict[str, set[str]] = defaultdict(set)
   362→    implementations: dict[str, set[str]] = defaultdict(set)
   363→    indirection_hotspots: list[dict[str, object]] = []
   364→    wide_param_bags: list[dict[str, object]] = []
   365→    delegation_classes: list[dict] = []
   366→    facade_modules: list[dict] = []
   367→    typed_dict_defs: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
   368→    parsed_trees: dict[str, ast.Module] = {}
   369→
   370→    total_function_signatures = 0
   371→    total_wrappers = 0
   372→
   373→    for filepath, content in file_contents.items():
   374→        rpath = rel(filepath)
   375→        loc = len(content.splitlines())
   376→        basename = Path(rpath).stem.lower()
   377→        if basename in {"utils", "helpers", "util", "helper", "common", "misc"}:
   378→            util_files.append(
   379→                {
   380→                    "file": rpath,
   381→                    "loc": loc,
   382→                    "excerpt": file_excerpt(filepath) or "",
   383→                }
   384→            )
   385→
   386→        # ── Regex-based detectors (all languages) ────────────
   387→        signatures = _DEF_SIGNATURE_RE.findall(content)
   388→        total_function_signatures += len(signatures)
   389→
   390→        ts_wrappers = [
   391→            (wrapper, target)
   392→            for wrapper, target in _TS_PASSTHROUGH_RE.findall(content)
   393→            if wrapper != target
   394→        ]
   395→
   396→        for match in _INTERFACE_RE.finditer(content):
   397→            iface = match.group(1) or match.group(2)
   398→            if iface:
   399→                interface_declarations[iface].add(rpath)
   400→
   401→        for match in _IMPLEMENTS_RE.finditer(content):
   402→            for iface in _extract_type_names(match.group(1)):
   403→                implementations[iface].add(rpath)
   404→        for match in _INHERITS_RE.finditer(content):
   405→            blob = match.group(1) or match.group(2) or ""
   406→            for iface in _extract_type_names(blob):
   407→                implementations[iface].add(rpath)
   408→
   409→        chain_matches = _CHAIN_RE.findall(content)
   410→        max_chain_depth = max((token.count(".") for token in chain_matches), default=0)
   411→        if max_chain_depth >= 3 or len(chain_matches) >= 6:
   412→            indirection_hotspots.append(
   413→                {
   414→                    "file": rpath,
   415→                    "max_chain_depth": max_chain_depth,
   416→                    "chain_count": len(chain_matches),
   417→                }
   418→            )
   419→
   420→        wide_functions = sum(
   421→            1 for params_blob in signatures if _count_signature_params(params_blob) >= 7
   422→        )
   423→        bag_mentions = len(_CONFIG_BAG_RE.findall(content))
   424→        if wide_functions > 0 or bag_mentions >= 10:
   425→            wide_param_bags.append(
   426→                {
   427→                    "file": rpath,
   428→                    "wide_functions": wide_functions,
   429→                    "config_bag_mentions": bag_mentions,
   430→                }
   431→            )
   432→
   433→        # ── AST-based detectors (Python files only) ──────────
   434→        try:
   435→            tree = ast.parse(content)
   436→        except SyntaxError:
   437→            tree = None
   438→
   439→        if tree is not None:
   440→            parsed_trees[filepath] = tree
   441→
   442→            py_wrappers = _find_python_passthrough_wrappers(tree)
   443→
   444→            for entry in _find_delegation_heavy_classes(tree):
   445→                delegation_classes.append({"file": rpath, **entry})
   446→
   447→            facade_result = _find_facade_modules(tree, loc=loc)
   448→            if facade_result is not None:
   449→                facade_modules.append({"file": rpath, **facade_result})
   450→
   451→            _collect_typed_dict_defs(tree, typed_dict_defs)
   452→        else:
   453→            py_wrappers = []
   454→
   455→        wrapper_pairs = py_wrappers + ts_wrappers
   456→        if wrapper_pairs:
   457→            total_wrappers += len(wrapper_pairs)
   458→            wrappers_by_file.append(
   459→                {
   460→                    "file": rpath,
   461→                    "count": len(wrapper_pairs),
   462→                    "samples": [f"{w}->{t}" for w, t in wrapper_pairs[:5]],
   463→                }
   464→            )
   465→
   466→    # ── Post-loop cross-file analysis ─────────────────────────
   467→
   468→    one_impl_interfaces: list[dict[str, object]] = []
   469→    for iface, declared_in in interface_declarations.items():
   470→        implemented_in = sorted(implementations.get(iface, set()))
   471→        if len(implemented_in) != 1:
   472→            continue
   473→        one_impl_interfaces.append(
   474→            {
   475→                "interface": iface,
   476→                "declared_in": sorted(declared_in),
   477→                "implemented_in": implemented_in,
   478→            }
   479→        )
   480→
   481→    typed_dict_violations = _find_typed_dict_usage_violations(
   482→        parsed_trees, typed_dict_defs
   483→    )[:20]
   484→    total_typed_dict_violations = sum(v.get("count", 1) for v in typed_dict_violations)
   485→    typed_dict_violation_files = {v["file"] for v in typed_dict_violations}
   486→
   487→    # ── Sort ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
   488→
   489→    wrappers_by_file.sort(key=lambda item: -int(item["count"]))
   490→    indirection_hotspots.sort(
   491→        key=lambda item: (-int(item["max_chain_depth"]), -int(item["chain_count"]))
   492→    )
   493→    wide_param_bags.sort(
   494→        key=lambda item: (
   495→            -int(item["wide_functions"]),
   496→            -int(item["config_bag_mentions"]),
   497→        )
   498→    )
   499→    one_impl_interfaces.sort(key=lambda item: str(item["interface"]))
   500→    delegation_classes.sort(key=lambda d: -d["delegation_ratio"])
   501→    delegation_classes = delegation_classes[:20]
   502→    facade_modules.sort(key=lambda d: -d["re_export_ratio"])
   503→    facade_modules = facade_modules[:20]
   504→
   505→    # ── Sub-axis scoring ──────────────────────────────────────
   506→
   507→    wrapper_rate = total_wrappers / max(total_function_signatures, 1)
   508→    abstraction_leverage = _score_clamped(
   509→        100 - (wrapper_rate * 120) - (len(util_files) * 1.5)
   510→    )
   511→    indirection_cost = _score_clamped(
   512→        100
   513→        - (sum(item["max_chain_depth"] for item in indirection_hotspots[:20]) * 2.5)
   514→        - (sum(item["wide_functions"] for item in wide_param_bags[:20]) * 2.0)
   515→    )
   516→    interface_honesty = _score_clamped(100 - (len(one_impl_interfaces) * 8))
   517→
   518→    top10_delegation = delegation_classes[:10]
   519→    avg_delegation_ratio = (
   520→        sum(d["delegation_ratio"] for d in top10_delegation) / len(top10_delegation)
   521→        if top10_delegation
   522→        else 0.0
   523→    )
   524→    delegation_density = _score_clamped(
   525→        100 - (avg_delegation_ratio * 80) - (len(delegation_classes) * 5)
   526→    )
   527→    avg_facade_ratio = (
   528→        sum(f["re_export_ratio"] for f in facade_modules[:10]) / len(facade_modules[:10])
   529→        if facade_modules
   530→        else 0.0
   531→    )
   532→    definition_directness = _score_clamped(
   533→        100 - (len(facade_modules) * 8) - (avg_facade_ratio * 50)
   534→    )
   535→    type_discipline = _score_clamped(
   536→        100
   537→        - (len(typed_dict_violation_files) * 6)
   538→        - (total_typed_dict_violations * 1.5)
   539→    )
   540→
   541→    util_files = sorted(util_files, key=lambda item: -item["loc"])[:20]
   542→    context: dict[str, object] = {
   543→        "util_files": util_files,
   544→        "summary": {
   545→            "wrapper_rate": round(wrapper_rate, 3),
   546→            "total_wrappers": total_wrappers,
   547→            "total_function_signatures": total_function_signatures,
   548→            "one_impl_interface_count": len(one_impl_interfaces),
   549→            "indirection_hotspot_count": len(indirection_hotspots),
   550→            "wide_param_bag_count": len(wide_param_bags),
   551→            "delegation_heavy_class_count": len(delegation_classes),
   552→            "facade_module_count": len(facade_modules),
   553→            "typed_dict_violation_count": total_typed_dict_violations,
   554→        },
   555→        "sub_axes": {
   556→            "abstraction_leverage": abstraction_leverage,
   557→            "indirection_cost": indirection_cost,
   558→            "interface_honesty": interface_honesty,
   559→            "delegation_density": delegation_density,
   560→            "definition_directness": definition_directness,
   561→            "type_discipline": type_discipline,
   562→        },
   563→    }
   564→    if wrappers_by_file:
   565→        context["pass_through_wrappers"] = wrappers_by_file[:20]
   566→    if one_impl_interfaces:
   567→        context["one_impl_interfaces"] = one_impl_interfaces[:20]
   568→    if indirection_hotspots:
   569→        context["indirection_hotspots"] = indirection_hotspots[:20]
   570→    if wide_param_bags:
   571→        context["wide_param_bags"] = wide_param_bags[:20]
   572→    if delegation_classes:
   573→        context["delegation_heavy_classes"] = delegation_classes
   574→    if facade_modules:
   575→        context["facade_modules"] = facade_modules
   576→    if typed_dict_violations:
   577→        context["typed_dict_violations"] = typed_dict_violations
   578→    return context
   579→
   580→
   581→def _codebase_stats(file_contents: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, int]:
   582→    total_loc = sum(len(content.splitlines()) for content in file_contents.values())
   583→    return {
   584→        "total_files": len(file_contents),
   585→        "total_loc": total_loc,
   586→    }
   587→

1→"""Holistic codebase-wide context gathering for cross-cutting review."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from pathlib import Path
     6→
     7→from desloppify.core.discovery_api import (
     8→    disable_file_cache,

    26→def select_holistic_files(path: Path, lang: object, files: list[str] | None) -> list[str]:

    48→def _architecture_context(lang, file_contents: dict[str, str]) -> dict:

    68→def _coupling_context(file_contents: dict[str, str]) -> dict:

    74→            if stripped.startswith(

    94→def _naming_conventions_context(file_contents: dict[str, str]) -> dict:

   101→        counter = dir_styles.setdefault(dir_name, Counter())
   102→        for name in _FUNC_NAME_RE.findall(content):

   105→            elif name[0].islower() and any(ch.isupper() for ch in name):
   106→                counter["camelCase"] += 1
   107→            elif name[0].isupper():
   108→                counter["PascalCase"] += 1
   109→    return {
   110→        name: dict(counter.most_common(3))
   111→        for name, counter in dir_styles.items()
   112→        if sum(counter.values()) >= 3
   113→    }

   116→def _sibling_behavior_context(
   117→    file_contents: dict[str, str], *, base_path: Path | str | None = None
   118→) -> dict:
   119→    root = Path(base_path).resolve() if base_path is not None else None
   120→
   121→    def _bucket_for(filepath: str) -> str | None:
   122→        target = Path(filepath).resolve()
   123→        if root is not None:
   124→            try:
   125→                parts = target.relative_to(root).parts
   126→                if len(parts) >= 2:
   127→                    return f"{parts[0]}/"
   128→                return None
   129→            except ValueError:
   130→                logger.debug("Path %s not relative to root %s, using fallback bucket", filepath, root)
   131→        parts = Path(filepath).parts
   132→        if len(parts) < 2:
   133→            return None
   134→        return f"{parts[-2]}/"
   135→
   136→    def _display_path(filepath: str) -> str:
   137→        target = Path(filepath).resolve()
   138→        if root is not None:
   139→            try:
   140→                return target.relative_to(root).as_posix()
   141→            except ValueError:
   142→                logger.debug("Path %s not relative to root %s, using rel() fallback", filepath, root)
   143→        return rel(filepath)
   144→
   145→    dir_imports: dict[str, dict[str, set[str]]] = {}
   146→    for filepath, content in file_contents.items():
   147→        dir_name = _bucket_for(filepath)
   148→        if dir_name is None:
   149→            continue
   150→        file_rel = _display_path(filepath)
   151→        dir_imports.setdefault(dir_name, {})[file_rel] = _extract_imported_names(content)
   152→
   153→    sibling_behavior: dict = {}
   154→    for dir_name, file_names_map in dir_imports.items():
   155→        total = len(file_names_map)
   156→        if total < 3:
   157→            continue
   158→        name_counts: Counter = Counter()
   159→        for names in file_names_map.values():
   160→            for name in names:
   161→                name_counts[name] += 1
   162→        threshold = total * 0.6
   163→        shared = {
   164→            name: count for name, count in name_counts.items() if count >= threshold
   165→        }
   166→        if not shared:
   167→            continue
   168→        outliers = []
   169→        for file_rel, names in file_names_map.items():
   170→            missing = [name for name in shared if name not in names]
   171→            if missing:
   172→                outliers.append({"file": file_rel, "missing": sorted(missing)})
   173→        if not outliers:
   174→            continue
   175→        sibling_behavior[dir_name] = {
   176→            "shared_patterns": {
   177→                name: {"count": count, "total": total}
   178→                for name, count in sorted(shared.items(), key=lambda item: -item[1])
   179→            },
   180→            "outliers": sorted(
   181→                outliers, key=lambda item: len(item["missing"]), reverse=True
   182→            ),
   183→        }
   184→    return sibling_behavior

   191→        if len(parts) < 2:

   193→        dir_name = parts[-2] + "/"
   194→        counter = dir_errors.setdefault(dir_name, Counter())
   195→        for pattern_name, pattern in _ERROR_PATTERNS.items():
   196→            matches = pattern.findall(content)
   197→            if matches:
   198→                counter[pattern_name] += len(matches)
   199→    return {
   200→        name: dict(counter.most_common(5))
   201→        for name, counter in dir_errors.items()
   202→        if sum(counter.values()) >= 2
   203→    }
   204→
   205→
   206→def _dependencies_context(state: dict) -> dict:
   207→    cycle_findings = [
   208→        finding
   209→        for finding in state.get("findings", {}).values()
   210→        if finding.get("detector") == "cycles" and finding.get("status") == "open"
   211→    ]
   212→    if not cycle_findings:
   213→        return {}
   214→    return {
   215→        "existing_cycles": len(cycle_findings),
   216→        "cycle_summaries": [finding["summary"][:120] for finding in cycle_findings[:10]],
   217→    }

   219→
   220→def _testing_context(lang, state: dict, file_contents: dict[str, str]) -> dict:

   241→            )
   242→    testing["critical_untested"] = sorted(
   243→        critical_untested,
   244→        key=lambda item: -item["importers"],

    17→from desloppify.intelligence.review._context.models import ReviewContext
    18→from desloppify.intelligence.review._context.patterns import (

    31→# ── Shared helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────
    32→
    33→
    34→def abs_path(filepath: str) -> str:
    35→    """Resolve filepath to absolute using resolve_path."""
    36→    return resolve_path(filepath)
    37→
    38→
    39→def file_excerpt(filepath: str, max_lines: int = 30) -> str | None:
    40→    """Read first *max_lines* of a file, returning the text or None."""
    41→    content = read_file_text(abs_path(filepath))
    42→    if content is None:
    43→        return None
    44→    lines = content.splitlines(keepends=True)
    45→    if len(lines) <= max_lines:
    46→        return content
    47→    return "".join(lines[:max_lines]) + f"\n... ({len(lines) - max_lines} more lines)"
    48→
    49→
    50→def dep_graph_lookup(graph: dict, filepath: str) -> dict:
    51→    """Look up a file in the dep graph, trying absolute and relative keys."""
    52→    resolved = resolve_path(filepath)
    53→    entry = graph.get(resolved)
    54→    if entry is not None:
    55→        return entry
    56→    # Try relative path
    57→    rpath = rel(filepath)
    58→    entry = graph.get(rpath)
    59→    if entry is not None:
    60→        return entry
    61→    return {}
    62→
    63→
    64→def importer_count(entry: dict) -> int:
    65→    """Extract importer count from a dep graph entry."""
    66→    importers = entry.get("importers", set())
    67→    if isinstance(importers, set):
    68→        return len(importers)
    69→    return entry.get("importer_count", 0)
    70→

    73→

    75→def build_review_context(
    76→    path: Path,
    77→    lang,
    78→    state: dict,
    79→    files: list[str] | None = None,
    80→) -> ReviewContext:
    81→    """Gather codebase conventions for contextual evaluation.
    82→
    83→    If *files* is provided, skip file_finder (avoids redundant filesystem walks).
    84→    """
    85→    if files is None:
    86→        files = lang.file_finder(path) if lang.file_finder else []
    87→    ctx = ReviewContext()
    88→
    89→    if not files:
    90→        return ctx
    91→
    92→    already_cached = is_file_cache_enabled()
    93→    if not already_cached:
    94→        enable_file_cache()
    95→    try:
    96→        return _build_review_context_inner(files, lang, state, ctx)
    97→    finally:
    98→        if not already_cached:
    99→            disable_file_cache()

   102→def _build_review_context_inner(

   109→    # Pre-read all file contents once (cache will store them)
   110→    file_contents: dict[str, str] = {}
   111→    for filepath in files:

   121→            total_names += 1
   122→            match = NAME_PREFIX_RE.match(name)
   123→            if match:
   124→                prefix_counter[match.group(1)] += 1
   125→    ctx.naming_vocabulary = {
   126→        "prefixes": dict(prefix_counter.most_common(20)),
   127→        "total_names": total_names,
   128→    }
   129→
   130→    # 2. Error handling conventions — scan for patterns
   131→    error_counts: Counter = Counter()
   132→    for content in file_contents.values():
   133→        for pattern_name, pattern in ERROR_PATTERNS.items():

   136→    ctx.error_conventions = dict(error_counts)
   137→
   138→    # 3. Module patterns — what each directory typically uses

   141→    if not callable(module_pattern_fn):

   154→        if re.search(r"\bclass\s+\w+", content):

   156→    ctx.module_patterns = {

   159→        if sum(c.values()) >= 3

   163→    if lang.dep_graph:

   170→        top = sorted(importer_counts.items(), key=lambda item: -item[1])[:20]
   171→        ctx.import_graph_summary = {"top_imported": dict(top)}

   178→    findings = state.get("findings", {})

   184→            )
   185→    ctx.existing_findings = by_file

   188→    total_files = len(file_contents)

   190→    ctx.codebase_stats = {

   200→

   214→        d: dict(c.most_common(5))
   215→        for d, c in dir_functions.items()
   216→        if sum(c.values()) >= 3
   217→    }
   218→
   219→    # 9. AI debt signals
   220→    ctx.ai_debt_signals = gather_ai_debt_signals(file_contents, rel_fn=rel)
   221→
   222→    # 10. Auth patterns
   223→    ctx.auth_patterns = gather_auth_context(file_contents, rel_fn=rel)
   224→
   225→    # 11. Error strategies per file
   226→    strategies: dict[str, str] = {}
   227→    for filepath, content in file_contents.items():
   228→        strategy = classify_error_strategy(content)
   229→        if strategy:
   230→            strategies[rel(filepath)] = strategy
   231→    ctx.error_strategies = strategies
   232→
   233→    ctx.normalize_sections(strict=True)
   234→    return ctx
   235→
   236→
   237→def serialize_context(ctx: ReviewContext) -> dict:
   238→    """Convert ReviewContext to a JSON-serializable dict."""
   239→    def _section_dict(value: object) -> dict:
   240→        if hasattr(value, "to_dict") and callable(value.to_dict):
   241→            data = value.to_dict()
   242→            return data if isinstance(data, dict) else {}
   243→        return dict(value) if isinstance(value, dict) else {}
   244→
   245→    metrics = ("total_files", "total_loc", "avg_file_loc")
   246→    codebase_stats = _section_dict(ctx.codebase_stats)
   247→    out = {
   248→        "naming_vocabulary": _section_dict(ctx.naming_vocabulary),
   249→        "error_conventions": _section_dict(ctx.error_conventions),
   250→        "module_patterns": _section_dict(ctx.module_patterns),
   251→        "import_graph_summary": _section_dict(ctx.import_graph_summary),
   252→        "zone_distribution": _section_dict(ctx.zone_distribution),
   253→        "existing_findings": _section_dict(ctx.existing_findings),
   254→        "codebase_stats": {
   255→            key: int(codebase_stats.get(key, 0))
   256→            for key in metrics
   257→        },
   258→        "sibling_conventions": _section_dict(ctx.sibling_conventions),
   259→    }
   260→    if ctx.ai_debt_signals:
   261→        out["ai_debt_signals"] = _section_dict(ctx.ai_debt_signals)
   262→    if ctx.auth_patterns:
   263→        out["auth_patterns"] = _section_dict(ctx.auth_patterns)
   264→    if ctx.error_strategies:
   265→        out["error_strategies"] = _section_dict(ctx.error_strategies)
   266→    return out

1→"""Directory-level structure/coupling context for holistic review."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from collections import Counter
     6→from pathlib import Path
     7→from typing import Any
     8→
     9→from desloppify.core.discovery_api import rel, resolve_path
    10→from desloppify.intelligence.review.context import importer_count
    11→
    12→
    13→def compute_structure_context(
    14→    file_contents: dict[str, str], lang: Any
    15→) -> dict[str, object]:
    16→    """Compute directory profiles, root-level file analysis, and coupling matrix."""
    17→    graph = lang.dep_graph or {}
    18→    structure: dict[str, object] = {}
    19→
    20→    file_info: dict[str, dict] = {}
    21→    for filepath, content in file_contents.items():
    22→        rel_path = rel(filepath)
    23→        loc = len(content.splitlines())
    24→        entry = graph.get(resolve_path(filepath), {})
    25→        fan_in = importer_count(entry)
    26→        imports_raw = entry.get("imports", set())
    27→        fan_out = (
    28→            len(imports_raw)
    29→            if isinstance(imports_raw, set)
    30→            else entry.get("import_count", 0)
    31→        )
    32→        file_info[rel_path] = {"loc": loc, "fan_in": fan_in, "fan_out": fan_out}
    33→
    34→    dir_files: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    35→    for rel_path in file_info:
    36→        parts = Path(rel_path).parts
    37→        dir_key = "." if len(parts) == 1 else str(Path(*parts[:-1])) + "/"
    38→        dir_files.setdefault(dir_key, []).append(rel_path)
    39→
    40→    dir_profiles: dict[str, dict] = {}
    41→    for dir_key, files_in_dir in dir_files.items():
    42→        if len(files_in_dir) < 2:
    43→            continue
    44→
    45→        total_loc = sum(file_info[file]["loc"] for file in files_in_dir)
    46→        avg_fan_in = sum(file_info[file]["fan_in"] for file in files_in_dir) / len(
    47→            files_in_dir
    48→        )
    49→        avg_fan_out = sum(file_info[file]["fan_out"] for file in files_in_dir) / len(
    50→            files_in_dir
    51→        )
    52→
    53→        imports_from: Counter = Counter()
    54→        imported_by: Counter = Counter()
    55→        for file in files_in_dir:
    56→            entry = graph.get(resolve_path(file), {})
    57→            for imp in entry.get("imports", set()):
    58→                imp_rel = rel(imp)
    59→                imp_parts = Path(imp_rel).parts
    60→                imp_dir = (
    61→                    str(Path(*imp_parts[:-1])) + "/" if len(imp_parts) > 1 else "."
    62→                )
    63→                if imp_dir != dir_key:
    64→                    imports_from[imp_dir] += 1
    65→            for imp in entry.get("importers", set()):
    66→                imp_rel = rel(imp)
    67→                imp_parts = Path(imp_rel).parts
    68→                imp_dir = (
    69→                    str(Path(*imp_parts[:-1])) + "/" if len(imp_parts) > 1 else "."
    70→                )
    71→                if imp_dir != dir_key:
    72→                    imported_by[imp_dir] += 1
    73→
    74→        zone_counts: Counter = Counter()
    75→        if lang.zone_map is not None:
    76→            for file in files_in_dir:
    77→                zone_counts[lang.zone_map.get(file).value] += 1
    78→
    79→        dir_profiles[dir_key] = {
    80→            "file_count": len(files_in_dir),
    81→            "files": [Path(file).name for file in sorted(files_in_dir)],
    82→            "total_loc": total_loc,
    83→            "avg_fan_in": round(avg_fan_in, 1),
    84→            "avg_fan_out": round(avg_fan_out, 1),
    85→        }
    86→        if zone_counts:
    87→            dir_profiles[dir_key]["zones"] = dict(zone_counts)
    88→        if imports_from:
    89→            dir_profiles[dir_key]["imports_from_dirs"] = dict(
    90→                imports_from.most_common(10)
    91→            )
    92→        if imported_by:
    93→            dir_profiles[dir_key]["imported_by_dirs"] = dict(
    94→                imported_by.most_common(10)
    95→            )
    96→
    97→    structure["directory_profiles"] = dir_profiles
    98→
    99→    root_files = []
   100→    for rel_path in dir_files.get(".", []):
   101→        info = file_info[rel_path]
   102→        role = "core" if info["fan_in"] >= 5 else "peripheral"
   103→        root_files.append(
   104→            {
   105→                "file": rel_path,
   106→                "loc": info["loc"],
   107→                "fan_in": info["fan_in"],
   108→                "fan_out": info["fan_out"],
   109→                "role": role,
   110→            }
   111→        )
   112→    if root_files:
   113→        root_files.sort(key=lambda item: -item["fan_in"])
   114→        structure["root_files"] = root_files
   115→
   116→    edge_counts: Counter = Counter()
   117→    for dir_key, profile in dir_profiles.items():
   118→        for target, count in profile.get("imports_from_dirs", {}).items():
   119→            edge_counts[f"{dir_key} → {target}"] += count
   120→    if edge_counts:
   121→        structure["coupling_matrix"] = dict(edge_counts.most_common(20))
   122→
   123→    return structure
   124→
   125→
   126→__all__ = ["compute_structure_context"]
   127→
