1→"""Sizing and truncation helpers for holistic context payloads."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import ast
     6→import re
     7→from collections import defaultdict
     8→from pathlib import Path
     9→
    10→from desloppify.core.discovery_api import rel
    11→from desloppify.intelligence.review.context import file_excerpt
    12→
    13→_DEF_SIGNATURE_RE = re.compile(
    14→    r"(?:^|\n)\s*(?:async\s+def|def|async\s+function|function)\s+\w+\s*\(([^)]*)\)",
    15→    re.MULTILINE,
    16→)
    17→_TS_PASSTHROUGH_RE = re.compile(
    18→    r"\bfunction\s+(\w+)\s*\([^)]*\)\s*\{\s*return\s+(\w+)\s*\(",
    19→    re.MULTILINE,
    20→)
    21→_INTERFACE_RE = re.compile(
    22→    r"\binterface\s+([A-Za-z_]\w*)\b|\bclass\s+([A-Za-z_]\w*Protocol)\b"
    23→)
    24→_IMPLEMENTS_RE = re.compile(r"\bclass\s+\w+\s+implements\s+([^{:\n]+)")
    25→_INHERITS_RE = re.compile(r"\bclass\s+\w+\s*(?:\(([^)\n]+)\)\s*:|:\s*([^\n{]+))")
    26→_CHAIN_RE = re.compile(r"\b(?:\w+\.){2,}\w+\b")
    27→_CONFIG_BAG_RE = re.compile(
    28→    r"\b(?:config|configs|options|opts|params|ctx|context)\b",
    29→    re.IGNORECASE,
    30→)
    31→
    32→
    33→def _count_signature_params(params_blob: str) -> int:
    34→    """Best-effort parameter counting for function signatures."""
    35→    cleaned = params_blob.strip()
    36→    if not cleaned:
    37→        return 0
    38→    parts = [part.strip() for part in cleaned.split(",") if part.strip()]
    39→    filtered = [part for part in parts if part not in {"self", "cls", "this"}]
    40→    return len(filtered)
    41→
    42→
    43→def _extract_type_names(blob: str) -> list[str]:
    44→    """Extract candidate type names from implements/inherits blobs."""
    45→    names: list[str] = []
    46→    for raw in re.split(r"[,\s()]+", blob):
    47→        token = raw.strip()
    48→        if not token:
    49→            continue
    50→        token = token.split(".")[-1]
    51→        token = token.split("<")[0]
    52→        token = token.strip(":")
    53→        if not token or not re.match(r"^[A-Za-z_]\w*$", token):
    54→            continue
    55→        names.append(token)
    56→    return names
    57→
    58→
    59→def _score_clamped(raw: float) -> int:
    60→    """Clamp score-like values to [0, 100]."""
    61→    return int(max(0, min(100, round(raw))))
    62→
    63→
    64→def _strip_docstring(body: list[ast.stmt]) -> list[ast.stmt]:
    65→    """Strip a leading docstring from a function/method body."""
    66→    if (
    67→        body
    68→        and isinstance(body[0], ast.Expr)
    69→        and isinstance(body[0].value, ast.Constant)
    70→        and isinstance(body[0].value.value, str)
    71→    ):
    72→        return body[1:]
    73→    return body
    74→
    75→
    76→def _python_passthrough_target(stmt: ast.stmt) -> str | None:
    77→    """Return passthrough call target when stmt is `return target(...)`."""
    78→    if not isinstance(stmt, ast.Return):
    79→        return None
    80→    value = stmt.value
    81→    if not isinstance(value, ast.Call):
    82→        return None
    83→    target = value.func
    84→    if isinstance(target, ast.Name):
    85→        return target.id
    86→    return None
    87→
    88→
    89→def _find_python_passthrough_wrappers(tree: ast.Module) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    90→    """Find Python wrapper pairs via AST traversal."""
    91→    wrappers: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    92→    for node in ast.walk(tree):
    93→        if not isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef):
    94→            continue
    95→
    96→        body = _strip_docstring(list(node.body))
    97→        if len(body) != 1:
    98→            continue
    99→
   100→        target_name = _python_passthrough_target(body[0])

    13→def compute_structure_context(
    14→    file_contents: dict[str, str], lang: Any
    15→) -> dict[str, object]:
    16→    """Compute directory profiles, root-level file analysis, and coupling matrix."""
    17→    graph = lang.dep_graph or {}
    18→    structure: dict[str, object] = {}
    19→
    20→    file_info: dict[str, dict] = {}
    21→    for filepath, content in file_contents.items():
    22→        rel_path = rel(filepath)
    23→        loc = len(content.splitlines())
    24→        entry = graph.get(resolve_path(filepath), {})
    25→        fan_in = importer_count(entry)
    26→        imports_raw = entry.get("imports", set())
    27→        fan_out = (
    28→            len(imports_raw)
    29→            if isinstance(imports_raw, set)
    30→            else entry.get("import_count", 0)
    31→        )
    32→        file_info[rel_path] = {"loc": loc, "fan_in": fan_in, "fan_out": fan_out}
    33→
    34→    dir_files: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    35→    for rel_path in file_info:
    36→        parts = Path(rel_path).parts
    37→        dir_key = "." if len(parts) == 1 else str(Path(*parts[:-1])) + "/"
    38→        dir_files.setdefault(dir_key, []).append(rel_path)
    39→
    40→    dir_profiles: dict[str, dict] = {}
    41→    for dir_key, files_in_dir in dir_files.items():
    42→        if len(files_in_dir) < 2:
    43→            continue
    44→
    45→        total_loc = sum(file_info[file]["loc"] for file in files_in_dir)
    46→        avg_fan_in = sum(file_info[file]["fan_in"] for file in files_in_dir) / len(
    47→            files_in_dir
    48→        )
    49→        avg_fan_out = sum(file_info[file]["fan_out"] for file in files_in_dir) / len(
    50→            files_in_dir
    51→        )
    52→
    53→        imports_from: Counter = Counter()
    54→        imported_by: Counter = Counter()
    55→        for file in files_in_dir:
    56→            entry = graph.get(resolve_path(file), {})
    57→            for imp in entry.get("imports", set()):
    58→                imp_rel = rel(imp)
    59→                imp_parts = Path(imp_rel).parts
    60→                imp_dir = (
    61→                    str(Path(*imp_parts[:-1])) + "/" if len(imp_parts) > 1 else "."
    62→                )
    63→                if imp_dir != dir_key:
    64→                    imports_from[imp_dir] += 1
    65→            for imp in entry.get("importers", set()):
    66→                imp_rel = rel(imp)
    67→                imp_parts = Path(imp_rel).parts
    68→                imp_dir = (
    69→                    str(Path(*imp_parts[:-1])) + "/" if len(imp_parts) > 1 else "."
    70→                )
    71→                if imp_dir != dir_key:
    72→                    imported_by[imp_dir] += 1
    73→
    74→        zone_counts: Counter = Counter()
    75→        if lang.zone_map is not None:
    76→            for file in files_in_dir:
    77→                zone_counts[lang.zone_map.get(file).value] += 1
    78→
    79→        dir_profiles[dir_key] = {
    80→            "file_count": len(files_in_dir),
    81→            "files": [Path(file).name for file in sorted(files_in_dir)],
    82→            "total_loc": total_loc,
    83→            "avg_fan_in": round(avg_fan_in, 1),
    84→            "avg_fan_out": round(avg_fan_out, 1),
    85→        }
    86→        if zone_counts:
    87→            dir_profiles[dir_key]["zones"] = dict(zone_counts)
    88→        if imports_from:
    89→            dir_profiles[dir_key]["imports_from_dirs"] = dict(
    90→                imports_from.most_common(10)
    91→            )
    92→        if imported_by:
    93→            dir_profiles[dir_key]["imported_by_dirs"] = dict(
    94→                imported_by.most_common(10)
    95→            )
    96→
    97→    structure["directory_profiles"] = dir_profiles
    98→
    99→    root_files = []
   100→    for rel_path in dir_files.get(".", []):
   101→        info = file_info[rel_path]
   102→        role = "core" if info["fan_in"] >= 5 else "peripheral"
   103→        root_files.append(
   104→            {
   105→                "file": rel_path,
   106→                "loc": info["loc"],
   107→                "fan_in": info["fan_in"],
   108→                "fan_out": info["fan_out"],
   109→                "role": role,
   110→            }
   111→        )
   112→    if root_files:
   113→        root_files.sort(key=lambda item: -item["fan_in"])
   114→        structure["root_files"] = root_files
   115→
   116→    edge_counts: Counter = Counter()
   117→    for dir_key, profile in dir_profiles.items():
   118→        for target, count in profile.get("imports_from_dirs", {}).items():
   119→            edge_counts[f"{dir_key} → {target}"] += count
   120→    if edge_counts:
   121→        structure["coupling_matrix"] = dict(edge_counts.most_common(20))
   122→
   123→    return structure
   124→
   125→
   126→__all__ = ["compute_structure_context"]

    62→def parse_batch_selection(raw: str | None, batch_count: int) -> list[int]:
    63→    """Parse optional 1-based CSV list of batches."""
    64→    if not raw:
    65→        return list(range(batch_count))
    66→
    67→    selected: list[int] = []
    68→    seen: set[int] = set()
    69→    for token in raw.split(","):
    70→        text = token.strip()
    71→        if not text:
    72→            continue
    73→        idx_1 = int(text)
    74→        if idx_1 < 1 or idx_1 > batch_count:
    75→            raise ValueError(f"batch index {idx_1} out of range 1..{batch_count}")
    76→        idx_0 = idx_1 - 1
    77→        if idx_0 in seen:
    78→            continue
    79→        seen.add(idx_0)
    80→        selected.append(idx_0)
    81→    return selected

    84→def extract_json_payload(raw: str, *, log_fn) -> dict[str, object] | None:

    86→    text = raw.strip()
    87→    if not text:
    88→        return None
    89→

    91→    last_decode_error: json.JSONDecodeError | None = None
    92→    for start, ch in enumerate(text):

    95→        try:

    97→        except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:

   102→            and isinstance(obj.get("assessments"), dict)
   103→            and isinstance(obj.get("findings"), list)

   106→    if last_decode_error is not None:
   107→        log_fn(f"  batch output JSON parse failed: {last_decode_error.msg}")
   108→    else:

   133→    if not isinstance(impact_scope, str) or not impact_scope.strip():

1→"""Finding factory functions — normalize raw detector output into Finding dicts."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from collections import defaultdict
     6→from pathlib import Path
     7→
     8→from desloppify.core.enums import Tier
     9→from desloppify.core.discovery_api import rel
    10→from desloppify.state import Finding, make_finding
    11→
    12→
    13→def make_unused_findings(entries: list[dict], stderr_fn) -> list[Finding]:
    14→    """Transform raw unused-detector entries into normalized findings.
    15→
    16→    Shared by both Python and TypeScript unused phases.
    17→    """
    18→    results = []
    19→    for e in entries:
    20→        tier = 1 if e["category"] == "imports" else 2
    21→        results.append(
    22→            make_finding(
    23→                "unused",
    24→                e["file"],
    25→                e["name"],
    26→                tier=tier,
    27→                confidence="high",
    28→                summary=f"Unused {e['category']}: {e['name']}",
    29→                detail={"line": e["line"], "category": e["category"]},
    30→            )
    31→        )
    32→    stderr_fn(f"         {len(entries)} instances -> {len(results)} findings")
    33→    return results
    34→
    35→
    36→def make_dupe_findings(entries: list[dict], stderr_fn) -> list[Finding]:
    37→    """Transform clustered duplicate entries into normalized findings.
    38→
    39→    Each entry represents a cluster of similar functions. One finding per cluster.
    40→    """
    41→    results = []
    42→    for e in entries:
    43→        a, b = e["fn_a"], e["fn_b"]
    44→        if a["loc"] < 10 and b["loc"] < 10:
    45→            continue
    46→        cluster_size = e.get("cluster_size", 2)
    47→        pair = sorted([(a["file"], a["name"]), (b["file"], b["name"])])
    48→        name = f"{pair[0][1]}::{rel(pair[1][0])}::{pair[1][1]}"
    49→        tier = 2 if e["kind"] == "exact" else 3
    50→        conf = "high" if e["kind"] == "exact" else "low"
    51→        kind_label = "Exact" if e["kind"] == "exact" else "Near"
    52→        if cluster_size > 2:
    53→            summary = (
    54→                f"{kind_label} dupe cluster ({cluster_size} functions, "
    55→                f"{e['similarity']:.0%} similar): "
    56→                f"{a['name']} ({rel(a['file'])}:{a['line']}), "
    57→                f"{b['name']} ({rel(b['file'])}:{b['line']}), ..."
    58→            )
    59→        else:
    60→            summary = (
    61→                f"{kind_label} dupe: "
    62→                f"{a['name']} ({rel(a['file'])}:{a['line']}) <-> "
    63→                f"{b['name']} ({rel(b['file'])}:{b['line']}) [{e['similarity']:.0%}]"
    64→            )
    65→        results.append(
    66→            make_finding(
    67→                "dupes",
    68→                pair[0][0],
    69→                name,
    70→                tier=tier,
    71→                confidence=conf,
    72→                summary=summary,
    73→                detail={
    74→                    "fn_a": a,
    75→                    "fn_b": b,
    76→                    "similarity": e["similarity"],
    77→                    "kind": e["kind"],
    78→                    "cluster_size": cluster_size,
    79→                    "cluster": e.get("cluster", [a, b]),
    80→                },
    81→            )
    82→        )
    83→    suppressed = sum(
    84→        1 for e in entries if e["fn_a"]["loc"] < 10 and e["fn_b"]["loc"] < 10
    85→    )
    86→    stderr_fn(f"         {len(entries)} clusters, {suppressed} suppressed (<10 LOC)")
    87→    return results
    88→
    89→
    90→def make_single_use_findings(
    91→    entries: list[dict],
    92→    get_area,
    93→    *,
    94→    loc_range: tuple[int, int] = (50, 200),
    95→    suppress_colocated: bool = True,
    96→    skip_dir_names: set[str] | None = None,
    97→    stderr_fn,
    98→) -> list[Finding]:
    99→    """Filter and normalize single-use entries into findings.
   100→
   101→    Suppresses entries within the LOC range (they're appropriately-sized abstractions),
   102→    entries co-located with their sole importer, and entries in skip_dir_names
   103→    directories (e.g., commands/ -- CLI modules are single-use by design).
   104→    """
   105→    results = []
   106→    colocated_suppressed = 0
   107→    lo, hi = loc_range
   108→    for e in entries:
   109→        if lo <= e["loc"] <= hi:
   110→            continue
   111→        # Skip files in directories that are single-use by design (e.g., commands/)
   112→        if skip_dir_names:
   113→            parts = Path(e["file"]).parts
   114→            if any(p in skip_dir_names for p in parts):
   115→                continue
   116→        if suppress_colocated and get_area:
   117→            src_area = get_area(rel(e["file"]))
   118→            imp_area = get_area(e["sole_importer"])
   119→            if src_area == imp_area:
   120→                colocated_suppressed += 1
   121→                continue
   122→        results.append(
   123→            make_finding(
   124→                "single_use",
   125→                e["file"],
   126→                "",
   127→                tier=3,
   128→                confidence="medium",
   129→                summary=f"Single-use ({e['loc']} LOC): only imported by {e['sole_importer']}",
   130→                detail={"loc": e["loc"], "sole_importer": e["sole_importer"]},
   131→            )
   132→        )
   133→    suppressed = len(entries) - len(results)
   134→    coloc_note = f", {colocated_suppressed} co-located" if colocated_suppressed else ""
   135→    stderr_fn(
   136→        f"         single-use: {len(entries)} found, {suppressed} suppressed "
   137→        f"({lo}-{hi} LOC{coloc_note})"
   138→    )
   139→    return results
   140→
   141→
   142→def make_cycle_findings(entries: list[dict], stderr_fn) -> list[Finding]:
   143→    """Normalize import cycles into findings."""
   144→    results = []
   145→    for cy in entries:
   146→        cycle_files = [rel(f) for f in cy["files"]]
   147→        name = "::".join(cycle_files[:4])
   148→        if len(cycle_files) > 4:
   149→            name += f"::+{len(cycle_files) - 4}"
   150→        tier = 3 if cy["length"] <= 3 else 4
   151→        results.append(
   152→            make_finding(
   153→                "cycles",
   154→                cy["files"][0],
   155→                name,
   156→                tier=tier,
   157→                confidence="high",
   158→                summary=f"Import cycle ({cy['length']} files): "
   159→                + " -> ".join(cycle_files[:5])
   160→                + (f" -> +{len(cycle_files) - 5}" if len(cycle_files) > 5 else ""),
   161→                detail={"files": cycle_files, "length": cy["length"]},
   162→            )
   163→        )
   164→    if entries:
   165→        stderr_fn(f"         cycles: {len(entries)} import cycles")
   166→    return results
   167→
   168→
   169→def make_orphaned_findings(entries: list[dict], stderr_fn) -> list[Finding]:
   170→    """Normalize orphaned file entries into findings."""
   171→    results = []
   172→    for e in entries:
   173→        results.append(
   174→            make_finding(
   175→                "orphaned",
   176→                e["file"],
   177→                "",
   178→                tier=3,
   179→                confidence="medium",
   180→                summary=f"Orphaned file ({e['loc']} LOC): zero importers, not an entry point",
   181→                detail={"loc": e["loc"]},
   182→            )
   183→        )
   184→    if entries:
   185→        stderr_fn(f"         orphaned: {len(entries)} files with zero importers")
   186→    return results
   187→
   188→
   189→SMELL_TIER_MAP = {"high": Tier.QUICK_FIX, "medium": Tier.JUDGMENT, "low": Tier.JUDGMENT}
   190→
   191→
   192→def make_smell_findings(entries: list[dict], stderr_fn) -> list[Finding]:
   193→    """Group smell entries by file and assign tiers from severity.
   194→
   195→    Input: list of smell dicts from detect_smells, each with id/label/severity/matches.
   196→    Output: findings grouped per (file, smell_id).
   197→    """

   199→    for e in entries:

    26→def _normalize_file_path(value: object) -> str | None:
    27→    """Normalize/validate candidate file paths for batch payloads."""
    28→    if not isinstance(value, str):
    29→        return None
    30→    text = value.strip().strip(",'\"")
    31→    if not text or text in {".", ".."}:
    32→        return None
    33→    if text.endswith("/"):
    34→        return None
    35→
    36→    basename = Path(text).name
    37→    if not basename:
    38→        return None
    39→    if "." not in basename and basename.lower() not in _EXTENSIONLESS_FILENAMES:
    40→        return None
    41→    return text
    42→
    43→
    44→def _collect_unique_files(
    45→    sources: list[list[dict]],
    46→    key: str = "file",
    47→    *,
    48→    max_files: int | None = None,
    49→) -> list[str]:
    50→    """Collect unique file paths from multiple source lists."""
    51→    seen: set[str] = set()
    52→    out: list[str] = []
    53→    for src in sources:
    54→        for item in src:
    55→            f = _normalize_file_path(item.get(key, ""))
    56→            if f and f not in seen:
    57→                seen.add(f)
    58→                out.append(f)
    59→                if max_files is not None and len(out) >= max_files:
    60→                    return out
    61→    return out
    62→
    63→
    64→def _existing_repo_files(
    65→    repo_root: Path | None,
    66→    candidates: tuple[str, ...],
    67→) -> list[str]:
    68→    """Return repository-relative paths for candidate files that exist."""
    69→    if repo_root is None:
    70→        return []
    71→    out: list[str] = []
    72→    for candidate in candidates:
    73→        if (repo_root / candidate).is_file():
    74→            out.append(candidate)
    75→    return out
    76→
    77→
    78→def _collect_files_from_batches(
    79→    batches: list[dict], *, max_files: int | None = None
    80→) -> list[str]:
    81→    """Collect unique file paths across batch payloads (preserving order)."""
    82→    seen: set[str] = set()
    83→    out: list[str] = []
    84→    for batch in batches:
    85→        for filepath in batch.get("files_to_read", []):
    86→            normalized = _normalize_file_path(filepath)
    87→            if not normalized:
    88→                continue
    89→            if normalized in seen:
    90→                continue
    91→            seen.add(normalized)
    92→            out.append(normalized)
    93→            if max_files is not None and len(out) >= max_files:
    94→                return out
    95→    return out

    98→def _representative_files_for_directory(
    99→    ctx: HolisticContext,
   100→    directory: str,

   104→    """Map a directory-level signal to representative file paths."""
   105→    if not isinstance(directory, str) or not directory.strip():
   106→        return []
   107→
   108→    dir_key = directory.strip()
   109→    if dir_key in {".", "./"}:
   110→        normalized_dir = "."
   111→    else:
   112→        normalized_dir = f"{dir_key.rstrip('/')}/"
   113→
   114→    profiles = ctx.structure.get("directory_profiles", {})
   115→    profile = profiles.get(normalized_dir)
   116→    if not isinstance(profile, dict):

   118→
   119→    out: list[str] = []
   120→    for filename in profile.get("files", []):
   121→        if not isinstance(filename, str) or not filename:
   122→            continue
   123→        filepath = (
   124→            filename
   125→            if normalized_dir == "."
   126→            else f"{normalized_dir.rstrip('/')}/{filename}"
   127→        )
   128→        normalized = _normalize_file_path(filepath)
   129→        if not normalized or normalized in out:
   130→            continue
   131→        out.append(normalized)
   132→        if len(out) >= max_files:
   133→            break
   134→    return out

   327→    largest_dirs = sorted(
   328→        dir_profiles.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1].get("file_count", 0)
   329→    )[:3]
   330→    for dir_key, profile in largest_dirs:
   331→        for fname in profile.get("files", [])[:3]:
   332→            dir_path = dir_key.rstrip("/")
   333→            rpath = f"{dir_path}/{fname}" if dir_path != "." else fname
   334→            struct_files.append({"file": rpath})
   335→    coupling_matrix = structure.get("coupling_matrix", {})
   336→    seen_edges: set[str] = set()
   337→    for edge in coupling_matrix:
   338→        if " → " in edge:
   339→            a, b = edge.split(" → ", 1)
   340→            reverse = f"{b} → {a}"
   341→            if reverse in coupling_matrix and edge not in seen_edges:
   342→                seen_edges.add(edge)
   343→                seen_edges.add(reverse)
   344→                for d in (a, b):
   345→                    for fname in dir_profiles.get(d, {}).get("files", [])[:2]:
   346→                        dir_path = d.rstrip("/")
   347→                        rpath = f"{dir_path}/{fname}" if dir_path != "." else fname
   348→                        struct_files.append({"file": rpath})
   349→    files = _collect_unique_files([struct_files], max_files=max_files)
   350→    return {
   351→        "name": "Package Organization",
   352→        "dimensions": ["package_organization", "high_level_elegance"],
   353→        "files_to_read": files,
   354→        "why": "file placement, directory boundaries, architectural layering",
   355→    }
   356→
   357→
   358→def _batch_governance_contracts(
   359→    ctx: HolisticContext,
   360→    *,
   361→    repo_root: Path | None,
   362→    max_files: int | None = None,
   363→) -> dict:
   364→    """Batch 8: Governance & Contracts - docs/policy promises vs runtime posture."""
   365→    docs = _existing_repo_files(repo_root, _GOVERNANCE_REFERENCE_FILES)
   366→    if not docs:
   367→        return {
   368→            "name": "Governance & Contracts",
   369→            "dimensions": [
   370→                "cross_module_architecture",
   371→                "high_level_elegance",
   372→                "test_strategy",
   373→                "package_organization",
   374→            ],
   375→            "files_to_read": [],
   376→            "why": "architecture contracts, compatibility policy, docs-vs-runtime scope, and quality-gate coverage",
   377→        }
   378→    top_imported = [
   379→        {"file": filepath}
   380→        for filepath in list(ctx.architecture.get("top_imported", {}).keys())[:5]
   381→        if isinstance(filepath, str)
   382→    ]
   383→    anchor_files = _collect_unique_files(
   384→        [
   385→            top_imported,
   386→            ctx.architecture.get("god_modules", []),
   387→            ctx.coupling.get("module_level_io", []),
   388→        ],
   389→        max_files=5,
   390→    )
   391→    seen = set(docs)
   392→    files = list(docs)
   393→    for filepath in anchor_files:
   394→        if filepath in seen:
   395→            continue
   396→        seen.add(filepath)
   397→        files.append(filepath)
   398→    if max_files is not None:
   399→        files = files[:max_files]
   400→    return {
   401→        "name": "Governance & Contracts",
   402→        "dimensions": [
   403→            "cross_module_architecture",
   404→            "high_level_elegance",
   405→            "test_strategy",
   406→            "package_organization",
   407→        ],
   408→        "files_to_read": files,
   409→        "why": "architecture contracts, compatibility policy, docs-vs-runtime scope, and quality-gate coverage",
   410→    }
   411→
   412→
   413→def _ensure_holistic_context(holistic_ctx: HolisticContext | dict) -> HolisticContext:
   414→    if isinstance(holistic_ctx, HolisticContext):
   415→        return holistic_ctx
   416→    return HolisticContext.from_raw(holistic_ctx)
   417→
   418→
   419→def build_investigation_batches(
   420→    holistic_ctx: HolisticContext | dict,
   421→    lang: object,
   422→    *,
   423→    repo_root: Path | None = None,
   424→    max_files_per_batch: int | None = None,
   425→) -> list[dict]:
   426→    """Derive parallelizable investigation batches from holistic context."""
   427→    ctx = _ensure_holistic_context(holistic_ctx)
   428→    del lang  # Reserved for future language-specific batch shaping.
   429→    batches = [
   430→        _batch_arch_coupling(ctx, max_files=max_files_per_batch),
   431→        _batch_conventions_errors(ctx, max_files=max_files_per_batch),
   432→        _batch_abstractions_deps(ctx, max_files=max_files_per_batch),
   433→        _batch_testing_api(ctx, max_files=max_files_per_batch),
   434→        _batch_authorization(ctx, max_files=max_files_per_batch),
   435→        _batch_ai_debt_migrations(ctx, max_files=max_files_per_batch),
   436→        _batch_package_organization(ctx, max_files=max_files_per_batch),
   437→        _batch_governance_contracts(
   438→            ctx,
   439→            repo_root=repo_root,
   440→            max_files=max_files_per_batch,
   441→        ),
   442→    ]
   443→    return [batch for batch in batches if batch["files_to_read"]]
   444→
   445→
   446→def filter_batches_to_dimensions(
   447→    batches: list[dict],
   448→    dimensions: list[str],
   449→    *,
   450→    fallback_max_files: int | None = 80,
   451→) -> list[dict]:
   452→    """Keep only dimensions explicitly active for this holistic review run.
   453→
   454→    If selected dimensions are not represented by any batch mapping, append a
   455→    fallback batch over representative files so scoped runs still get guidance.
   456→    """
   457→    selected = [d for d in dimensions if isinstance(d, str) and d]
   458→    if not selected:
   459→        return []
   460→    selected_set = set(selected)
   461→    filtered: list[dict] = []
   462→    covered: set[str] = set()
   463→    for batch in batches:
   464→        batch_dims = [dim for dim in batch.get("dimensions", []) if dim in selected_set]
   465→        if not batch_dims:
   466→            continue
   467→        filtered.append({**batch, "dimensions": batch_dims})
   468→        covered.update(batch_dims)
   469→
   470→    missing = [dim for dim in selected if dim not in covered]
   471→    if not missing:
   472→        return filtered
   473→
   474→    # Keep fallback batches tractable; giant sweeps are expensive and often
   475→    # unnecessary when dimensions are already explicitly scoped.
   476→    max_files = fallback_max_files if isinstance(fallback_max_files, int) else None
   477→    if isinstance(max_files, int) and max_files <= 0:
   478→        max_files = None
   479→    fallback_files = _collect_files_from_batches(filtered or batches, max_files=max_files)
   480→    if not fallback_files:
   481→        return filtered
   482→
   483→    filtered.append(
   484→        {
   485→            "name": "Cross-cutting Sweep",
   486→            "dimensions": missing,
   487→            "files_to_read": fallback_files,
   488→            "why": "selected dimensions had no direct batch mapping; review representative cross-cutting files",
   489→        }
   490→    )
   491→    return filtered
   492→
   493→
   494→def batch_concerns(
   495→    concerns: list,
   496→    *,
   497→    max_files: int | None = None,
   498→) -> dict | None:
   499→    """Build investigation batch from mechanical concern signals.
   500→
   501→    *concerns* should be a list of Concern dataclass instances from
   502→    ``desloppify.engine.concerns``.
   503→    """
   504→    if not concerns:
   505→        return None
   506→    types = sorted({c.type for c in concerns if c.type})
   507→    why_parts = ["mechanical detectors identified structural patterns needing judgment"]
   508→    if types:
   509→        why_parts.append(f"concern types: {', '.join(types)}")
   510→    files: list[str] = []
   511→    seen: set[str] = set()
   512→    for concern in concerns:
   513→        candidate = _normalize_file_path(getattr(concern, "file", ""))
   514→        if not candidate or candidate in seen:
   515→            continue
   516→        seen.add(candidate)
   517→        files.append(candidate)
   518→
   519→    total_candidate_files = len(files)
   520→    if (
   521→        max_files is not None
   522→        and isinstance(max_files, int)
   523→        and max_files > 0
   524→        and total_candidate_files > max_files
   525→    ):
   526→        files = files[:max_files]
   527→        why_parts.append(
   528→            f"truncated to {max_files} files from {total_candidate_files} candidates"
   529→        )
   530→
   531→    return {
   532→        "name": "Design coherence — Mechanical Concern Signals",
   533→        "dimensions": ["design_coherence"],
   534→        "files_to_read": files,
   535→        "why": "; ".join(why_parts),
   536→        "total_candidate_files": total_candidate_files,
   537→    }
   538→
   539→
   540→__all__ = ["batch_concerns", "build_investigation_batches", "filter_batches_to_dimensions"]
   541→

   243→    finally:

### 1. **BATCH CONSTRUCTION & DIMENSION MAPPING** (`prepare_batches.py`)

#### Data Structure:
Each batch is a `dict` with this contract:
```python
{
    "name": str,                    # Human-readable batch title
    "dimensions": list[str],        # Which dimension(s) this batch addresses
    "files_to_read": list[str],     # Relative paths (normalized via _normalize_file_path)
    "why": str,                     # Explanation of why these files were selected
}
```

#### The 8 Standard Batches (lines 429-442):
1. **Architecture & Coupling** → dimensions: `["cross_module_architecture", "high_level_elegance"]`
   - Source: god_modules, module_level_io (import-time side effects)
   
2. **Conventions & Errors** → dimensions: `["convention_outlier", "error_consistency", "mid_level_elegance"]`
   - Source: sibling_behavior outliers, mixed error strategies by directory
   
3. **Abstractions & Dependencies** → dimensions: `["abstraction_fitness", "dependency_health", "mid_level_elegance", "low_level_elegance"]`
   - Source: util files, pass-through wrappers, indirection hotspots, param bags, interfaces, delegation-heavy classes, facade modules, type violations, cycles
   
4. **Testing & API** → dimensions: `["test_strategy", "api_surface_coherence", "mid_level_elegance"]`
   - Source: critical untested paths, sync/async mix
   
5. **Authorization** → dimensions: `["authorization_consistency", "mid_level_elegance"]`
   - Source: route auth gaps, service role usage
   
6. **AI Debt & Migrations** → dimensions: `["ai_generated_debt", "incomplete_migration", "low_level_elegance"]`
   - Source: deprecated markers, migration TODOs
   
7. **Package Organization** → dimensions: `["package_organization", "high_level_elegance"]`
   - Source: root_files (peripheral role), largest directories, bidirectional coupling
   
8. **Governance & Contracts** → dimensions: `["cross_module_architecture", "high_level_elegance", "test_strategy", "package_organization"]`
   - Source: reference docs (README, pyproject.toml, etc.), top imported files, god modules

#### Seed File Selection Pattern:
- Files are collected from HolisticContext sections via `_collect_unique_files()` (line 44-61)
- Each batch calls `_collect_unique_files()` on multiple signal lists from context sections
- Files are normalized by `_normalize_file_path()` which enforces:
  - Must have a file extension OR be in `_EXTENSIONLESS_FILENAMES` set
  - No trailing slashes, no ".", "..", empty strings
  - Returns `None` for invalid paths, deduplicates automatically
- Maximum files capped per batch via `max_files` parameter

---

### 2. **DIMENSION DEFINITIONS** (`dimensions.json`)

#### Structure:
```json
{
  "default_dimensions": [list of 20 dimensions],
  "dimension_prompts": {
    "dimension_name": {
      "description": "1-line summary",
      "look_for": ["pattern 1", "pattern 2", ...],
      "skip": ["exception 1", "exception 2", ...],
      "meta": {
        "display_name": "...",
        "weight": 10.0,
        "reset_on_scan": true
      }  // optional
    }
  },
  "system_prompt": "..."
}
```

#### Key Dimensions (with look_for/skip patterns):
- **naming_quality**: Generic verbs (process, handle), name/behavior mismatch, vocabulary drift
- **logic_clarity**: Dead code, always-true conditions, redundant checks, async without await
- **type_safety**: Return type divergence, union types that could narrow, missing annotations
- **contract_coherence**: Return lies, docstring/signature mismatch, hidden side effects
- **error_consistency**: Mixed strategies (throw vs null vs Result), lost context, silent swallowing
- **abstraction_fitness**: Pass-through wrappers, util dumping grounds, leaky abstractions, wide param bags
- **ai_generated_debt**: Restating comments, nosy logging, defensive overengineering, boilerplate
- **high_level_elegance**: Clear decomposition, coherent ownership, domain-aligned structure
- **mid_level_elegance**: Explicit handoffs, minimal data translation, predictable error propagation
- **low_level_elegance**: Direct control flow, bounded mutations, balanced extraction
- **cross_module_architecture**: Layer violations, cycles, hub modules, import-time side effects
- **initialization_coupling**: Boot-order deps, module-level code, global singletons
- **convention_outlier**: Naming drift, inconsistent file org, mixed export patterns
- **dependency_health**: Multiple libs for same purpose, heavy deps for light use, cycles, unused
- **test_strategy**: Untested critical paths, test-production coupling, snapshot overuse
- **api_surface_coherence**: Inconsistent shapes, mixed sync/async, overloaded interfaces
- **authorization_consistency**: Missing auth on sibling endpoints, magic literals, mixed trust boundaries
- **incomplete_migration**: Old+new API coexistence, deprecated-but-called, stale shims
- **package_organization**: Straggler roots, import-affinity mismatch, coupling-direction failures
- **design_coherence**: Functions doing too many things, parameter lists that should be objects, deep nesting

**Assessment Scale** (0-100, one decimal):
- 100: Exemplary, no material issues
- 90: Strong, minor questionable choices
- 80: Solid with repeated minor issues or one moderate
- 70: Mixed quality, multiple moderate issues
- 60: Significant quality drag
- 40: Poor, systemic problems
- 20: Severely problematic

---

### 3. **HOLISTIC CONTEXT SECTIONS** (`context_holistic/orchestrator.py`, `models.py`)

#### HolisticContext Data Model (models.py, lines 135-208):

13 named sections, each a `SectionPayload` (MutableMapping wrapper):

```python
HolisticContext(
    architecture: dict,           # god_modules, top_imported
    coupling: dict,               # module_level_io (import-time side effects)
    conventions: dict,            # naming_by_directory, sibling_behavior
    errors: dict,                 # strategy_by_directory
    abstractions: dict,           # util_files, pass_through_wrappers, one_impl_interfaces,
                                  # indirection_hotspots, wide_param_bags, delegation_heavy_classes,
                                  # facade_modules, typed_dict_violations, sub_axes (6 sub-scores)
    dependencies: dict,           # existing_cycles, cycle_summaries
    testing: dict,                # critical_untested, total_files
    api_surface: dict,            # sync_async_mix (language-specific)
    structure: dict,              # root_files, directory_profiles, coupling_matrix
    codebase_stats: dict,         # total_files, total_loc
    authorization: dict,          # route_auth_coverage, service_role_usage (optional)
    ai_debt_signals: dict,        # file_signals, markers (optional)
    migration_signals: dict,      # deprecated_markers, migration_todos (optional)
)
```

#### How Build Pipeline Works (orchestrator.py, lines 48-104):

1. **File Selection** (line 55):
   - Calls `select_holistic_files()` → gets file list from `lang.file_finder(path)` if available
   - Filters out EXCLUDED_ZONE_VALUES zones (test, generated, vendor, etc.)

2. **Cache Management** (lines 57-64):
   - Enables file cache if not already enabled (opt-in per section builders)
   - Caches file contents to avoid redundant reads during all section building

3. **Section Building** (lines 73-100):
   - `_architecture_context()`: from lang.dep_graph
   - `_coupling_context()`: scans first 50 lines for module-level I/O patterns
   - `_naming_conventions_context()`: extracts snake_case/camelCase/PascalCase by directory
   - `_sibling_behavior_context()`: finds import pattern outliers in sibling files
   - `_error_strategy_context()`: counts error patterns by directory (from `_ERROR_PATTERNS`)
   - `_abstractions_context()`: runs regex + AST analysis on all files (budget.py, lines 358-578)
   - `_dependencies_context()`: extracts cycle findings from state
   - `_testing_context()`: finds untested high-importer files from state
   - `_api_surface_context()`: calls `lang.review_api_surface_fn(file_contents)` if available
   - `compute_structure_context()`: directory/coupling analysis
   - `gather_auth_context()`: checks for auth patterns (if language-specific)
   - `gather_ai_debt_signals()`: scans for AI-generated patterns
   - `gather_migration_signals()`: finds deprecated markers and TODOs

4. **Normalization** (line 103):
   - Coerces all sections to `SectionPayload` instances with strict schema validation

---

### 4. **BUDGET.PY: SUB-AXIS SCORING** (`budget.py`, lines 505-563)

#### The Scoring System (6 sub-axes within abstractions section):

```python
"sub_axes": {
    "abstraction_leverage": 100 - (wrapper_rate * 120) - (len(util_files) * 1.5),
    "indirection_cost": 100 - (sum(chain_depths) * 2.5) - (sum(wide_funcs) * 2.0),
    "interface_honesty": 100 - (len(one_impl_interfaces) * 8),
    "delegation_density": 100 - (avg_delegation_ratio * 80) - (len(delegation_classes) * 5),
    "definition_directness": 100 - (len(facade_modules) * 8) - (avg_facade_ratio * 50),
    "type_discipline": 100 - (len(typed_dict_violation_files) * 6) - (total_violations * 1.5),
}
```

Each is clamped to [0, 100] via `_score_clamped()`.

**Metrics collected per file:**
- **wrappers**: Regex-based + AST-based passthrough function pairs
- **util_files**: Detected by filename (utils, helpers, util, helper, common, misc)
- **indirection_hotspots**: 3+ chained attribute accesses OR 6+ chain matches
- **wide_param_bags**: Functions with 7+ parameters OR 10+ config/context mentions
- **delegation_heavy_classes**: Classes where 50%+ of methods delegate to single inner object
- **facade_modules**: 70%+ of public names are re-exports with <3 defined symbols
- **typed_dict_violations**: Usage of .get()/.setdefault()/.pop() on TypedDict-typed vars

---

### 5. **HOW MECHANICAL FINDINGS WIRE IN: CONCERN SYSTEM** (`concerns.py`)

#### The Concern Dataclass (lines 21-31):
```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Concern:
    type: str                      # e.g., "mixed_responsibilities", "structural_complexity"
    file: str                      # Primary file (relative path)
    summary: str                   # Human-readable 1-liner
    evidence: tuple[str, ...]      # Supporting data points
    question: str                  # Specific LLM evaluation question
    fingerprint: str               # Stable hash for dismissal tracking
    source_findings: tuple[str, ...] # Finding IDs that triggered this
```

#### Generation Pipeline (lines 433-454):
1. **_file_concerns()** (lines 307-358):
   - Groups findings by file, filters to JUDGMENT_DETECTORS
   - Flags if 2+ judgment detectors OR 1 with elevated signals:
     - `max_params >= 8`, `max_nesting >= 6`, `loc >= 300` (monster function)
   - Extracts signals: max_params, max_nesting, loc, function_count, monster_loc, monster_funcs
   - Classifies as: mixed_responsibilities, structural_complexity, duplication_design, coupling_design, interface_design, design_concern
   - Checks dismissals via fingerprint

2. **_cross_file_patterns()** (lines 361-427):
   - Groups files by detector combo (judgment detectors only)
   - Flags if 3+ files share same detector combo
   - Classifies as: systemic_pattern

#### Integration into Batches (`prepare.py`, lines 268-279):
```python
concerns = generate_concerns(state, lang_name=lang.name)
concerns_batch = _batch_concerns(
    concerns,
    max_files=resolved_options.max_files_per_batch,
)
if concerns_batch:
    batches.append(concerns_batch)
```

#### The batch_concerns() Function (`prepare_batches.py`, lines 494-538):
- Converts Concern list to single investigation batch
- Maps to dimension: `["design_coherence"]`
- Normalizes file paths via `_normalize_file_path()`
- Adds `total_candidate_files` count for diagnostics
- Truncates to `max_files` if needed, reports in "why"

### 6. **EXTENSION POINTS & PATTERNS**

#### How to Add New Signal Feeds:

**Pattern 1: Add to existing HolisticContext section**
- Edit `budget.py` or one of the selector functions in `selection.py`
- Compute signals, add to dict
- No schema change needed (SectionPayload accepts any dict)
- Example: Add new key to `abstractions["summary"]` or `structure`

**Pattern 2: Create new optional HolisticContext section**
- Add field to `HolisticContext` dataclass in `models.py` (lines 135-168)
- Add to `_SECTION_NAMES` tuple
- Conditionally populate in `orchestrator.py` (like `authorization`, `ai_debt_signals`, `migration_signals`)
- Usage: Reference in batch builders like `_batch_auth()` or `_batch_ai_debt_migrations()`

**Pattern 3: Wire mechanical findings as Concern signals (EXISTING PATTERN)**
- Modify `_file_concerns()` or `_cross_file_patterns()` in `concerns.py`
- Add new detector types to JUDGMENT_DETECTORS in registry.py
- Extract signals into ConcernSignals TypedDict
- Update classification logic in `_classify()`
- Update evidence/question builders
- Concerns automatically become "design_coherence" batch via `batch_concerns()`

**Pattern 4: Create new batch in prepare_batches.py**
- Write `_batch_xxx()` function following the pattern:
  ```python
  def _batch_xxx(ctx: HolisticContext, *, max_files: int | None = None) -> dict:
      files = _collect_unique_files([...sources...], max_files=max_files)
      return {
          "name": "...",
          "dimensions": ["dim1", "dim2"],
          "files_to_read": files,
          "why": "..."
      }
  ```
- Add to `batches` list in `build_investigation_batches()` (line 429+)
- Files must pass `_normalize_file_path()` validation

**Pattern 5: Language-specific API surface signals**
- Implement `lang.review_api_surface_fn(file_contents: dict[str, str]) -> dict`
- Returns dict with keys like `"sync_async_mix": [filepath, ...]`
- Called automatically in `_api_surface_context()`, results in batch via `_batch_testing_api()`

---

### 7. **KEY STRUCTURAL INVARIANTS**

1. **File Path Normalization**: All file paths in batches MUST be repo-relative and pass `_normalize_file_path()`:
   - No trailing slashes
   - No ".", ".."
   - Has extension OR is in `_EXTENSIONLESS_FILENAMES`
   - Empty strings and non-strings become None

2. **Dimension-Batch Mapping**: Not 1:1. Batch can address 1-4 dimensions. A dimension can appear in multiple batches. `filter_batches_to_dimensions()` filters to selected dims, adds "Cross-cutting Sweep" fallback if any dimension has no direct batch.

3. **Section Coercion**: HolisticContext.normalize_sections(strict=True) converts all section values to SectionPayload instances. Mapping interface allows dict-like access.

4. **Dismissal Tracking**: Concerns have stable fingerprints (SHA256 of type/file/detector combo). Dismissals live in state['concern_dismissals'][fingerprint] and block concern generation if source_finding_ids unchanged.

5. **Sub-axis Scoring**: Abstractions section includes 6 sub-axis scores computed via weighted formulas. All sub-axes clamped to [0, 100].

6. **Optional Sections**: authorization, ai_debt_signals, migration_signals are conditionally populated only if non-empty. No schema error if omitted.

---

### 8. **DATA FLOW DIAGRAM**

```
[lang.file_finder() or explicit files]
           ↓
[select_holistic_files] → filter by EXCLUDED_ZONE_VALUES
           ↓
[_read_file_contents] → cache enabled
           ↓
[13 section builders in parallel]
  ├─ _architecture_context (dep_graph)
  ├─ _coupling_context (module I/O scan)
  ├─ _naming_conventions_context (regex on function names)
  ├─ _sibling_behavior_context (import patterns)
  ├─ _error_strategy_context (error patterns by dir)
  ├─ _abstractions_context (regex + AST analysis) → 6 sub-axes
  ├─ _dependencies_context (cycle findings from state)
  ├─ _testing_context (untested high-importers from state)
  ├─ _api_surface_context (lang.review_api_surface_fn)
  ├─ compute_structure_context (dir/coupling profiles)
  ├─ gather_auth_context (auth patterns, optional)
  ├─ gather_ai_debt_signals (AI markers, optional)
  └─ gather_migration_signals (deprecated/migration TODOs, optional)
           ↓
[HolisticContext instance]
           ↓
[build_investigation_batches]
  ├─ 8 fixed batches from standard builders
  ├─ generate_concerns (from state findings)
  └─ batch_concerns → "design_coherence" batch (optional)
           ↓
[filter_batches_to_dimensions] → keep only requested dims
           ↓
[investigation_batches list]
           ↓
[LLM review over batches with dimension_prompts]
           ↓
[Assessment scores + Findings per dimension]
```

---

### SUMMARY FOR WIRING MECHANICAL FINDINGS

To integrate a new class of mechanical findings (e.g., "mutation hotspots", "circular imports", "god objects"):

1. **Compute signals** in `budget.py` or `selection.py` section builder
2. **Add to HolisticContext** as new key in existing section OR new optional section
3. **Create batch builder** `_batch_xxx()` in `prepare_batches.py` that reads from context
4. **Register in build_investigation_batches()** (line 429+)
5. **OR** wire via Concern generator:
   - Add detector type to JUDGMENT_DETECTORS
   - Modify `_file_concerns()` classification logic
   - Auto-surfaces as "design_coherence" batch
6. **Validate** files pass `_normalize_file_path()` and dimensions exist in `dimensions.json`

The system is **explicitly designed for compositional signal mixing** — each section is independent, batches derive from context sections, and concerns are computed on-demand from state findings without persistence overhead.

## Finding Dict Base Schema (All Detectors)

All detectors produce entries that are normalized into the canonical `Finding` TypedDict (from `schema.py:45–66`):

```python
class Finding(TypedDict):
    id: str                                    # unique identifier
    detector: str                              # detector name
    file: str                                  # file path
    tier: int                                  # 1–4 (1=quick_fix, 4=judgment)
    confidence: str                            # "high", "medium", "low"
    summary: str                               # human-readable summary
    detail: dict[str, Any]                     # detector-specific metadata
    status: FindingStatus                      # "open", "fixed", "auto_resolved", "wontfix", "false_positive"
    note: str | None
    first_seen: str                            # ISO timestamp
    last_seen: str                             # ISO timestamp
    resolved_at: str | None
    reopen_count: int
    suppressed: bool (optional)
    zone: str (optional)                       # production/test/config/generated/script/vendor
    lang: str (optional)                       # language plugin name
```

## Holistic Context Integration Summary

**Only 2 detectors currently feed into holistic context:**

1. **cycles** → `orchestrator.py:_build_holistic_context_inner()` calls `selection.py:_dependencies_context()` which extracts open cycle findings and counts them
2. **test_coverage** → `orchestrator.py` calls `selection.py:_testing_context()` which identifies files with coverage issues and finds "critical untested" files (those imported by ≥3 other files)

**Not used in holistic context:**
- complexity, large, flat_dirs, orphaned, naming, single_use, coupling, dupes
- All Python-specific detectors (smells, mutable_state, responsibility_cohesion, coupling_contracts, private_imports, unused, uncalled_functions, dict_keys)
- security, review_coverage

This means **17 of 19 detector categories are isolated from holistic review context** — they feed into the mechanical dimension scoring but don't influence the cross-cutting contextual understanding built for review prompts.

## Context Architecture Overview

### 1. Core Context Models (`_context/models.py`)

**Two main typed contracts:**

- **`HolisticContext`** (13 sections): Codebase-wide signals built during review prep
  - `architecture`, `coupling`, `conventions`, `errors`, `abstractions`, `dependencies`, `testing`, `api_surface`, `structure`, `codebase_stats`, `authorization`, `ai_debt_signals`, `migration_signals`
  
- **`ReviewContext`** (11 sections): Per-file evaluation context (not holistic)
  - `naming_vocabulary`, `error_conventions`, `module_patterns`, `import_graph_summary`, etc.

- **`SectionPayload`**: MutableMapping wrapper for each section (name + dict)

Each section is coerced to a normalized `SectionPayload` via `normalize_sections(strict=True)`, which validates that:
- Non-empty values must be Mapping-like (dict, SectionPayload, or Mapping)
- Values are converted to dicts via `to_dict()`
- Strict mode raises on non-Mapping values

### 2. Orchestrator Pipeline (`orchestrator.py`)

**`build_holistic_context_model(path, lang, state, files=None)`** is the entry point:

```
1. Select holistic files (filters by zone, excludes test/config/generated/vendor)
2. Enable file cache for scan efficiency
3. Read all file contents into memory dict: {filepath: content_str}
4. Build each context section:
   - From file_contents: _architecture, _coupling, _conventions, _errors, _abstractions, _api_surface, _codebase_stats, structure
   - From state: _dependencies, _testing (reads "test_coverage" findings), _naming_conventions
   - From signal modules: gather_auth_context, gather_ai_debt_signals, gather_migration_signals
5. Normalize all sections (strict=True)
6. Return fully typed HolisticContext dataclass
```

**Access to data:**
- Has **full file contents** (all files passed through `_read_file_contents`)
- Has **state dict** with scan findings (accessed in `_dependencies_context`, `_testing_context`)
- Uses **lang.dep_graph** (import graph) for architecture/testing analysis
- Uses **lang.zone_map** for per-file zone classification (production/test/config/etc)

### 3. Context Section Builders

The pattern for each section builder (in `selection.py` and `budget.py`):

1. **Input**: `file_contents: dict[str, str]` (all files), `state: dict` (findings), `lang` object
2. **Processing**: Regex + heuristics on file text, cross-file analysis (e.g., Counter-based patterns)
3. **Output**: Dict with structure matching section contract
4. **Example** (`_testing_context`):
   ```python
   # Read state findings
   tc_findings = {
       finding["file"]
       for finding in state.get("findings", {}).values()
       if finding.get("detector") == "test_coverage" and finding.get("status") == "open"
   }
   # Cross-reference with dep_graph to find critical untested
   critical_untested = [
       {...file, importers: count}
       for filepath in tc_findings
       if importer_count(lang.dep_graph.get(filepath)) >= 3
   ]
   ```

### 4. Context Signal Modules (`context_signals/`)

**Standalone generator functions** for cross-cutting signals:

- **`gather_ai_debt_signals(file_contents, rel_fn)`** → dict with:
  - `file_signals`: {file: {comment_ratio, log_density, guard_density}}
  - `codebase_avg_comment_ratio`: float
  - Top 20 files by signal count
  
- **`gather_auth_context(file_contents, rel_fn)`** → dict with:
  - `route_auth_coverage`: {file: {handlers, with_auth, without_auth}}
  - `rls_coverage`: {with_rls, without_rls} tables
  - `service_role_usage`: [files]
  - Nested patterns: auth_patterns, auth_guard_patterns, auth_usage_patterns
  
- **`gather_migration_signals(file_contents, lang, rel_fn)`** → dict with:
  - `deprecated_markers`: {total, files: {file: count}}
  - `migration_todos`: [{file, text}, ...]
  - `pattern_pairs`: [{name, old_count, new_count}, ...] (language-specific old→new pattern matching)
  - `mixed_extensions`: [stems] (files with both .ts and .js, etc)

**Pattern**: Each takes `rel_fn: Callable[[str], str]` to normalize paths for output. Scans all files, emits only non-empty results.

### 5. Batch Construction (`prepare_batches.py`)

**Core function**: `build_investigation_batches(holistic_ctx, lang, repo_root=None, max_files_per_batch=None)`

Returns 8 fixed batches (if they have files):

| Batch | Source Sections | Purpose |
|-------|-----------------|---------|
| Architecture & Coupling | `architecture.god_modules`, `coupling.module_level_io` | Top 20 by signal |
| Conventions & Errors | `conventions.sibling_behavior` outliers, `errors.strategy_by_directory` mixed dirs | Outlier detection |
| Abstractions & Dependencies | `abstractions.*`, `dependencies.cycle_summaries` | Util files, wrappers, delegation, facades, TypedDict violations, cycles |
| Testing & API | `testing.critical_untested`, `api_surface.sync_async_mix` | Coverage + API shape |
| Authorization | `authorization.route_auth_coverage` (where `without_auth>0`), `service_role_usage` | Auth gaps |
| AI Debt & Migrations | `ai_debt_signals.file_signals`, `migration_signals.deprecated_markers` + `.migration_todos` | Deprecated + migration TODOs |
| Package Organization | `structure.root_files` (role=peripheral), largest directories, coupling reciprocal edges | File placement |
| Governance & Contracts | Governance docs + top imported/god modules | Docs vs runtime |

**Seed file selection**:
```python
def _collect_unique_files(sources: list[list[dict]], key: str = "file", max_files=None):
    # Collects {item[key] for item in source if normalized(item[key]) is valid}
    # Stops at max_files, preserves order
```

Each batch dict: `{name, dimensions: [str, ...], files_to_read: [path, ...], why: str}`

### 6. Integration into Review Prepare (`prepare.py`)

**`prepare_holistic_review(path, lang, state, options=...)`**:

```python
1. Construct HolisticContext via build_holistic_context(path, lang, state, files=all_files)
2. Also build per-file ReviewContext (for reference)
3. Load dimension prompts, determine active dimensions
4. Call build_investigation_batches(context, lang, repo_root=path, ...)
5. [OPTIONAL] Append design_coherence batch from mechanical concerns via generate_concerns(state, lang_name)
6. Filter batches to only active dimensions
7. [OPTIONAL] Append retrospective historical issue focus to each batch
```

**Output payload** (written to `.desloppify/query.json`):
```json
{
  "command": "review",
  "mode": "holistic",
  "language": "python",
  "dimensions": ["cross_module_architecture", ...],
  "holistic_context": {full HolisticContext.to_dict()},
  "review_context": {...},
  "investigation_batches": [
    {"name": "Batch 1", "dimensions": [...], "files_to_read": [...], "why": "..."}
  ]
}
```

---

## How Batch Context is Surfaced to Agents (`batch_prompt_template.py`)

**`render_batch_prompt(repo_root, packet_path, batch_index, batch)`** generates:

1. **Static metadata**: batch name, index, dimensions, files_to_read
2. **Holistic context references** in task requirements (lines 84–106):
   - **package_organization**: "ground in `holistic_context.structure` (root_files fan_in/fan_out, directory_profiles, coupling_matrix)"
   - **abstraction_fitness**: "use `holistic_context.abstractions` (delegation_heavy_classes, facade_modules, typed_dict_violations)"
3. **NOT hardcoded per-file**: Generic task description tells agent to read files + use holistic context as reference
4. **Holistic context is delivered separately** in the query.json packet, not in the prompt text itself

**Key insight**: The prompt doesn't inline holistic context data—it just directs agents to consult the `holistic_context` object they receive from the packet.

## Key Architectural Answers

**Q: Does orchestrator have access to scan state?**  
**A**: Yes. `build_holistic_context_model(path, lang, state, files=None)` receives `state: dict` and passes it to section builders like `_dependencies_context(state)`, `_testing_context(lang, state, ...)`. Sections read findings via `state.get("findings", {}).values()`.

**Q: How to add a new section?**  
**A**: 
1. Create a builder function returning `dict[str, object]`
2. Add field to `HolisticContext` dataclass (or reuse existing section)
3. Update `_SECTION_NAMES` tuple
4. Call builder in `_build_holistic_context_inner`, assign to context
5. Create batch builder in `prepare_batches.py` that consumes the new section
6. Add batch to `build_investigation_batches` list

**Q: How is context surfaced in prompts?**  
**A**: Via the `.desloppify/query.json` packet. The prompt template references holistic context by name (e.g., "use `holistic_context.structure`") but doesn't inline it. The packet delivers both prompt + full context dict separately, and agents receive both.

**Q: What's SectionPayload?**  
**A**: A `MutableMapping[str, Any]` wrapper with:
- `name: str` (section identifier)
- `_data: dict[str, Any]` (content)
- Methods: `__getitem__`, `__setitem__`, `__iter__`, `to_dict()`, `__eq__`
Allows typed coercion + consistent section interface.

**Q: Pattern for reading state findings?**  
**A**: 
```python
open_findings = [
    f for f in state.get("findings", {}).values()
    if f.get("detector") == "test_coverage" and f.get("status") == "open"
]
```
Findings are a dict with keys: `detector`, `file`, `status`, `summary`, `confidence`, etc.

**Q: Seed file selection per batch?**  
**A**: 
- Signal sections emit `{file: {...metrics...}}` or lists of dicts with `"file"` key
- `_collect_unique_files([signal1, signal2, ...], key="file", max_files=N)` extracts + deduplicates
- Batches preserve order, stop at max_files
- Files validated via `_normalize_file_path()` (must have extension + valid basename)

You are designing a major architectural enhancement for desloppify, a Python codebase health tool. I need you to think through this design carefully and produce a detailed plan.

## Background

Desloppify has two analysis layers:
1. **Mechanical detectors** — deterministic analysis (AST, regex, heuristics) that produce per-file findings stored in state
2. **Subjective review** — LLM-based investigation batches that evaluate code across 20 dimensions

The problem: **17 of 19 mechanical detectors produce findings that sit in state but are NOT fed into the holistic context that guides the LLM reviewer.** Only `cycles` and `test_coverage` currently bridge from mechanical → subjective.

## Current Architecture

### Mechanical Detectors (what they produce)
- `large` — files > 500 LOC, produces {file, loc}
- `complexity` — weighted complexity score, produces {file, loc, score, complexity_signals: ["22 params", "nesting depth 5"]}
- `responsibility_cohesion` — disconnected function clusters, produces {file, loc, function_count, component_count, component_sizes, family_count, families}
- `flat_dirs` — directory organization issues, produces {directory, file_count, child_dir_count, combined_score, kind}
- `smells` — grouped by smell_id per file, produces {smell_id, severity, count, lines}. Key subtypes: monster_function, deferred_import, broad_except, silent_except, empty_except, optional_param_sprawl, nested_closure, high_cyclomatic_complexity, swallowed_error, lru_cache_mutable, mutable_ref_hack, annotation_quality
- `mutable_state` — module-level mutable names with mutation sites, produces {file, name, line, mutation_count, mutation_lines}
- `coupling` — boundary violations, produces {file, target, direction, tool}
- `single_use` — files imported by exactly one other, produces {file, loc, sole_importer}
- `orphaned` — dead files, produces {file, loc, import_count}
- `uncalled_functions` — dead private functions, produces {file, name, line, loc}
- `naming` — per-directory naming inconsistency, produces {directory, majority, minority, outliers}
- `dupes` — near/exact duplicate function clusters, produces {fn_a, fn_b, similarity, kind, cluster_size, cluster}
- `private_imports` — cross-boundary private symbol use, produces {file, symbol, source_file, target_file}
- `dict_keys` — schema drift / dead writes, produces {file, kind, key, line, context}
- `security` — bandit findings, produces {file, kind, severity, line, description}
- `unused` — dead imports/variables, produces {file, line, name, category}
- `review_coverage` — files lacking review, produces like test_coverage

### Current Holistic Context Sections (13 sections)
- `architecture` — god modules from dep_graph (built from file contents)
- `coupling` — module-level I/O from first 50 lines (built from file contents)
- `conventions` — naming by directory, sibling behavior (built from file contents)
- `errors` — error strategy by directory (built from file contents)
- `abstractions` — wrappers, delegation, facades, param bags, typed_dict violations + 6 sub-axis scores (built from file contents via budget.py)
- `dependencies` — cycle findings (**reads from state**)
- `testing` — critical untested files (**reads from state**)
- `api_surface` — sync/async mix (language-specific)
- `structure` — directory profiles, coupling matrix, root files
- `codebase_stats` — totals
- `authorization` — auth patterns (optional)
- `ai_debt_signals` — comment/log/guard density (optional)
- `migration_signals` — deprecated markers, TODOs (optional)

### Current 8 Investigation Batches
1. **Architecture & Coupling** → cross_module_architecture, high_level_elegance
2. **Conventions & Errors** → convention_outlier, error_consistency, mid_level_elegance
3. **Abstractions & Dependencies** → abstraction_fitness, dependency_health, mid_level_elegance, low_level_elegance
4. **Testing & API** → test_strategy, api_surface_coherence, mid_level_elegance
5. **Authorization** → authorization_consistency, mid_level_elegance
6. **AI Debt & Migrations** → ai_generated_debt, incomplete_migration, low_level_elegance
7. **Package Organization** → package_organization, high_level_elegance
8. **Governance & Contracts** → cross_module_architecture, high_level_elegance, test_strategy, package_organization

Plus an optional **concerns batch** → design_coherence (conditional, only when 2+ judgment detectors fire on same file)

### Underserved Dimensions (not primary in any batch)
- `initialization_coupling`
- `design_coherence` (only via conditional concerns)
- `naming_quality`, `logic_clarity`, `type_safety`, `contract_coherence` (per-file review only, no holistic investigation)

### Extension Points
- New section: add field to HolisticContext dataclass, add builder in orchestrator.py
- State reading: pattern exists (see _testing_context, _dependencies_context) — iterate state["findings"].values() filtered by detector/status
- New batch: add _batch_xxx() to prepare_batches.py, register in build_investigation_batches()
- Seed files: _collect_unique_files() extracts file paths from signal lists
- Prompt template: references holistic_context sections by name

## Design Requirements

1. **Every mechanical detector's findings should be available to the LLM reviewer as investigative leads**
2. **Signals should be aggregated** — not raw finding dumps. The LLM needs hotspot files, systemic patterns, and per-file evidence summaries.
3. **Existing batches should be enriched** with mechanical evidence (new seed files, richer "why")
4. **Underserved dimensions need batch coverage** (especially initialization_coupling and design_coherence)
5. **The concerns mechanism should be expanded** (currently too restrictive)
6. **Budget.py's re-analysis of file contents should be reduced** where mechanical detectors already found the same signals (e.g., budget.py regex-scans for wide params, but complexity detector already found "function with 22 params")

## What I Need

Design the complete system:

1. **Signal Clusters**: How should mechanical findings be grouped for aggregation? What are the natural investigation topics? For each cluster:
   - Which detectors feed in
   - What aggregated signal it produces (hotspot files, patterns, per-file evidence)
   - Which holistic context section it enriches
   - Which batches consume it

2. **New/Modified Batches**: Should we add new batches? Modify existing ones? For each:
   - Dimensions covered
   - Signal sources
   - Seed file strategy
   - Investigation question for the LLM

3. **Context Section Design**: How to structure the aggregated mechanical data in holistic context. Should it be:
   - New sections? (like `mechanical_signals`)
   - Expansions of existing sections?
   - Both?

4. **Concerns Mechanism**: How to expand it to be more comprehensive

5. **Prompt Template Updates**: What new evidence references to add

6. **Deduplication with budget.py**: Where does budget.py re-derive signals that mechanical detectors already found? How to consolidate?

Think carefully about the trade-offs. More batches = more LLM cost. Too much context = noise. The goal is to give the LLM the RIGHT leads to investigate ROOT CAUSES, not just surface symptoms.

Produce a detailed design document.

    44→    """Gather codebase-wide data for holistic review."""
    45→    return build_holistic_context_model(path, lang, state, files=files).to_dict()

    47→
    48→def build_holistic_context_model(
    49→    path: Path,
    50→    lang,
    51→    state: dict,
    52→    files: list[str] | None = None,
    53→) -> HolisticContext:
    54→    """Gather holistic context and return a typed context contract."""
    55→    selected_files = select_holistic_files(path, lang, files)
    56→
    57→    already_cached = is_file_cache_enabled()
    58→    if not already_cached:
    59→        enable_file_cache()
    60→    try:
    61→        return _build_holistic_context_inner(path, selected_files, lang, state)
    62→    finally:
    63→        if not already_cached:
    64→            disable_file_cache()
    65→
    66→
    67→def _build_holistic_context_inner(
    68→    path: Path, files: list[str], lang, state: dict
    69→) -> HolisticContext:
    70→    """Inner holistic context builder (runs with file cache enabled)."""
    71→    file_contents = _read_file_contents(files)
    72→
    73→    context = HolisticContext(
    74→        architecture=_architecture_context(lang, file_contents),
    75→        coupling=_coupling_context(file_contents),
    76→        conventions={
    77→            "naming_by_directory": _naming_conventions_context(file_contents),
    78→            "sibling_behavior": _sibling_behavior_context(file_contents, base_path=path),
    79→        },
    80→        errors={
    81→            "strategy_by_directory": _error_strategy_context(file_contents),
    82→        },
    83→        abstractions=_abstractions_context(file_contents),
    84→        dependencies=_dependencies_context(state),
    85→        testing=_testing_context(lang, state, file_contents),
    86→        api_surface=_api_surface_context(lang, file_contents),
    87→        structure=compute_structure_context(file_contents, lang),
    88→    )
    89→
    90→    auth_ctx = gather_auth_context(file_contents, rel_fn=rel)
    91→    if auth_ctx:
    92→        context.authorization = auth_ctx
    93→
    94→    ai_debt = gather_ai_debt_signals(file_contents, rel_fn=rel)
    95→    if ai_debt.get("file_signals"):
    96→        context.ai_debt_signals = ai_debt
    97→
    98→    migration = gather_migration_signals(file_contents, lang, rel_fn=rel)
    99→    if migration:
   100→        context.migration_signals = migration
   101→
   102→    context.codebase_stats = _codebase_stats(file_contents)
   103→    context.normalize_sections(strict=True)
   104→    return context
   105→

    33→def _count_signature_params(params_blob: str) -> int:

    39→    filtered = [part for part in parts if part not in {"self", "cls", "this"}]

    43→def _extract_type_names(blob: str) -> list[str]:

   106→def _is_delegation_stmt(stmt: ast.stmt) -> str | None:
   107→    """Return the delegate attribute name if *stmt* is a pure delegation.
   108→
   109→    Matches patterns like:
   110→    - ``return self.x.method(...)``
   111→    - ``return self.x``  (property forwarding)
   112→    - ``self.x.method(...)``  (void delegation)
   113→    """
   114→    # Unwrap Expr nodes (void calls like ``self.x.do()``)
   115→    if isinstance(stmt, ast.Expr):
   116→        value = stmt.value
   117→    elif isinstance(stmt, ast.Return) and stmt.value is not None:
   118→        value = stmt.value
   119→    else:
   120→        return None
   121→
   122→    # ``self.x.method(...)`` or ``self.x(...)``
   123→    if isinstance(value, ast.Call):
   124→        value = value.func
   125→
   126→    # Walk the attribute chain to find ``self.<attr>``
   127→    node = value
   128→    depth = 0
   129→    while isinstance(node, ast.Attribute):
   130→        node = node.value
   131→        depth += 1
   132→    if depth < 1 or not isinstance(node, ast.Name) or node.id != "self":
   133→        return None
   134→
   135→    # The first attribute after self — walk back down from the outermost
   136→    # Attribute to find the one whose .value is the Name("self") node.
   137→    first = value
   138→    while isinstance(first, ast.Attribute) and isinstance(first.value, ast.Attribute):
   139→        first = first.value
   140→    if isinstance(first, ast.Attribute) and isinstance(first.value, ast.Name):
   141→        return first.attr
   142→    return None
   143→

   145→def _find_delegation_heavy_classes(tree: ast.Module) -> list[dict]:
   146→    """Find classes where most methods delegate to a single inner object."""
   147→    results: list[dict] = []
   148→    for node in ast.walk(tree):
   149→        if not isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef):
   150→            continue
   151→
   152→        methods: list[ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef] = [
   153→            child
   154→            for child in node.body
   155→            if isinstance(child, ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef)
   156→            and child.name != "__init__"
   157→        ]
   158→        if len(methods) <= 3:
   159→            continue
   160→
   161→        # Track which methods delegate to which attribute
   162→        delegating_methods: dict[str, list[str]] = {}  # attr -> [method_names]
   163→        for method in methods:
   164→            body = _strip_docstring(list(method.body))
   165→            if len(body) != 1:
   166→                continue
   167→            attr = _is_delegation_stmt(body[0])
   168→            if attr:
   169→                delegating_methods.setdefault(attr, []).append(method.name)
   170→
   171→        if not delegating_methods:
   172→            continue
   173→
   174→        # Use the most common delegate target
   175→        top_attr = max(delegating_methods, key=lambda a: len(delegating_methods[a]))
   176→        delegate_count = len(delegating_methods[top_attr])
   177→        ratio = delegate_count / len(methods)
   178→        if ratio > 0.5:
   179→            results.append(
   180→                {
   181→                    "class_name": node.name,
   182→                    "line": node.lineno,
   183→                    "delegation_ratio": round(ratio, 2),
   184→                    "method_count": len(methods),
   185→                    "delegate_count": delegate_count,
   186→                    "delegate_target": top_attr,
   187→                    "sample_methods": delegating_methods[top_attr][:5],
   188→                }
   189→            )
   190→    return results

   193→def _find_facade_modules(tree: ast.Module, *, loc: int) -> dict | None:
   194→    """Detect modules where >70% of public names come from imports."""
   195→    import_names: set[str] = set()
   196→    defined_names: set[str] = set()
   197→
   198→    for node in ast.iter_child_nodes(tree):
   199→        if isinstance(node, ast.Import):
   200→            for alias in node.names:
   201→                name = alias.asname or alias.name.split(".")[-1]
   202→                import_names.add(name)
   203→        elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):
   204→            for alias in node.names:
   205→                if alias.name == "*":
   206→                    continue
   207→                name = alias.asname or alias.name
   208→                import_names.add(name)
   209→        elif isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef):
   210→            defined_names.add(node.name)
   211→        elif isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef):
   212→            defined_names.add(node.name)
   213→        elif isinstance(node, ast.Assign):
   214→            for target in node.targets:
   215→                if isinstance(target, ast.Name) and target.id == "__all__":
   216→                    continue
   217→                if isinstance(target, ast.Name):
   218→                    defined_names.add(target.id)
   219→
   220→    # Remove private names
   221→    public_imports = {n for n in import_names if not n.startswith("_")}
   222→    public_defs = {n for n in defined_names if not n.startswith("_")}
   223→
   224→    total_public = len(public_imports | public_defs)
   225→    if total_public < 3:
   226→        return None
   227→
   228→    # Re-exported = imported names that aren't shadowed by a local definition
   229→    re_exported = public_imports - public_defs
   230→    re_export_ratio = len(re_exported) / total_public
   231→
   232→    if re_export_ratio < 0.7 or len(public_defs) > 3:
   233→        return None
   234→
   235→    return {
   236→        "re_export_ratio": round(re_export_ratio, 2),
   237→        "defined_symbols": len(public_defs),
   238→        "re_exported_symbols": len(re_exported),
   239→        "samples": sorted(re_exported)[:5],
   240→        "loc": loc,
   241→    }
