   244→def _collect_typed_dict_defs(
   245→    tree: ast.Module, accumulator: dict[str, set[str]]
   246→) -> None:
   247→    """Collect TypedDict class definitions from a single file's AST."""
   248→    for node in ast.walk(tree):
   249→        if not isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef):
   250→            continue
   251→        is_typed_dict = any(
   252→            (isinstance(b, ast.Name) and b.id == "TypedDict")
   253→            or (isinstance(b, ast.Attribute) and b.attr == "TypedDict")
   254→            for b in node.bases
   255→        )
   256→        if not is_typed_dict:
   257→            continue
   258→        fields: set[str] = set()
   259→        for child in node.body:
   260→            if isinstance(child, ast.AnnAssign) and isinstance(child.target, ast.Name):
   261→                fields.add(child.target.id)
   262→        if fields:
   263→            accumulator[node.name] = fields
   264→
   265→
   266→_VIOLATION_METHODS = frozenset({"get", "setdefault", "pop"})
   267→
   268→
   269→def _find_typed_dict_usage_violations(
   270→    parsed_trees: dict[str, ast.Module],
   271→    typed_dicts: dict[str, set[str]],
   272→) -> list[dict]:
   273→    """Find .get()/.setdefault()/.pop() calls on TypedDict-annotated variables.
   274→
   275→    *parsed_trees* maps absolute file paths to pre-parsed ASTs (built during
   276→    the main collection loop to avoid redundant parses).
   277→
   278→    Returns a list of violation dicts with file, typed_dict_name, violation_type,
   279→    line, field (when extractable), and count.
   280→    """
   281→    if not typed_dicts:
   282→        return []
   283→
   284→    violations: list[dict] = []
   285→    for filepath, tree in parsed_trees.items():
   286→        rpath = rel(filepath)
   287→
   288→        # Collect variable names annotated with known TypedDict types
   289→        typed_vars: dict[str, str] = {}  # var_name -> TypedDict name
   290→        for node in ast.walk(tree):
   291→            if isinstance(node, ast.AnnAssign) and isinstance(node.target, ast.Name):
   292→                ann = node.annotation
   293→                ann_name = None
   294→                if isinstance(ann, ast.Name):
   295→                    ann_name = ann.id
   296→                elif isinstance(ann, ast.Attribute):
   297→                    ann_name = ann.attr
   298→                if ann_name in typed_dicts:
   299→                    typed_vars[node.target.id] = ann_name
   300→            # Also check function param annotations
   301→            if isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef):
   302→                for arg in node.args.args + node.args.kwonlyargs:
   303→                    ann = arg.annotation
   304→                    if ann is None:
   305→                        continue
   306→                    ann_name = None
   307→                    if isinstance(ann, ast.Name):
   308→                        ann_name = ann.id
   309→                    elif isinstance(ann, ast.Attribute):
   310→                        ann_name = ann.attr
   311→                    if ann_name in typed_dicts:
   312→                        typed_vars[arg.arg] = ann_name
   313→
   314→        if not typed_vars:
   315→            continue
   316→
   317→        # Scan for violation calls — collect per (td_name, method, field)
   318→        hits: list[tuple[str, str, str | None, int]] = []
   319→        for node in ast.walk(tree):
   320→            if not isinstance(node, ast.Call):
   321→                continue
   322→            func = node.func
   323→            if not isinstance(func, ast.Attribute):
   324→                continue
   325→            if func.attr not in _VIOLATION_METHODS:
   326→                continue
   327→            if not isinstance(func.value, ast.Name) or func.value.id not in typed_vars:
   328→                continue
   329→            td_name = typed_vars[func.value.id]
   330→            # Extract the field name from the first argument if it's a string constant
   331→            field: str | None = None
   332→            if node.args and isinstance(node.args[0], ast.Constant):
   333→                val = node.args[0].value
   334→                if isinstance(val, str):
   335→                    field = val
   336→            hits.append((td_name, func.attr, field, node.lineno))
   337→
   338→        # Group by (td_name, method, field) for compact reporting
   339→        groups: dict[tuple[str, str, str | None], list[int]] = {}
   340→        for td_name, method, field, lineno in hits:
   341→            groups.setdefault((td_name, method, field), []).append(lineno)
   342→
   343→        for (td_name, method, field), lines in groups.items():
   344→            entry: dict = {
   345→                "file": rpath,
   346→                "typed_dict_name": td_name,
   347→                "violation_type": method,
   348→                "line": lines[0],
   349→                "count": len(lines),
   350→            }
   351→            if field is not None:
   352→                entry["field"] = field
   353→            violations.append(entry)
   354→
   355→    return violations

   358→def _abstractions_context(file_contents: dict[str, str]) -> dict:
   359→    util_files = []
   360→    wrappers_by_file: list[dict[str, object]] = []
   361→    interface_declarations: dict[str, set[str]] = defaultdict(set)
   362→    implementations: dict[str, set[str]] = defaultdict(set)
   363→    indirection_hotspots: list[dict[str, object]] = []
   364→    wide_param_bags: list[dict[str, object]] = []
   365→    delegation_classes: list[dict] = []
   366→    facade_modules: list[dict] = []
   367→    typed_dict_defs: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
   368→    parsed_trees: dict[str, ast.Module] = {}
   369→
   370→    total_function_signatures = 0
   371→    total_wrappers = 0
   372→
   373→    for filepath, content in file_contents.items():
   374→        rpath = rel(filepath)
   375→        loc = len(content.splitlines())
   376→        basename = Path(rpath).stem.lower()
   377→        if basename in {"utils", "helpers", "util", "helper", "common", "misc"}:
   378→            util_files.append(
   379→                {
   380→                    "file": rpath,
   381→                    "loc": loc,
   382→                    "excerpt": file_excerpt(filepath) or "",
   383→                }
   384→            )
   385→
   386→        # ── Regex-based detectors (all languages) ────────────
   387→        signatures = _DEF_SIGNATURE_RE.findall(content)
   388→        total_function_signatures += len(signatures)
   389→
   390→        ts_wrappers = [
   391→            (wrapper, target)
   392→            for wrapper, target in _TS_PASSTHROUGH_RE.findall(content)
   393→            if wrapper != target
   394→        ]
   395→
   396→        for match in _INTERFACE_RE.finditer(content):
   397→            iface = match.group(1) or match.group(2)
   398→            if iface:
   399→                interface_declarations[iface].add(rpath)
   400→
   401→        for match in _IMPLEMENTS_RE.finditer(content):
   402→            for iface in _extract_type_names(match.group(1)):
   403→                implementations[iface].add(rpath)
   404→        for match in _INHERITS_RE.finditer(content):
   405→            blob = match.group(1) or match.group(2) or ""
   406→            for iface in _extract_type_names(blob):
   407→                implementations[iface].add(rpath)
   408→
   409→        chain_matches = _CHAIN_RE.findall(content)
   410→        max_chain_depth = max((token.count(".") for token in chain_matches), default=0)
   411→        if max_chain_depth >= 3 or len(chain_matches) >= 6:
   412→            indirection_hotspots.append(
   413→                {
   414→                    "file": rpath,
   415→                    "max_chain_depth": max_chain_depth,
   416→                    "chain_count": len(chain_matches),
   417→                }
   418→            )
   419→
   420→        wide_functions = sum(
   421→            1 for params_blob in signatures if _count_signature_params(params_blob) >= 7
   422→        )
   423→        bag_mentions = len(_CONFIG_BAG_RE.findall(content))
   424→        if wide_functions > 0 or bag_mentions >= 10:
   425→            wide_param_bags.append(
   426→                {
   427→                    "file": rpath,
   428→                    "wide_functions": wide_functions,
   429→                    "config_bag_mentions": bag_mentions,
   430→                }
   431→            )
   432→
   433→        # ── AST-based detectors (Python files only) ──────────
   434→        try:
   435→            tree = ast.parse(content)
   436→        except SyntaxError:
   437→            tree = None
   438→
   439→        if tree is not None:
   440→            parsed_trees[filepath] = tree
   441→
   442→            py_wrappers = _find_python_passthrough_wrappers(tree)
   443→
   444→            for entry in _find_delegation_heavy_classes(tree):
   445→                delegation_classes.append({"file": rpath, **entry})
   446→
   447→            facade_result = _find_facade_modules(tree, loc=loc)
   448→            if facade_result is not None:
   449→                facade_modules.append({"file": rpath, **facade_result})

   451→            _collect_typed_dict_defs(tree, typed_dict_defs)
   452→        else:
   453→            py_wrappers = []
   454→
   455→        wrapper_pairs = py_wrappers + ts_wrappers
   456→        if wrapper_pairs:
   457→            total_wrappers += len(wrapper_pairs)
   458→            wrappers_by_file.append(
   459→                {
   460→                    "file": rpath,
   461→                    "count": len(wrapper_pairs),
   462→                    "samples": [f"{w}->{t}" for w, t in wrapper_pairs[:5]],
   463→                }
   464→            )
   465→
   466→    # ── Post-loop cross-file analysis ─────────────────────────
   467→
   468→    one_impl_interfaces: list[dict[str, object]] = []
   469→    for iface, declared_in in interface_declarations.items():
   470→        implemented_in = sorted(implementations.get(iface, set()))
   471→        if len(implemented_in) != 1:
   472→            continue
   473→        one_impl_interfaces.append(

   477→                "implemented_in": implemented_in,
   478→            }
   479→        )
   480→
   481→    typed_dict_violations = _find_typed_dict_usage_violations(
   482→        parsed_trees, typed_dict_defs
   483→    )[:20]
   484→    total_typed_dict_violations = sum(v.get("count", 1) for v in typed_dict_violations)
   485→    typed_dict_violation_files = {v["file"] for v in typed_dict_violations}
   486→
   487→    # ── Sort ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
   488→
   489→    wrappers_by_file.sort(key=lambda item: -int(item["count"]))
   490→    indirection_hotspots.sort(
   491→        key=lambda item: (-int(item["max_chain_depth"]), -int(item["chain_count"]))
   492→    )
   493→    wide_param_bags.sort(
   494→        key=lambda item: (
   495→            -int(item["wide_functions"]),
   496→            -int(item["config_bag_mentions"]),
   497→        )
   498→    )
   499→    one_impl_interfaces.sort(key=lambda item: str(item["interface"]))
   500→    delegation_classes.sort(key=lambda d: -d["delegation_ratio"])
   501→    delegation_classes = delegation_classes[:20]
   502→    facade_modules.sort(key=lambda d: -d["re_export_ratio"])
   503→    facade_modules = facade_modules[:20]
   504→
   505→    # ── Sub-axis scoring ──────────────────────────────────────
   506→
   507→    wrapper_rate = total_wrappers / max(total_function_signatures, 1)
   508→    abstraction_leverage = _score_clamped(
   509→        100 - (wrapper_rate * 120) - (len(util_files) * 1.5)
   510→    )
   511→    indirection_cost = _score_clamped(
   512→        100
   513→        - (sum(item["max_chain_depth"] for item in indirection_hotspots[:20]) * 2.5)
   514→        - (sum(item["wide_functions"] for item in wide_param_bags[:20]) * 2.0)
   515→    )
   516→    interface_honesty = _score_clamped(100 - (len(one_impl_interfaces) * 8))
   517→
   518→    top10_delegation = delegation_classes[:10]
   519→    avg_delegation_ratio = (
   520→        sum(d["delegation_ratio"] for d in top10_delegation) / len(top10_delegation)
   521→        if top10_delegation
   522→        else 0.0
   523→    )
   524→    delegation_density = _score_clamped(
   525→        100 - (avg_delegation_ratio * 80) - (len(delegation_classes) * 5)
   526→    )
   527→    avg_facade_ratio = (
   528→        sum(f["re_export_ratio"] for f in facade_modules[:10]) / len(facade_modules[:10])
   529→        if facade_modules
   530→        else 0.0
   531→    )
   532→    definition_directness = _score_clamped(
   533→        100 - (len(facade_modules) * 8) - (avg_facade_ratio * 50)
   534→    )
   535→    type_discipline = _score_clamped(
   536→        100
   537→        - (len(typed_dict_violation_files) * 6)
   538→        - (total_typed_dict_violations * 1.5)
   539→    )
   540→
   541→    util_files = sorted(util_files, key=lambda item: -item["loc"])[:20]
   542→    context: dict[str, object] = {
   543→        "util_files": util_files,
   544→        "summary": {
   545→            "wrapper_rate": round(wrapper_rate, 3),
   546→            "total_wrappers": total_wrappers,
   547→            "total_function_signatures": total_function_signatures,
   548→            "one_impl_interface_count": len(one_impl_interfaces),
   549→            "indirection_hotspot_count": len(indirection_hotspots),
   550→            "wide_param_bag_count": len(wide_param_bags),
   551→            "delegation_heavy_class_count": len(delegation_classes),
   552→            "facade_module_count": len(facade_modules),
   553→            "typed_dict_violation_count": total_typed_dict_violations,
   554→        },
   555→        "sub_axes": {
   556→            "abstraction_leverage": abstraction_leverage,
   557→            "indirection_cost": indirection_cost,
   558→            "interface_honesty": interface_honesty,
   559→            "delegation_density": delegation_density,
   560→            "definition_directness": definition_directness,
   561→            "type_discipline": type_discipline,
   562→        },
   563→    }
   564→    if wrappers_by_file:
   565→        context["pass_through_wrappers"] = wrappers_by_file[:20]
   566→    if one_impl_interfaces:
   567→        context["one_impl_interfaces"] = one_impl_interfaces[:20]
   568→    if indirection_hotspots:
   569→        context["indirection_hotspots"] = indirection_hotspots[:20]
   570→    if wide_param_bags:
   571→        context["wide_param_bags"] = wide_param_bags[:20]
   572→    if delegation_classes:
   573→        context["delegation_heavy_classes"] = delegation_classes
   574→    if facade_modules:
   575→        context["facade_modules"] = facade_modules
   576→    if typed_dict_violations:
   577→        context["typed_dict_violations"] = typed_dict_violations
   578→    return context

   583→    return {

    26→def select_holistic_files(path: Path, lang: object, files: list[str] | None) -> list[str]:
    27→    selected = files if files is not None else (lang.file_finder(path) if lang.file_finder else [])
    28→    if not selected:

    31→    zone_map = getattr(lang, "zone_map", None)

    39→            zone_value = getattr(zone, "value", str(zone))
    40→        except (AttributeError, KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):

    43→            continue

    48→def _architecture_context(lang, file_contents: dict[str, str]) -> dict:

    53→    importer_counts = {}

    56→        if entry_importer_count > 0:
    57→            importer_counts[rel(filepath)] = entry_importer_count
    58→    top_imported = sorted(importer_counts.items(), key=lambda item: -item[1])[:10]
    59→    arch["god_modules"] = [
    60→        {"file": filepath, "importers": count, "excerpt": file_excerpt(filepath) or ""}
    61→        for filepath, count in top_imported
    62→        if count >= 5

    64→    arch["top_imported"] = dict(top_imported)
    65→    return arch

    68→def _coupling_context(file_contents: dict[str, str]) -> dict:
    69→    coupling: dict = {}
    70→    module_level_io = []
    71→    for filepath, content in file_contents.items():
    72→        for idx, raw_line in enumerate(content.splitlines()[:50]):
    73→            stripped = raw_line.strip()
    74→            if stripped.startswith(
    75→                ("def ", "class ", "async def ", "if ", "#", "@", "import ", "from ")

    78→            if re.search(

    88→                )

    94→def _naming_conventions_context(file_contents: dict[str, str]) -> dict:
    95→    dir_styles: dict[str, Counter] = {}
    96→    for filepath, content in file_contents.items():
    97→        parts = Path(filepath).parts
    98→        if len(parts) < 2:
    99→            continue
   100→        dir_name = parts[-2] + "/"
   101→        counter = dir_styles.setdefault(dir_name, Counter())
   102→        for name in _FUNC_NAME_RE.findall(content):
   103→            if "_" in name and name.islower():
   104→                counter["snake_case"] += 1
   105→            elif name[0].islower() and any(ch.isupper() for ch in name):
   106→                counter["camelCase"] += 1
   107→            elif name[0].isupper():
   108→                counter["PascalCase"] += 1
   109→    return {
   110→        name: dict(counter.most_common(3))
   111→        for name, counter in dir_styles.items()
   112→        if sum(counter.values()) >= 3
   113→    }

   116→def _sibling_behavior_context(
   117→    file_contents: dict[str, str], *, base_path: Path | str | None = None
   118→) -> dict:
   119→    root = Path(base_path).resolve() if base_path is not None else None
   120→
   121→    def _bucket_for(filepath: str) -> str | None:
   122→        target = Path(filepath).resolve()
   123→        if root is not None:
   124→            try:
   125→                parts = target.relative_to(root).parts
   126→                if len(parts) >= 2:
   127→                    return f"{parts[0]}/"
   128→                return None
   129→            except ValueError:
   130→                logger.debug("Path %s not relative to root %s, using fallback bucket", filepath, root)
   131→        parts = Path(filepath).parts
   132→        if len(parts) < 2:
   133→            return None
   134→        return f"{parts[-2]}/"
   135→
   136→    def _display_path(filepath: str) -> str:
   137→        target = Path(filepath).resolve()
   138→        if root is not None:
   139→            try:
   140→                return target.relative_to(root).as_posix()
   141→            except ValueError:
   142→                logger.debug("Path %s not relative to root %s, using rel() fallback", filepath, root)
   143→        return rel(filepath)
   144→
   145→    dir_imports: dict[str, dict[str, set[str]]] = {}
   146→    for filepath, content in file_contents.items():
   147→        dir_name = _bucket_for(filepath)
   148→        if dir_name is None:
   149→            continue
   150→        file_rel = _display_path(filepath)
   151→        dir_imports.setdefault(dir_name, {})[file_rel] = _extract_imported_names(content)
   152→
   153→    sibling_behavior: dict = {}
   154→    for dir_name, file_names_map in dir_imports.items():
   155→        total = len(file_names_map)
   156→        if total < 3:
   157→            continue
   158→        name_counts: Counter = Counter()
   159→        for names in file_names_map.values():
   160→            for name in names:
   161→                name_counts[name] += 1
   162→        threshold = total * 0.6
   163→        shared = {
   164→            name: count for name, count in name_counts.items() if count >= threshold
   165→        }
   166→        if not shared:
   167→            continue
   168→        outliers = []
   169→        for file_rel, names in file_names_map.items():
   170→            missing = [name for name in shared if name not in names]
   171→            if missing:
   172→                outliers.append({"file": file_rel, "missing": sorted(missing)})
   173→        if not outliers:
   174→            continue
   175→        sibling_behavior[dir_name] = {
   176→            "shared_patterns": {
   177→                name: {"count": count, "total": total}
   178→                for name, count in sorted(shared.items(), key=lambda item: -item[1])
   179→            },
   180→            "outliers": sorted(
   181→                outliers, key=lambda item: len(item["missing"]), reverse=True
   182→            ),
   183→        }
   184→    return sibling_behavior
   185→
   186→
   187→def _error_strategy_context(file_contents: dict[str, str]) -> dict:
   188→    dir_errors: dict[str, Counter] = {}
   189→    for filepath, content in file_contents.items():
   190→        parts = Path(filepath).parts
   191→        if len(parts) < 2:
   192→            continue
   193→        dir_name = parts[-2] + "/"
   194→        counter = dir_errors.setdefault(dir_name, Counter())
   195→        for pattern_name, pattern in _ERROR_PATTERNS.items():
   196→            matches = pattern.findall(content)
   197→            if matches:
   198→                counter[pattern_name] += len(matches)
   199→    return {
   200→        name: dict(counter.most_common(5))
   201→        for name, counter in dir_errors.items()
   202→        if sum(counter.values()) >= 2
   203→    }
   204→
   205→
   206→def _dependencies_context(state: dict) -> dict:
   207→    cycle_findings = [

   210→        if finding.get("detector") == "cycles" and finding.get("status") == "open"

   212→    if not cycle_findings:

   220→def _testing_context(lang, state: dict, file_contents: dict[str, str]) -> dict:
   221→    testing: dict = {"total_files": len(file_contents)}

1→"""Holistic investigation batch builders for review preparation."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from pathlib import Path
     6→
     7→from desloppify.intelligence.review._context.models import HolisticContext
     8→
     9→_EXTENSIONLESS_FILENAMES = {
    10→    "makefile",
    11→    "dockerfile",
    12→    "readme",
    13→    "license",
    14→    "build",
    15→    "workspace",
    16→}
    17→
    18→_GOVERNANCE_REFERENCE_FILES: tuple[str, ...] = (
    19→    "README.md",
    20→    "DEVELOPMENT_PHILOSOPHY.md",
    21→    "desloppify/README.md",
    22→    "pyproject.toml",
    23→)
    24→
    25→
    26→def _normalize_file_path(value: object) -> str | None:
    27→    """Normalize/validate candidate file paths for batch payloads."""
    28→    if not isinstance(value, str):
    29→        return None
    30→    text = value.strip().strip(",'\"")
    31→    if not text or text in {".", ".."}:
    32→        return None
    33→    if text.endswith("/"):
    34→        return None
    35→
    36→    basename = Path(text).name
    37→    if not basename:
    38→        return None
    39→    if "." not in basename and basename.lower() not in _EXTENSIONLESS_FILENAMES:
    40→        return None
    41→    return text
    42→
    43→
    44→def _collect_unique_files(
    45→    sources: list[list[dict]],
    46→    key: str = "file",
    47→    *,
    48→    max_files: int | None = None,
    49→) -> list[str]:
    50→    """Collect unique file paths from multiple source lists."""
    51→    seen: set[str] = set()
    52→    out: list[str] = []
    53→    for src in sources:
    54→        for item in src:
    55→            f = _normalize_file_path(item.get(key, ""))
    56→            if f and f not in seen:
    57→                seen.add(f)
    58→                out.append(f)
    59→                if max_files is not None and len(out) >= max_files:
    60→                    return out
    61→    return out
    62→
    63→
    64→def _existing_repo_files(
    65→    repo_root: Path | None,
    66→    candidates: tuple[str, ...],
    67→) -> list[str]:
    68→    """Return repository-relative paths for candidate files that exist."""
    69→    if repo_root is None:
    70→        return []
    71→    out: list[str] = []
    72→    for candidate in candidates:
    73→        if (repo_root / candidate).is_file():
    74→            out.append(candidate)
    75→    return out
    76→
    77→
    78→def _collect_files_from_batches(
    79→    batches: list[dict], *, max_files: int | None = None
    80→) -> list[str]:
    81→    """Collect unique file paths across batch payloads (preserving order)."""
    82→    seen: set[str] = set()
    83→    out: list[str] = []
    84→    for batch in batches:
    85→        for filepath in batch.get("files_to_read", []):
    86→            normalized = _normalize_file_path(filepath)
    87→            if not normalized:
    88→                continue
    89→            if normalized in seen:
    90→                continue
    91→            seen.add(normalized)
    92→            out.append(normalized)
    93→            if max_files is not None and len(out) >= max_files:
    94→                return out
    95→    return out
    96→
    97→
    98→def _representative_files_for_directory(
    99→    ctx: HolisticContext,
   100→    directory: str,
   101→    *,
   102→    max_files: int = 3,
   103→) -> list[str]:
   104→    """Map a directory-level signal to representative file paths."""
   105→    if not isinstance(directory, str) or not directory.strip():
   106→        return []
   107→
   108→    dir_key = directory.strip()
   109→    if dir_key in {".", "./"}:
   110→        normalized_dir = "."
   111→    else:
   112→        normalized_dir = f"{dir_key.rstrip('/')}/"
   113→
   114→    profiles = ctx.structure.get("directory_profiles", {})
   115→    profile = profiles.get(normalized_dir)
   116→    if not isinstance(profile, dict):
   117→        return []
   118→
   119→    out: list[str] = []
   120→    for filename in profile.get("files", []):
   121→        if not isinstance(filename, str) or not filename:
   122→            continue
   123→        filepath = (
   124→            filename
   125→            if normalized_dir == "."
   126→            else f"{normalized_dir.rstrip('/')}/{filename}"
   127→        )
   128→        normalized = _normalize_file_path(filepath)
   129→        if not normalized or normalized in out:
   130→            continue
   131→        out.append(normalized)
   132→        if len(out) >= max_files:
   133→            break
   134→    return out
   135→
   136→
   137→def _batch_arch_coupling(ctx: HolisticContext, *, max_files: int | None = None) -> dict:
   138→    """Batch 1: Architecture & Coupling - god modules, import-time side effects."""
   139→    files = _collect_unique_files(
   140→        [
   141→            ctx.architecture.get("god_modules", []),
   142→            ctx.coupling.get("module_level_io", []),
   143→        ],
   144→        max_files=max_files,
   145→    )
   146→    return {
   147→        "name": "Architecture & Coupling",
   148→        "dimensions": ["cross_module_architecture", "high_level_elegance"],
   149→        "files_to_read": files,
   150→        "why": "god modules, import-time side effects",
   151→    }
   152→
   153→
   154→def _batch_conventions_errors(
   155→    ctx: HolisticContext, *, max_files: int | None = None
   156→) -> dict:
   157→    """Batch 2: Conventions & Errors - sibling behavior outliers, mixed strategies."""
   158→    sibling = ctx.conventions.get("sibling_behavior", {})
   159→    outlier_files = [
   160→        {"file": o["file"]} for di in sibling.values() for o in di.get("outliers", [])
   161→    ]
   162→    error_dirs = ctx.errors.get("strategy_by_directory", {})
   163→    mixed_dir_files: list[dict[str, str]] = []
   164→    for directory, strategies in error_dirs.items():
   165→        if not isinstance(strategies, dict) or len(strategies) < 3:
   166→            continue
   167→        for filepath in _representative_files_for_directory(ctx, directory):
   168→            mixed_dir_files.append({"file": filepath})
   169→
   170→    files = _collect_unique_files(

   174→    return {

   186→    util_files = ctx.abstractions.get("util_files", [])

   203→    for item in ctx.abstractions.get("one_impl_interfaces", []):

   289→def _batch_ai_debt_migrations(
   290→    ctx: HolisticContext, *, max_files: int | None = None
   291→) -> dict:
   292→    """Batch 6: AI Debt & Migrations - deprecated markers, migration TODOs."""
   293→    ai_debt = ctx.ai_debt_signals
   294→    migration = ctx.migration_signals
   295→    debt_files: list[dict] = []

   300→        for entry in dep_files:
   301→            debt_files.append({"file": entry})

   314→    }

   316→
   317→def _batch_package_organization(
   318→    ctx: HolisticContext, *, max_files: int | None = None
   319→) -> dict:
   320→    """Batch 7: Package Organization - file placement, directory boundaries."""
   321→    structure = ctx.structure
   322→    struct_files: list[dict] = []
   323→    for rf in structure.get("root_files", []):
   324→        if rf.get("role") == "peripheral":
   325→            struct_files.append({"file": rf["file"]})
   326→    dir_profiles = structure.get("directory_profiles", {})
   327→    largest_dirs = sorted(
   328→        dir_profiles.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1].get("file_count", 0)
   329→    )[:3]
   330→    for dir_key, profile in largest_dirs:
   331→        for fname in profile.get("files", [])[:3]:
   332→            dir_path = dir_key.rstrip("/")
   333→            rpath = f"{dir_path}/{fname}" if dir_path != "." else fname
   334→            struct_files.append({"file": rpath})
   335→    coupling_matrix = structure.get("coupling_matrix", {})
   336→    seen_edges: set[str] = set()
   337→    for edge in coupling_matrix:
   338→        if " → " in edge:
   339→            a, b = edge.split(" → ", 1)
   340→            reverse = f"{b} → {a}"
   341→            if reverse in coupling_matrix and edge not in seen_edges:
   342→                seen_edges.add(edge)
   343→                seen_edges.add(reverse)
   344→                for d in (a, b):
   345→                    for fname in dir_profiles.get(d, {}).get("files", [])[:2]:
   346→                        dir_path = d.rstrip("/")
   347→                        rpath = f"{dir_path}/{fname}" if dir_path != "." else fname
   348→                        struct_files.append({"file": rpath})
   349→    files = _collect_unique_files([struct_files], max_files=max_files)
   350→    return {
   351→        "name": "Package Organization",
   352→        "dimensions": ["package_organization", "high_level_elegance"],
   353→        "files_to_read": files,
   354→        "why": "file placement, directory boundaries, architectural layering",
   355→    }

   358→def _batch_governance_contracts(
   359→    ctx: HolisticContext,
   360→    *,
   361→    repo_root: Path | None,
   362→    max_files: int | None = None,
   363→) -> dict:
   364→    """Batch 8: Governance & Contracts - docs/policy promises vs runtime posture."""
   365→    docs = _existing_repo_files(repo_root, _GOVERNANCE_REFERENCE_FILES)
   366→    if not docs:
   367→        return {
   368→            "name": "Governance & Contracts",

   370→                "cross_module_architecture",

   374→            ],

   376→            "why": "architecture contracts, compatibility policy, docs-vs-runtime scope, and quality-gate coverage",
   377→        }
   378→    top_imported = [
   379→        {"file": filepath}
   380→        for filepath in list(ctx.architecture.get("top_imported", {}).keys())[:5]
   381→        if isinstance(filepath, str)
   382→    ]
   383→    anchor_files = _collect_unique_files(
   384→        [
   385→            top_imported,
   386→            ctx.architecture.get("god_modules", []),
   387→            ctx.coupling.get("module_level_io", []),
   388→        ],
   389→        max_files=5,
   390→    )
   391→    seen = set(docs)
   392→    files = list(docs)
   393→    for filepath in anchor_files:
   394→        if filepath in seen:
   395→            continue
   396→        seen.add(filepath)
   397→        files.append(filepath)
   398→    if max_files is not None:
   399→        files = files[:max_files]
   400→    return {
   401→        "name": "Governance & Contracts",
   402→        "dimensions": [
   403→            "cross_module_architecture",
   404→            "high_level_elegance",
   405→            "test_strategy",
   406→            "package_organization",
   407→        ],
   408→        "files_to_read": files,
   409→        "why": "architecture contracts, compatibility policy, docs-vs-runtime scope, and quality-gate coverage",
   410→    }

   413→def _ensure_holistic_context(holistic_ctx: HolisticContext | dict) -> HolisticContext:
   414→    if isinstance(holistic_ctx, HolisticContext):
   415→        return holistic_ctx
   416→    return HolisticContext.from_raw(holistic_ctx)

   419→def build_investigation_batches(
   420→    holistic_ctx: HolisticContext | dict,
   421→    lang: object,
   422→    *,
   423→    repo_root: Path | None = None,
   424→    max_files_per_batch: int | None = None,
   425→) -> list[dict]:
   426→    """Derive parallelizable investigation batches from holistic context."""
   427→    ctx = _ensure_holistic_context(holistic_ctx)
   428→    del lang  # Reserved for future language-specific batch shaping.
   429→    batches = [
   430→        _batch_arch_coupling(ctx, max_files=max_files_per_batch),
   431→        _batch_conventions_errors(ctx, max_files=max_files_per_batch),
   432→        _batch_abstractions_deps(ctx, max_files=max_files_per_batch),
   433→        _batch_testing_api(ctx, max_files=max_files_per_batch),
   434→        _batch_authorization(ctx, max_files=max_files_per_batch),
   435→        _batch_ai_debt_migrations(ctx, max_files=max_files_per_batch),
   436→        _batch_package_organization(ctx, max_files=max_files_per_batch),
   437→        _batch_governance_contracts(
   438→            ctx,
   439→            repo_root=repo_root,
   440→            max_files=max_files_per_batch,
   441→        ),
   442→    ]
   443→    return [batch for batch in batches if batch["files_to_read"]]
   444→
   445→
   446→def filter_batches_to_dimensions(
   447→    batches: list[dict],
   448→    dimensions: list[str],
   449→    *,
   450→    fallback_max_files: int | None = 80,
   451→) -> list[dict]:
   452→    """Keep only dimensions explicitly active for this holistic review run.
   453→
   454→    If selected dimensions are not represented by any batch mapping, append a
   455→    fallback batch over representative files so scoped runs still get guidance.
   456→    """
   457→    selected = [d for d in dimensions if isinstance(d, str) and d]
   458→    if not selected:
   459→        return []
   460→    selected_set = set(selected)
   461→    filtered: list[dict] = []
   462→    covered: set[str] = set()
   463→    for batch in batches:
   464→        batch_dims = [dim for dim in batch.get("dimensions", []) if dim in selected_set]
   465→        if not batch_dims:
   466→            continue
   467→        filtered.append({**batch, "dimensions": batch_dims})
   468→        covered.update(batch_dims)
   469→
   470→    missing = [dim for dim in selected if dim not in covered]
   471→    if not missing:
   472→        return filtered
   473→
   474→    # Keep fallback batches tractable; giant sweeps are expensive and often
   475→    # unnecessary when dimensions are already explicitly scoped.
   476→    max_files = fallback_max_files if isinstance(fallback_max_files, int) else None
   477→    if isinstance(max_files, int) and max_files <= 0:
   478→        max_files = None
   479→    fallback_files = _collect_files_from_batches(filtered or batches, max_files=max_files)
   480→    if not fallback_files:
   481→        return filtered
   482→
   483→    filtered.append(
   484→        {
   485→            "name": "Cross-cutting Sweep",
   486→            "dimensions": missing,
   487→            "files_to_read": fallback_files,
   488→            "why": "selected dimensions had no direct batch mapping; review representative cross-cutting files",
   489→        }
   490→    )
   491→    return filtered
   492→
   493→
   494→def batch_concerns(
   495→    concerns: list,
   496→    *,
   497→    max_files: int | None = None,
   498→) -> dict | None:
   499→    """Build investigation batch from mechanical concern signals.
   500→
   501→    *concerns* should be a list of Concern dataclass instances from
   502→    ``desloppify.engine.concerns``.
   503→    """
   504→    if not concerns:
   505→        return None
   506→    types = sorted({c.type for c in concerns if c.type})
   507→    why_parts = ["mechanical detectors identified structural patterns needing judgment"]
   508→    if types:
   509→        why_parts.append(f"concern types: {', '.join(types)}")
   510→    files: list[str] = []
   511→    seen: set[str] = set()
   512→    for concern in concerns:
   513→        candidate = _normalize_file_path(getattr(concern, "file", ""))
   514→        if not candidate or candidate in seen:
   515→            continue
   516→        seen.add(candidate)
   517→        files.append(candidate)
   518→
   519→    total_candidate_files = len(files)
   520→    if (
   521→        max_files is not None
   522→        and isinstance(max_files, int)
   523→        and max_files > 0
   524→        and total_candidate_files > max_files
   525→    ):
   526→        files = files[:max_files]
   527→        why_parts.append(
   528→            f"truncated to {max_files} files from {total_candidate_files} candidates"
   529→        )
   530→
   531→    return {
   532→        "name": "Design coherence — Mechanical Concern Signals",
   533→        "dimensions": ["design_coherence"],
   534→        "files_to_read": files,
   535→        "why": "; ".join(why_parts),
   536→        "total_candidate_files": total_candidate_files,
   537→    }
   538→
   539→
   540→__all__ = ["batch_concerns", "build_investigation_batches", "filter_batches_to_dimensions"]

   198→    def from_raw(cls, payload: Mapping[str, Any] | None) -> HolisticContext:
   199→        if payload is not None and not isinstance(payload, Mapping):
   200→            raise ReviewContextSchemaError(
   201→                f"holistic review context payload must be an object, got {type(payload).__name__}"
   202→            )
   203→        raw = payload if isinstance(payload, Mapping) else {}
   204→        return cls(**{section: raw.get(section) for section in cls._SECTION_NAMES})
   205→
   206→    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, object]:
   207→        return {section: getattr(self, section).to_dict() for section in self._SECTION_NAMES}
   208→
   209→
   210→__all__ = [
   211→    "HolisticContext",
   212→    "ReviewContext",
   213→    "ReviewContextSchemaError",

     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from collections import Counter
     6→from pathlib import Path
     7→from typing import Any
     8→
     9→from desloppify.core.discovery_api import rel, resolve_path
    10→from desloppify.intelligence.review.context import importer_count
    11→
    12→
    13→def compute_structure_context(
    14→    file_contents: dict[str, str], lang: Any
    15→) -> dict[str, object]:
    16→    """Compute directory profiles, root-level file analysis, and coupling matrix."""
    17→    graph = lang.dep_graph or {}
    18→    structure: dict[str, object] = {}
    19→
    20→    file_info: dict[str, dict] = {}
    21→    for filepath, content in file_contents.items():
    22→        rel_path = rel(filepath)
    23→        loc = len(content.splitlines())
    24→        entry = graph.get(resolve_path(filepath), {})
    25→        fan_in = importer_count(entry)
    26→        imports_raw = entry.get("imports", set())
    27→        fan_out = (
    28→            len(imports_raw)
    29→            if isinstance(imports_raw, set)
    30→            else entry.get("import_count", 0)
    31→        )
    32→        file_info[rel_path] = {"loc": loc, "fan_in": fan_in, "fan_out": fan_out}
    33→
    34→    dir_files: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    35→    for rel_path in file_info:
    36→        parts = Path(rel_path).parts
    37→        dir_key = "." if len(parts) == 1 else str(Path(*parts[:-1])) + "/"
    38→        dir_files.setdefault(dir_key, []).append(rel_path)
    39→
    40→    dir_profiles: dict[str, dict] = {}
    41→    for dir_key, files_in_dir in dir_files.items():
    42→        if len(files_in_dir) < 2:
    43→            continue
    44→
    45→        total_loc = sum(file_info[file]["loc"] for file in files_in_dir)
    46→        avg_fan_in = sum(file_info[file]["fan_in"] for file in files_in_dir) / len(
    47→            files_in_dir
    48→        )
    49→        avg_fan_out = sum(file_info[file]["fan_out"] for file in files_in_dir) / len(
    50→            files_in_dir
    51→        )
    52→
    53→        imports_from: Counter = Counter()
    54→        imported_by: Counter = Counter()
    55→        for file in files_in_dir:
    56→            entry = graph.get(resolve_path(file), {})
    57→            for imp in entry.get("imports", set()):
    58→                imp_rel = rel(imp)
    59→                imp_parts = Path(imp_rel).parts
    60→                imp_dir = (
    61→                    str(Path(*imp_parts[:-1])) + "/" if len(imp_parts) > 1 else "."
    62→                )
    63→                if imp_dir != dir_key:
    64→                    imports_from[imp_dir] += 1
    65→            for imp in entry.get("importers", set()):
    66→                imp_rel = rel(imp)
    67→                imp_parts = Path(imp_rel).parts
    68→                imp_dir = (
    69→                    str(Path(*imp_parts[:-1])) + "/" if len(imp_parts) > 1 else "."
    70→                )
    71→                if imp_dir != dir_key:
    72→                    imported_by[imp_dir] += 1
    73→
    74→        zone_counts: Counter = Counter()
    75→        if lang.zone_map is not None:
    76→            for file in files_in_dir:
    77→                zone_counts[lang.zone_map.get(file).value] += 1
    78→
    79→        dir_profiles[dir_key] = {
    80→            "file_count": len(files_in_dir),
    81→            "files": [Path(file).name for file in sorted(files_in_dir)],
    82→            "total_loc": total_loc,
    83→            "avg_fan_in": round(avg_fan_in, 1),
    84→            "avg_fan_out": round(avg_fan_out, 1),
    85→        }
    86→        if zone_counts:
    87→            dir_profiles[dir_key]["zones"] = dict(zone_counts)
    88→        if imports_from:
    89→            dir_profiles[dir_key]["imports_from_dirs"] = dict(
    90→                imports_from.most_common(10)
    91→            )
    92→        if imported_by:
    93→            dir_profiles[dir_key]["imported_by_dirs"] = dict(
    94→                imported_by.most_common(10)
    95→            )
    96→
    97→    structure["directory_profiles"] = dir_profiles
    98→
    99→    root_files = []
   100→    for rel_path in dir_files.get(".", []):
   101→        info = file_info[rel_path]
   102→        role = "core" if info["fan_in"] >= 5 else "peripheral"
   103→        root_files.append(
   104→            {
   105→                "file": rel_path,
   106→                "loc": info["loc"],
   107→                "fan_in": info["fan_in"],
   108→                "fan_out": info["fan_out"],
   109→                "role": role,
   110→            }
   111→        )
   112→    if root_files:
   113→        root_files.sort(key=lambda item: -item["fan_in"])
   114→        structure["root_files"] = root_files
   115→
   116→    edge_counts: Counter = Counter()
   117→    for dir_key, profile in dir_profiles.items():
   118→        for target, count in profile.get("imports_from_dirs", {}).items():
   119→            edge_counts[f"{dir_key} → {target}"] += count
   120→    if edge_counts:
   121→        structure["coupling_matrix"] = dict(edge_counts.most_common(20))
   122→
   123→    return structure
   124→
   125→
   126→__all__ = ["compute_structure_context"]
   127→

1→"""Concern generators — mechanical findings → subjective review bridge.
     2→
     3→Concerns are ephemeral: computed on-demand from current state, never persisted.
     4→Only LLM-confirmed concerns become persistent Finding objects via review import.
     5→
     6→Generators focus on cross-cutting synthesis — bundling all signals per file so
     7→the LLM gets a complete picture, and surfacing systemic patterns across files
     8→that no single detector captures.
     9→"""

    25→    type: str  # concern classification
    26→    file: str  # primary file (relative path)
    27→    summary: str  # human-readable 1-liner
    28→    evidence: tuple[str, ...]  # supporting data points
    29→    question: str  # specific question for LLM to evaluate
    30→    fingerprint: str  # stable hash for dismissal tracking

    49→def _update_max_signal(signals: ConcernSignals, key: SignalKey, value: object) -> None:
    50→    """Update numeric signal key with max(existing, value) when value is valid."""
    51→    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int | float) or value <= 0:
    52→        return
    53→    current = float(signals.get(key, 0.0))
    54→    signals[key] = max(current, float(value))
    55→
    56→
    57→def _fingerprint(concern_type: str, file: str, key_signals: tuple[str, ...]) -> str:
    58→    """Stable hash of (type, file, sorted key signals)."""
    59→    raw = f"{concern_type}::{file}::{','.join(sorted(key_signals))}"
    60→    return hashlib.sha256(raw.encode()).hexdigest()[:16]

    62→
    63→def _is_dismissed(
    64→    dismissals: dict, fingerprint: str, source_finding_ids: tuple[str, ...]
    65→) -> bool:
    66→    """Check if a concern was previously dismissed and source findings unchanged."""
    67→    entry = dismissals.get(fingerprint)
    68→    if not isinstance(entry, dict):
    69→        return False
    70→    prev_sources = set(entry.get("source_finding_ids", []))
    71→    return prev_sources == set(source_finding_ids)
    72→
    73→
    74→def _open_findings(state: dict[str, Any]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    75→    """Return all open findings from state."""
    76→    findings = state.get("findings", {})
    77→    return [
    78→        f for f in findings.values()
    79→        if isinstance(f, dict) and f.get("status") == "open"
    80→    ]
    81→
    82→
    83→def _group_by_file(state: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]]:
    84→    """Group open findings by file, excluding holistic (file='.')."""
    85→    by_file: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]] = defaultdict(list)
    86→    for f in _open_findings(state):
    87→        file = f.get("file", "")
    88→        if file and file != ".":
    89→            by_file[file].append(f)
    90→    return dict(by_file)
    91→
    92→
    93→# ── Signal extraction ────────────────────────────────────────────────
    94→
    95→
    96→def _extract_signals(findings: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> ConcernSignals:
    97→    """Extract key quantitative signals from a file's findings."""
    98→    signals: ConcernSignals = {}
    99→    monster_funcs: list[str] = []
   100→
   101→    for f in findings:
   102→        det = f.get("detector", "")
   103→        detail_raw = f.get("detail", {})
   104→        detail = detail_raw if isinstance(detail_raw, dict) else {}
   105→
   106→        if det == "structural":
   107→            s = detail.get("signals", {})
   108→            if isinstance(s, dict):
   109→                for key in _NUMERIC_SIGNAL_KEYS:
   110→                    _update_max_signal(signals, cast(SignalKey, key), s.get(key, 0))
   111→
   112→        if det == "smells" and detail.get("smell_id") == "monster_function":
   113→            _update_max_signal(signals, "monster_loc", detail.get("loc", 0))
   114→            func = detail.get("function", "")
   115→            if isinstance(func, str) and func:
   116→                monster_funcs.append(func)
   117→
   118→    if monster_funcs:
   119→        signals["monster_funcs"] = monster_funcs
   120→    return signals
   121→
   122→
   123→def _has_elevated_signals(findings: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> bool:
   124→    """Does any finding have signals strong enough to flag on its own?"""
   125→    for f in findings:
   126→        det = f.get("detector", "")
   127→        detail = f.get("detail", {})
   128→
   129→        if det == "structural":
   130→            s = detail.get("signals", {})
   131→            if isinstance(s, dict):
   132→                if s.get("max_params", 0) >= 8:
   133→                    return True
   134→                if s.get("max_nesting", 0) >= 6:
   135→                    return True
   136→                if s.get("loc", 0) >= 300:
   137→                    return True
   138→
   139→        if det == "smells" and detail.get("smell_id") == "monster_function":
   140→            return True
   141→
   142→        if det in ("dupes", "boilerplate_duplication", "coupling",
   143→                    "responsibility_cohesion"):
   144→            return True
   145→
   146→    return False
   147→
   148→
   149→# ── Concern classification ───────────────────────────────────────────
   150→
   151→
   152→def _classify(detectors: set[str], signals: ConcernSignals) -> str:
   153→    """Pick the most specific concern type from what's present."""
   154→    if len(detectors) >= 3:
   155→        return "mixed_responsibilities"
   156→    if "dupes" in detectors or "boilerplate_duplication" in detectors:
   157→        return "duplication_design"
   158→    if signals.get("monster_loc", 0) > 0:
   159→        return "structural_complexity"
   160→    if "coupling" in detectors:
   161→        return "coupling_design"
   162→    if signals.get("max_params", 0) >= 8:
   163→        return "interface_design"
   164→    if signals.get("max_nesting", 0) >= 6:
   165→        return "structural_complexity"
   166→    if "responsibility_cohesion" in detectors:
   167→        return "mixed_responsibilities"
   168→    return "design_concern"
   169→
   170→
   171→def _build_summary(
   172→    concern_type: str,
   173→    detectors: set[str],
   174→    signals: ConcernSignals,
   175→) -> str:
   176→    """Human-readable one-liner."""
   177→    if concern_type == "mixed_responsibilities":
   178→        return (
   179→            f"Issues from {len(detectors)} detectors — "
   180→            "may have too many responsibilities"
   181→        )
   182→    if concern_type == "structural_complexity":
   183→        parts: list[str] = []
   184→        monster_loc = signals.get("monster_loc", 0)
   185→        if monster_loc:
   186→            funcs = signals.get("monster_funcs", [])
   187→            label = f" ({', '.join(funcs[:3])})" if funcs else ""
   188→            parts.append(f"monster function{label}: {int(monster_loc)} lines")
   189→        nesting = signals.get("max_nesting", 0)
   190→        if nesting >= 6:
   191→            parts.append(f"nesting depth {int(nesting)}")
   192→        params = signals.get("max_params", 0)
   193→        if params >= 8:
   194→            parts.append(f"{int(params)} parameters")
   195→        return f"Structural complexity: {', '.join(parts) or 'elevated signals'}"
   196→    if concern_type == "duplication_design":
   197→        return "Duplication pattern — assess if extraction is warranted"
   198→    if concern_type == "coupling_design":
   199→        return "Coupling pattern — assess if boundaries need adjustment"
   200→    if concern_type == "interface_design":
   201→        return f"Interface complexity: {int(signals.get('max_params', 0))} parameters"
   202→    return f"Design signals from {', '.join(sorted(detectors))}"
   203→
   204→
   205→def _build_evidence(
   206→    findings: list[dict[str, Any]],
   207→    signals: ConcernSignals,
   208→) -> tuple[str, ...]:
   209→    """Build evidence tuple from all findings and extracted signals."""
   210→    evidence: list[str] = []
   211→
   212→    detectors = sorted({f.get("detector", "") for f in findings})
   213→    evidence.append(f"Flagged by: {', '.join(detectors)}")
   214→
   215→    loc = signals.get("loc")
   216→    if loc:
   217→        evidence.append(f"File size: {int(loc)} lines")
   218→    params = signals.get("max_params")
   219→    if params and params >= 8:
   220→        evidence.append(f"Max parameters: {int(params)}")
   221→    nesting = signals.get("max_nesting")
   222→    if nesting and nesting >= 6:
   223→        evidence.append(f"Max nesting depth: {int(nesting)}")
   224→    monster_loc = signals.get("monster_loc")
   225→    if monster_loc:
   226→        funcs = signals.get("monster_funcs", [])
   227→        label = f" ({', '.join(funcs[:3])})" if funcs else ""
   228→        evidence.append(f"Monster function{label}: {int(monster_loc)} lines")
   229→
   230→    # Individual finding summaries — give LLM the full picture, capped.
   231→    for f in findings[:10]:
   232→        summary = f.get("summary", "")
   233→        if summary:
   234→            evidence.append(f"[{f.get('detector', '')}] {summary}")
   235→
   236→    return tuple(evidence)
   237→
   238→
   239→def _build_question(
   240→    detectors: set[str], signals: ConcernSignals
   241→) -> str:
   242→    """Build targeted question from dominant signals."""
   243→    parts: list[str] = []
   244→
   245→    if len(detectors) >= 3:
   246→        parts.append(
   247→            f"This file has issues across {len(detectors)} dimensions "
   248→            f"({', '.join(sorted(detectors))}). Is it trying to do too many "
   249→            "things, or is this complexity inherent to its domain?"
   250→        )
   251→
   252→    funcs = signals.get("monster_funcs", [])
   253→    if funcs:
   254→        parts.append(
   255→            f"What are the distinct responsibilities in {funcs[0]}()? "
   256→            "Should it be decomposed into focused functions?"
   257→        )
   258→
   259→    if signals.get("max_params", 0) >= 8:
   260→        parts.append(
   261→            "Should the parameters be grouped into a config/context object? "
   262→            "Which ones belong together?"
   263→        )
   264→
   265→    if signals.get("max_nesting", 0) >= 6:
   266→        parts.append(
   267→            "Can the nesting be reduced with early returns, guard clauses, "
   268→            "or extraction into helper functions?"
   269→        )
   270→
   271→    if "dupes" in detectors or "boilerplate_duplication" in detectors:
   272→        parts.append(
   273→            "Is the duplication worth extracting into a shared utility, "
   274→            "or is it intentional variation?"
   275→        )
   276→
   277→    if "coupling" in detectors:
   278→        parts.append(
   279→            "Is the coupling intentional or does it indicate a missing "
   280→            "abstraction boundary?"
   281→        )
   282→
   283→    if "orphaned" in detectors:
   284→        parts.append(
   285→            "Is this file truly dead, or is it used via a non-import mechanism "
   286→            "(dynamic import, CLI entry point, plugin)?"
   287→        )
   288→
   289→    if "responsibility_cohesion" in detectors:
   290→        parts.append(
   291→            "What are the distinct responsibilities? Should this module be "
   292→            "split along those lines?"
   293→        )
   294→
   295→    if not parts:
   296→        parts.append(
   297→            "Review the flagged patterns — are they design problems that "
   298→            "need addressing, or acceptable given the file's role?"
   299→        )
   300→
   301→    return " ".join(parts)
   302→
   303→
   304→# ── Generators ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   305→
   306→
   307→def _file_concerns(state: dict[str, Any], dismissals: dict[str, Any]) -> list[Concern]:
   308→    """Per-file design concerns from aggregated mechanical signals.
   309→
   310→    Flags a file if it has 2+ judgment-needed detectors OR a single
   311→    detector with elevated signals (monster function, high params,
   312→    deep nesting, duplication, coupling, mixed responsibilities).
   313→    Bundles ALL findings for that file so the LLM sees the full picture.
   314→    """
   315→    by_file = _group_by_file(state)
   316→    concerns: list[Concern] = []
   317→
   318→    for file, all_findings in by_file.items():
   319→        judgment = [
   320→            f for f in all_findings
   321→            if f.get("detector", "") in JUDGMENT_DETECTORS
   322→        ]
   323→        if not judgment:
   324→            continue
   325→
   326→        judgment_dets = {f.get("detector", "") for f in judgment}
   327→        elevated = _has_elevated_signals(judgment)
   328→
   329→        # Flag if 2+ judgment detectors OR 1 with elevated signals.
   330→        if len(judgment_dets) < 2 and not elevated:
   331→            continue
   332→
   333→        signals = _extract_signals(judgment)
   334→        concern_type = _classify(judgment_dets, signals)
   335→        evidence = _build_evidence(judgment, signals)
   336→        question = _build_question(judgment_dets, signals)
   337→        summary = _build_summary(concern_type, judgment_dets, signals)
   338→
   339→        all_ids = tuple(sorted(f.get("id", "") for f in judgment))
   340→        fp_keys = tuple(sorted(judgment_dets))
   341→        fp = _fingerprint(concern_type, file, fp_keys)
   342→
   343→        if _is_dismissed(dismissals, fp, all_ids):
   344→            continue
   345→
   346→        concerns.append(
   347→            Concern(
   348→                type=concern_type,
   349→                file=file,
   350→                summary=summary,
   351→                evidence=evidence,
   352→                question=question,
   353→                fingerprint=fp,
   354→                source_findings=all_ids,
   355→            )
   356→        )
   357→
   358→    return concerns
   359→
   360→
   361→def _cross_file_patterns(state: dict[str, Any], dismissals: dict[str, Any]) -> list[Concern]:
   362→    """Systemic patterns: same judgment detector combo across 3+ files.
   363→
   364→    When multiple files share the same combination of detector types,
   365→    that's likely a codebase-wide pattern rather than isolated issues.
   366→    """
   367→    by_file = _group_by_file(state)
   368→
   369→    # Group files by their judgment detector profile.
   370→    profile_to_files: dict[frozenset[str], list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
   371→    for file, findings in by_file.items():
   372→        dets = frozenset(
   373→            f.get("detector", "") for f in findings
   374→            if f.get("detector", "") in JUDGMENT_DETECTORS
   375→        )
   376→        if len(dets) >= 2:
   377→            profile_to_files[dets].append(file)
   378→
   379→    concerns: list[Concern] = []
   380→    for det_combo, files in profile_to_files.items():
   381→        if len(files) < 3:
   382→            continue
   383→
   384→        sorted_files = sorted(files)
   385→        combo_names = tuple(sorted(det_combo))
   386→        all_ids = tuple(sorted(
   387→            f.get("id", "")
   388→            for file in sorted_files
   389→            for f in by_file[file]
   390→            if f.get("detector", "") in det_combo
   391→        ))
   392→        # Use first few files in fingerprint so it's stable but bounded.
   393→        fp = _fingerprint(
   394→            "systemic_pattern",
   395→            ",".join(sorted_files[:5]),
   396→            combo_names,
   397→        )
   398→
   399→        if _is_dismissed(dismissals, fp, all_ids):
   400→            continue
   401→
   402→        concerns.append(
   403→            Concern(
   404→                type="systemic_pattern",
   405→                file=sorted_files[0],
   406→                summary=(
   407→                    f"{len(files)} files share the same problem pattern "
   408→                    f"({', '.join(combo_names)})"
   409→                ),
   410→                evidence=(
   411→                    f"Affected files: {', '.join(sorted_files[:10])}",
   412→                    f"Shared detectors: {', '.join(combo_names)}",
   413→                    f"Total files: {len(files)}",
   414→                ),
   415→                question=(
   416→                    f"These {len(files)} files all have the same combination "
   417→                    f"of issues ({', '.join(combo_names)}). Is this a systemic "
   418→                    "pattern that should be addressed at the architecture level "
   419→                    "(shared base class, framework change, lint rule), or are "
   420→                    "these independent issues that happen to look similar?"
   421→                ),
   422→                fingerprint=fp,
   423→                source_findings=all_ids,
   424→            )
   425→        )
   426→
   427→    return concerns
   428→
   429→
   430→_GENERATORS = [_file_concerns, _cross_file_patterns]
   431→
   432→
   433→def generate_concerns(
   434→    state: dict[str, Any],
   435→    lang_name: str | None = None,
   436→) -> list[Concern]:
   437→    """Run all concern generators against current state.
   438→
   439→    Returns deduplicated list sorted by (type, file).
   440→    lang_name is reserved for future language-specific generators.
   441→    """
   442→    del lang_name  # Reserved for future use.
   443→    dismissals = state.get("concern_dismissals", {})
   444→    concerns: list[Concern] = []
   445→    seen_fps: set[str] = set()
   446→
   447→    for gen in _GENERATORS:
   448→        for concern in gen(state, dismissals):
   449→            if concern.fingerprint not in seen_fps:
   450→                seen_fps.add(concern.fingerprint)
   451→                concerns.append(concern)
   452→
   453→    concerns.sort(key=lambda c: (c.type, c.file))
   454→    return concerns
   455→
   456→
   457→def cleanup_stale_dismissals(state: dict[str, Any]) -> int:
   458→    """Remove dismissals whose source findings all disappeared.
   459→
   460→    Returns the number of stale entries removed.  Dismissals without
   461→    ``source_finding_ids`` (legacy) are left untouched.
   462→    """
   463→    dismissals = state.get("concern_dismissals", {})
   464→    if not dismissals:
   465→        return 0
   466→    open_ids = {f.get("id", "") for f in _open_findings(state)}
   467→    stale_fps = [
   468→        fp
   469→        for fp, entry in dismissals.items()
   470→        if entry.get("source_finding_ids")
   471→        and not any(sid in open_ids for sid in entry["source_finding_ids"])
   472→    ]
   473→    for fp in stale_fps:
   474→        del dismissals[fp]
   475→    return len(stale_fps)
   476→
   477→
   478→__all__ = ["Concern", "cleanup_stale_dismissals", "generate_concerns"]
   479→

   325→JUDGMENT_DETECTORS: frozenset[str] = frozenset(
   326→    name for name, meta in DETECTORS.items() if meta.needs_judgment
   327→)
   328→
   329→_on_register_callbacks: list[Callable[[], None]] = []
   330→
   331→
   332→def on_detector_registered(callback: Callable[[], None]) -> None:
   333→    """Register a callback invoked after register_detector(). No-arg."""
   334→    _on_register_callbacks.append(callback)
   335→
   336→
   337→def register_detector(meta: DetectorMeta) -> None:
   338→    """Register a detector at runtime (used by generic plugins)."""
   339→    global JUDGMENT_DETECTORS
   340→    DETECTORS[meta.name] = meta
   341→    if meta.name not in _DISPLAY_ORDER:
   342→        _DISPLAY_ORDER.append(meta.name)
   343→    JUDGMENT_DETECTORS = frozenset(
   344→        name for name, m in DETECTORS.items() if m.needs_judgment
   345→    )
   346→    for cb in _on_register_callbacks:
   347→        cb()
   348→
   349→
   350→def detector_names() -> list[str]:
   351→    """All registered detector names, sorted."""
   352→    return sorted(DETECTORS.keys())
   353→
   354→
   355→def display_order() -> list[str]:
   356→    """Canonical display order for terminal output."""
   357→    return list(_DISPLAY_ORDER)
   358→
   359→
   360→_ACTION_PRIORITY = {"auto_fix": 0, "reorganize": 1, "refactor": 2, "manual_fix": 3}
   361→_ACTION_LABELS = {
   362→    "auto_fix": "fix",
   363→    "reorganize": "move",
   364→    "refactor": "refactor",
   365→    "manual_fix": "manual",
   366→}
   367→
   368→
   369→def dimension_action_type(dim_name: str) -> str:
   370→    """Return a compact action type label for a dimension based on its detectors."""
   371→    best = "manual"
   372→    best_pri = 99
   373→    for d in DETECTORS.values():
   374→        if d.dimension == dim_name:
   375→            pri = _ACTION_PRIORITY.get(d.action_type, 99)
   376→            if pri < best_pri:
   377→                best_pri = pri
   378→                best = d.action_type
   379→    return _ACTION_LABELS.get(best, "manual")
   380→
   381→
   382→def detector_tools() -> dict[str, dict]:
   383→    """Build detector tool metadata keyed by detector name."""
   384→    result = {}
   385→    for name, d in DETECTORS.items():
   386→        entry: dict = {
   387→            "fixers": list(d.fixers),
   388→            "action_type": d.action_type,
   389→        }
   390→        if d.tool:
   391→            entry["tool"] = d.tool
   392→        if d.guidance:
   393→            entry["guidance"] = d.guidance
   394→        result[name] = entry
   395→    return result

    41→def hash_file(filepath: str) -> str:

    66→    cache = state.get("review_cache", {}).get("files", {})
    67→    now = datetime.now(UTC)
    68→    candidates = []
    69→
    70→    for filepath in files:
    71→        rpath = rel(filepath)
    72→
    73→        # Skip non-production files
    74→        if lang.zone_map is not None:
    75→            zone = lang.zone_map.get(filepath)
    76→            if zone.value in ("test", "generated", "vendor"):
    77→                continue
    78→
    79→        # Skip if cached, content unchanged, and not stale
    80→        if not resolved_options.force_refresh:
    81→            entry = cache.get(rpath)
    82→            if entry:
    83→                current_hash = hash_file(abs_path(filepath))
    84→                if current_hash and current_hash == entry.get("content_hash"):
    85→                    reviewed_at = entry.get("reviewed_at", "")
    86→                    if reviewed_at:
    87→                        try:
    88→                            reviewed = datetime.fromisoformat(reviewed_at)
    89→                            age_days = (now - reviewed).days
    90→                            if age_days <= resolved_options.max_age_days:
    91→                                continue  # Still fresh
    92→                        except (ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
    93→                            entry["reviewed_at"] = ""
    94→                            logger.debug(
    95→                                "Invalid reviewed_at value %r for %s: %s",
    96→                                reviewed_at,
    97→                                rpath,
    98→                                exc,
    99→                            )
   100→
   101→        priority = _compute_review_priority(filepath, lang, state)
   102→        if priority >= 0:  # Negative = filtered out (too small)
   103→            candidates.append((filepath, priority))
   104→
   105→    candidates.sort(key=lambda x: -x[1])
   106→    selected = [f for f, _ in candidates]
   107→    if resolved_options.max_files is None:
   108→        return selected
   109→    return selected[: resolved_options.max_files]
   110→
   111→
   112→def _compute_review_priority(filepath: str, lang, state: dict) -> int:
   113→    """Higher = more important to review.
   114→
   115→    Prioritizes implementation files with high blast radius and existing findings.
   116→    Deprioritizes types/constants files (low subjective review value).
   117→    """
   118→    score = 0
   119→    rpath = rel(filepath)
   120→
   121→    content = read_file_text(abs_path(filepath))
   122→    loc = len(content.splitlines()) if content is not None else 0
   123→
   124→    # Skip tiny files — not enough to review
   125→    if loc < MIN_REVIEW_LOC:
   126→        return -1
   127→
   128→    # Low-value files: language-provided pattern or generic fallback.
   129→    is_low_value = is_low_value_file(rpath, lang)
   130→
   131→    # High blast radius (many importers)
   132→    if lang.dep_graph:
   133→        entry = dep_graph_lookup(lang.dep_graph, filepath)
   134→        ic = importer_count(entry)
   135→        if is_low_value:
   136→            score += ic * 2
   137→        else:
   138→            score += ic * 10
   139→
   140→    # Already has programmatic findings (compound value — review will be richer)
   141→    findings = state.get("findings", {})
   142→    n_findings = sum(
   143→        1 for f in findings.values() if f.get("file") == rpath and f["status"] == "open"
   144→    )
   145→    score += n_findings * 5
   146→
   147→    # High-complexity files with wontfixed structural findings
   148→    # (mechanical detector says "complex" but can't say why — subjective review can)
   149→    n_wontfix_structural = sum(
   150→        1
   151→        for f in findings.values()
   152→        if f.get("file") == rpath
   153→        and f["status"] == "wontfix"
   154→        and f.get("detector") in ("structural", "smells")
   155→    )
   156→    if n_wontfix_structural:
   157→        score += n_wontfix_structural * 15  # Strong boost — these need human insight
   158→
   159→    # Complexity score from mechanical detectors (if available)
   160→    complexity_map = getattr(lang, "complexity_map", None)
   161→    if isinstance(complexity_map, dict) and complexity_map.get(rpath, 0) > 100:
   162→        score += 20  # Very complex files need subjective review most
   163→
   164→    # Larger files have more to review
   165→    score += loc // 50
   166→
   167→    # Low-value penalty — push toward bottom but don't exclude entirely
   168→    if is_low_value:
   169→        score = score // 3
   170→
   171→    return score
   172→
   173→
   174→def low_value_pattern(lang_or_name: Any = None) -> re.Pattern[str]:
   175→    """Return the low-value filename regex for a language, with generic fallback."""
   176→    if lang_or_name is not None and hasattr(lang_or_name, "review_low_value_pattern"):
   177→        pattern = getattr(lang_or_name, "review_low_value_pattern", None)
   178→        if isinstance(pattern, re.Pattern):
   179→            return pattern
   180→
   181→    if isinstance(lang_or_name, str):
   182→        try:
   183→            pattern = getattr(
   184→                get_lang(lang_or_name), "review_low_value_pattern", None
   185→            )
   186→            if isinstance(pattern, re.Pattern):
   187→                return pattern
   188→        except (ImportError, ValueError, TypeError, AttributeError) as exc:
   189→            pattern = None
   190→            logger.debug(
   191→                "Unable to load low-value review pattern for %s: %s", lang_or_name, exc
   192→            )
   193→
   194→    return LOW_VALUE_NAMES
   195→
   196→
   197→def is_low_value_file(filepath: str, lang_or_name=None) -> bool:
   198→    """Whether a file path is low-value for subjective review."""
   199→    pattern = low_value_pattern(lang_or_name)
   200→    return bool(pattern.search(filepath))
   201→
   202→
   203→def get_file_findings(state: dict, filepath: str) -> list[dict]:
   204→    """Get existing open findings for a file (summaries for context)."""
   205→    rpath = rel(filepath)
   206→    findings = state.get("findings", {})
   207→    return [
   208→        {"detector": f["detector"], "summary": f["summary"], "id": f["id"]}
   209→        for f in findings.values()
   210→        if f.get("file") == rpath and f["status"] == "open"
   211→    ]
   212→
   213→
   214→def count_fresh(state: dict, max_age_days: int) -> int:
   215→    """Count files in review cache that are still fresh."""
   216→    cache = state.get("review_cache", {}).get("files", {})
   217→    now = datetime.now(UTC)
   218→    count = 0
   219→    for entry in cache.values():
   220→        reviewed_at = entry.get("reviewed_at", "")
   221→        if reviewed_at:
   222→            try:
   223→                reviewed = datetime.fromisoformat(reviewed_at)
   224→                if (now - reviewed).days <= max_age_days:
   225→                    count += 1
   226→            except (ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
   227→                logger.debug(
   228→                    "Invalid review cache date %r while counting fresh files: %s",
   229→                    reviewed_at,
   230→                    exc,
   231→                )
   232→    return count
   233→
   234→
   235→def count_stale(state: dict, max_age_days: int) -> int:
   236→    """Count files in review cache that are stale."""
   237→    cache = state.get("review_cache", {}).get("files", {})
   238→    total = len(cache)
   239→    return total - count_fresh(state, max_age_days)
   240→

1→"""Duplicate / near-duplicate function detection via body hashing + difflib similarity.
     2→
     3→Output is clustered: N similar functions produce 1 entry (not N^2/2 pairwise entries).
     4→Each entry contains a representative pair for display plus the full cluster membership.
     5→"""

     7→import difflib
     8→import os
     9→import sys

    12→
    13→def _build_clusters(
    14→    pairs: list[tuple[int, int, float, str]], n: int
    15→) -> list[list[int]]:
    16→    """Union-find clustering from pairwise matches. Returns list of clusters (size >= 2)."""
    17→    parent = list(range(n))
    18→
    19→    def find(x):
    20→        while parent[x] != x:
    21→            parent[x] = parent[parent[x]]
    22→            x = parent[x]
    23→        return x
    24→
    25→    def union(a, b):
    26→        ra, rb = find(a), find(b)
    27→        if ra != rb:
    28→            parent[ra] = rb
    29→
    30→    for i, j, _, _ in pairs:
    31→        union(i, j)
    32→
    33→    clusters: dict[int, list[int]] = {}
    34→    for i in range(n):
    35→        r = find(i)
    36→        clusters.setdefault(r, []).append(i)
    37→    return [c for c in clusters.values() if len(c) >= 2]

     2→
     3→from collections import defaultdict
     4→from pathlib import Path
     5→
     6→from desloppify.core.discovery_api import rel
     7→
     8→
     9→def _classify_convention(filename: str) -> str | None:
    10→    """Classify a filename (without extension) into a naming convention."""
    11→    stem = filename.rsplit(".", 1)[0] if "." in filename else filename
    12→    if not stem:
    13→        return None
    14→
    15→    if "-" in stem and stem == stem.lower():
    16→        return "kebab-case"
    17→    if stem[0].isupper() and "-" not in stem:
    18→        return "PascalCase"
    19→    if stem[0].islower() and any(c.isupper() for c in stem) and "-" not in stem:
    20→        return "camelCase"
    21→    if "_" in stem and stem == stem.lower():
    22→        return "snake_case"
    23→    if stem.islower() and "-" not in stem:
    24→        return "flat_lower"
    25→    return None
    26→
    27→
    28→def detect_naming_inconsistencies(
    29→    path: Path,
    30→    file_finder,
    31→    skip_names: set[str] | None = None,
    32→    skip_dirs: set[str] | None = None,
    33→) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:

    35→
    36→    Thresholds: minority must have >= 5 files (absolute) and >= 15% of total (proportional).
    37→    """
    38→    all_skip_names = skip_names or set()
    39→    all_skip_dirs = skip_dirs or set()
    40→    files = file_finder(path)
    41→
    42→    dir_files: dict[str, dict[str, list[str]]] = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(list))
    43→
    44→    for filepath in files:
    45→        p = Path(filepath)
    46→        dirname = str(p.parent)
    47→        rdir = rel(dirname)
    48→        filename = p.name
    49→
    50→        if filename in all_skip_names:
    51→            continue
    52→        if rdir in all_skip_dirs:

1→"""Shared regex patterns and pattern-based helpers for review context."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import re
     6→
     7→FUNC_NAME_RE = re.compile(r"(?:function|def|async\s+def|async\s+function)\s+(\w+)")
     8→CLASS_NAME_RE = re.compile(r"(?:class|interface|type)\s+(\w+)")
     9→
    10→ERROR_PATTERNS = {
    11→    "try_catch": re.compile(r"\b(?:try\s*\{|try\s*:)"),
    12→    "returns_null": re.compile(r"\breturn\s+(?:null|None|undefined)\b"),
    13→    "result_type": re.compile(r"\b(?:Result|Either|Ok|Err)\b"),
    14→    "throws": re.compile(r"\b(?:throw\s+new|raise\s+\w)"),
    15→}
    16→
    17→NAME_PREFIX_RE = re.compile(
    18→    r"^(get|set|is|has|can|should|use|create|make|build|parse|format|"
    19→    r"validate|check|find|fetch|load|save|update|delete|remove|add|"
    20→    r"handle|on|init|setup|render|compute|calculate|transform|convert|"
    21→    r"to|from|with|ensure|assert|process|run|do|manage|execute)"
    22→)
    23→
    24→FROM_IMPORT_RE = re.compile(
    25→    r"^(?:from\s+\S+\s+import\s+(.+)|import\s+(.+))$", re.MULTILINE
    26→)
    27→
    28→
    29→def extract_imported_names(content: str) -> set[str]:
    30→    """Extract imported symbol names from a file's import statements."""
    31→    names: set[str] = set()
    32→    for match in FROM_IMPORT_RE.finditer(content):
    33→        raw = match.group(1) or match.group(2)
    34→        if raw is None:
    35→            continue
    36→        for part in raw.split(","):
    37→            part = part.strip()
    38→            if not part:
    39→                continue
    40→            token = part.split()[0]
    41→            if token.startswith("(") or token == "\\":
    42→                continue
    43→            token = token.strip("()")
    44→            if token.isidentifier():
    45→                names.add(token)
    46→    return names
    47→
    48→
    49→def default_review_module_patterns(content: str) -> list[str]:
    50→    """Fallback module-pattern extraction used when language hook is absent."""
    51→    out: list[str] = []
    52→    if re.search(r"\bexport\s+default\b", content):
    53→        out.append("default_export")
    54→    if re.search(r"\bexport\s+(?:function|const|class)\b", content):
    55→        out.append("named_export")
    56→    if re.search(r"\bdef\s+\w+", content):
    57→        out.append("functions")
    58→    if re.search(r"^__all__\s*=", content, re.MULTILINE):
    59→        out.append("explicit_api")
    60→    return out
    61→
    62→__all__ = [
    63→    "CLASS_NAME_RE",
    64→    "ERROR_PATTERNS",
    65→    "FROM_IMPORT_RE",
    66→    "FUNC_NAME_RE",
    67→    "NAME_PREFIX_RE",
    68→    "default_review_module_patterns",
    69→    "extract_imported_names",
    70→]
    71→

     9→HOLISTIC_WORKFLOW = [
    10→    "Read .desloppify/query.json for context, excerpts, and investigation batches",
    11→    "For each batch: start from listed seed files, then explore likely hotspots/unreviewed neighbors; evaluate the batch's dimensions (batches are independent — parallelize)",
    12→    "Cross-reference findings with the sibling_behavior and convention data",
    13→    "IMPORTANT: findings must be defects only — never positive observations. High scores capture quality; findings capture problems.",
    14→    "Write ALL findings to findings.json — do NOT fix code before importing. Import creates tracked state entries that let desloppify correlate fixes to findings.",
    15→    "Preferred local Codex path: desloppify review --run-batches --runner codex --parallel --scan-after-import",
    16→    "Claude cloud durable path: run `desloppify review --external-start --external-runner claude`, follow the session template/instructions, then run the printed `--external-submit` command",
    17→    "Fallback path: `desloppify review --import findings.json` (findings only). Use manual override only for emergency/provisional imports.",
    18→    "AFTER importing: run `desloppify show review --status open` to see the work queue, then fix each finding in code and `desloppify resolve fixed <id>`",
    19→]

    22→def append_full_sweep_batch(
    23→    *,
    24→    batches: list[dict[str, Any]],
    25→    dims: list[str],
    26→    all_files: list[str],
    27→    lang: Any,
    28→    max_files: int | None = None,
    29→) -> None:
    30→    """Append an optional cross-cutting full-codebase batch."""
    31→    if not dims:
    32→        return
    33→    all_rel_files: list[str] = []
    34→    for filepath in all_files:
    35→        if lang.zone_map is not None:
    36→            zone = lang.zone_map.get(filepath)
    37→            if zone.value in ("test", "generated", "vendor"):
    38→                continue
    39→        all_rel_files.append(rel(filepath))
    40→        if isinstance(max_files, int) and max_files > 0 and len(all_rel_files) >= max_files:
    41→            break
    42→    if not all_rel_files:
    43→        return
    44→    batches.append(
    45→        {
    46→            "name": "Full Codebase Sweep",
    47→            "dimensions": list(dims),
    48→            "files_to_read": all_rel_files,
    49→            "why": "thorough default: evaluate cross-cutting quality across all production files",
    50→        }
    51→    )
